On the day before the Ides.

### Day 13

On the Ides the devoted people of Poitiers  
Serve Hilary, whose honour as their shepherd made him shine.

### Day 14

Felix the holy confessor adorns the day  
Which is established as the nineteenth before the Kalends of February.

### Day 15

Habakkuk and Micah together honour the eighteenth day.

### Day 16

The seventeenth day after the Ides shines  
With the merits and name of Marcellus the martyr  
And of the supreme pontiff.

### Day 17

The sixteenth day is called by the virtue of Antony;  
It also possesses the honour of his companion, Geminus,  
Whom the people of Langres celebrate, enclosed in one marble tomb.

(Then the sun also enters the star of the cloud-bearing Water-Bearer.)

### Day 18

The fifteenth day rejoices in Prisca as a martyr.  
And in Saint Volusianus the confessor.

### Day 19

The fourteenth day shines with Nicetas and Hautmarus.  
And with Mary and Martha.

### Day 20

The thirteenth day after the Ides flourishes for Fabian the bishop,  
Whom Sebastian accompanies with equal virtue;  
Happy Soissons frequently celebrates him, carried there from Rome.

[Note: “For Fabian the bishop.” We preferred to print this with the Royal and Bigot manuscripts rather than the earlier reading *praeside* (“as presiding”). Below, from the same manuscripts, we wrote *Bissena est Agne* (“the twelfth is Agnes”), where the earlier edition had *Bissexta est Agnes*.]

### Day 21

The twelfth day is Agnes, whom the virgin and martyr honours.

And Saint Fructuosus the bishop.

### Day 22

The mighty Levite Vincent adorns the eleventh day.

The virtue of the excellent Anastasius is joined to him.

### Day 23

After Emerentiana, great praise shines on the tenth day.

### Day 24

On the ninth day the virtue and martyrdom of Babylas shine.

And of Timothy, disciple of the Apostle Paul.

### Day 25

On the eighth day glory honours Paul, converted from Saul;  
And Auvergne, celebrating its Projectus, adorns the day.

[Note: “On the eighth day, from Saul.” This is the excellent reading of both manuscripts; the earlier edition was misled by *ex saeclo* (“from the age”). Immediately afterward the same manuscripts have *Projectum*, where the earlier edition had *Praejectum*; in the Royal manuscript there is also *Arvernis*.]

### Day 26

The seventh day soon shines with the blood of Polycarp,  
Whom Smyrna truly celebrates as burned for the King.

### Day 27

The Punic land venerates its Avitus on the sixth day;  
Sulpicius, Batildis, and Aldegundis also flourish.

Of Caelestine and Victoria.

[Note: “Venerates Avitus.” The reading *veneratur Adjutum*, written in the Royal manuscript, is not without value, since the author himself warned that he had not everywhere observed the rules of metre. I do not see why the remaining, less significant matters should be copied here.]

### Day 28

On the fifth day the Roman offspring, holy Agnes, declares:

[Light, glory of the world, love of the fatherland, grief and pain,  
Exalted with the lofty honour of imperial power;  
Then Charles, departing, left the sceptres to Louis.]

### Day 29

On the fourth day the martyrdom of Papias and Maurus shines;  
Then, too, at Trier they rejoice in Valerius as bishop.

### Day 30

And the third day proclaims Hippolytus to the city of Antioch.

### Day 31

Your glorious Saturninus, and the trophy of Tircus,  
And Victorius together determine the orbit of January.

Of Gelasius and Ursinus. In Alexandria, of Zotichus, Ammonius, Cyriacus, and Geminus, and the passion of Saint Gallicinus and fifteen other priests. In Africa, of Victor and Polycarp.

## FEBRUARY

Now also let us weave in song the course of February  
And the signs of the feasts which its days likewise bring.

### Day 1

The powerful virgin Brigid, first, consecrates  
The Kalends of February to herself,  
Celebrated by the Scots with wondrous devotion.

In Greece, of Saints Polycarp and Dionysius. In Scotland, of Brigid the virgin, and Saint Sur…

### Day 2

On the fourth day before the Nones, the Lamb, brought into the temple, declares the day.  
As God purifies it, the believing people place the living temple  
There with a devout mind and spread out the accepted tribunal.

### Day 3

On the third day before the Nones, the feast is consecrated to Lupicinus;  
On these days, Celerinus and Celerina shine  
With pious blood, as do the blessed Ignatius and Laurentinus.

### Day 4

Then on the day before the Nones the holy Aquilinus claims the day;  
And the bishop Phileas shines together with Philoromus.

And the birthday of Saints Forosenpron, Geminus, Gelasius, Magnus, Donatus, and Aquilinus; likewise of Donatus and Timothy.

### Day 5

On the Nones, Agatha subdues the peoples of Sicily,  
Her virtue celebrated for the extraordinary beauty of her virginity.

In the East, at the city of Patras, the ordination of Saint Andrew the Apostle to the episcopate.

### Day 6

On the eighth day before the Ides the martyr Dorothy shines.

At Syracuse, the passion of Saint Lucy the virgin. At Rome, on the Appian Way, Saint Soteris the virgin. And the burial of Saint Amandus.

### Day 7

On the seventh day, O Augulus, you triumph over the world by conquering it.

(Then also bright spring first breaks forth into its beginnings.)

And of Saints Ammonius, Stationus, and Saturninus.

[Note: “On the seventh day, O Augulus.” In the Royal manuscript, *Angule*. Following the authority of that manuscript, we printed this verse before the verse beginning *Tum quoque*, which occupied the earlier place in the first edition. And lest you think this was done without reason, know that in the same manuscript, after the prose note for the day, it is written: “THE SUN IN PISCES.”]

### Day 8

Dionysius and Aemilianus adorn the sixth day.

And of Saints Paul the bishop and Tyrsus.

### Day 9

On the fifth day pious vows commemorate blessed Ammon.

In Alexandria, of Paul, Dionysius, and Ammonius.

[Note: “On the fifth day, Ammon.” Thus the Royal manuscript; the earlier edition has *Ammonem*. From the same manuscript below we wrote *Barcilon*, where the reading was *Barcinon*. The former reading is better, while the latter was more usual in the author’s age.]

### Day 10

Soter, Irenaeus, and the virgin Scholastica  
Shine together on the fourth day with outstanding praise of their merits.

At the monastery of Nivelles, Saint Gertrude the virgin. And Saint Silvanus the bishop.

### Day 11

On the third day Desiderius crowns  
The walls of Lyons; at Rome, Parthenius and Calocerus shine.

In Africa, of Victor, Januarius, Vitalis, Zotichus, and Cyriacus.

### Day 12

On the day before the Ides, the feast and blood of Eulalia shine,  
The illustrious city of Barcelona rejoicing in its martyr.

In Africa, of Damian, Julian, Victor, Felix, and Secundus. And of Simplicius the bishop.

### Day 13

On the Ides Julian ascends to heavenly honour,  
And the blessed bride [Basilissa] joins her exultant mind to heaven.

In Alexandria, of Tullianus and Ammonius. At Lyons, the burial of Saint Stephen.

### Day 14

Then, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends,  
The martyr Vitalis shines, with Felicula the virgin,  
And they commemorate Valentinus as blessed through his deeds.

Of Felix and Zeno, and of Saints Germanus and Julian.

[Note: “The martyr Vitalis.” In the Royal manuscript, *partis Vit.*; in the Bigot manuscript, *Par his*, a reading which I prefer to the common text. Both manuscripts lack the verses for this day, as well as the verse concerning Faustus of Brescia.]

### Day 15

Hence on the fifteenth day the merit of Agape grows bright.

On this day Brescia venerates Faustinus, celebrated and holy Jovita,  
Slain by cruel punishments.

In Antioch, the birthday of Joseph, Apollonius, Romanus, Zosimus, and Agape the virgin.

(On this day also the sun enters the star of the Twins.)

### Day 16

On the fourteenth day the martyr Juliana shines  
And honours Onesimus, blessed under the teaching of Paul.

In Africa, of Maximus, Vincentius, and Paul. And the burial of Tetradius the bishop.

### Day 17

The thirteenth day brings back the feast of Polychronius  
And Donatus, whom faith, blood, and the altar joined.

And the passion of Saints Secundianus, Justa, Romula, and Silvanus.

### Day 18

Saint Martial honours the twelfth day.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Rutulus, Silvanus, Secundus, Damasus, Paul, Marcellus, and Geminus.

### Day 19

Publius and Julian adorn the eleventh day together.

And the birthday of Saints Marcellus, Tullius, likewise Julian, Lampasius, Maiulus, and Julius.

### Day 20

Soon the tenth day commemorates the praise and fame of Corona.

[Note: “And the fame of Corona.” We corrected this from both the Royal and Bigot manuscripts; the earlier edition corruptly read *famamque coronat* (“and crowns the fame”).]

At Cyprus, the birthday of Potamia; at Rome, on the Appian Way, the burial of Bishop Gagi. And elsewhere, of Victor, Corona, and ten others.

### Day 21

On the ninth day your name, Victorinus, shines.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Secundinus, Servulus, Siricus, and Saturninus. And elsewhere, of Crispinus, Rusticus, Justus, Amator.

### Day 22

On the eighth day the chair and teaching of Peter shine,  
In the joyful city of Antioch, where he first flourished as bishop.

At Nicomedia, the birthday of Saint Thecla the virgin and Saint Concordia.

### Day 23

The seventh day shines with the extraordinary honour of Polycarp,  
The presbyter who, following Christ’s commands with his mouth,  
Was able through martyrdom to preserve the faithful crowd.

In Africa, of Zeno, Arion, Hippolytus, another Zeno, and Elirulus.

### Day 24

On the sixth day Matthias shines with apostolic virtue;  
The leap day is inserted here and in the fourth year.

And here the Baptist uncovers the head long kept hidden.

And the passion of Saints Nicotorus, Claudianus, Dioscorus, and Sarapion.

### Day 25

The fifth day is increased by the praise of blessed Crescentius.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Donatus, Justus, Herenaeus, Aurelius, and Ingenua. In Pamphylia, the birthday of Saints Nestor and Casta.

### Day 26

On the fourth day Nestor rejoices, together with his companion Theon.

And the birthday of Saints Alexander and Abundantius…

[Note: “On the fourth day, Nestor.” The Bigot manuscript has *Mestore*.]

### Day 27

The third day flourishes for Leander the bishop of Spain.

### Day 28

On the day before the Kalends, the holy Rufinus is joined to Macarius.

In Thessalonica, the birthday of Saints Alexander, Abundantius, Severianus, and Januarius. In the city of Smyrna in Asia, of Saints Servilianus…

Here the light of the month of February is brought to an end.

The birthday of Celer, the orphan, Claudianus, Quintus, and Mansuetus.

## MARCH

March, distinguished and released at its proper season,  
We shall briefly relate according to whose honour it stands foremost.

### Day 1

Donatus holds the Kalends of March, and Albinus also.

On the Kalends of March, Saints Donatus and Abundantius, and the burial of Albinus the bishop.

### Day 2

On the sixth day before the Nones, Heraclus and Paul are soon honoured.

In Caesarea of Cappadocia, Luke the bishop and Januarius.

### Day 3

On the fifth day before the Nones, Magra defends the day with pious love;  
On this day also Emeterius, Chelidonius, and Marinus,  
And Asterius, shine, famous for their poured-out blood.

[Note: “Chelidonius.” The Royal manuscript has *Celedonius*, and in the following verse *Austeriusque*.]

And of Saints Felix, Justus, and Fortunatus. In Africa, of Felix and Emeterius.

### Day 4

On the fourth day Pope Lucius shines through a precious death,  
And the excellent company of eight hundred martyrs shines.

At Nicomedia, the passion of Saint Adrian with thirty-three others.

### Day 5

On the third day the martyr Phocas possesses the honour of his merits,  
Who conquered death by blood and the dragon by his virtue.

At Antioch, the passion of Saint Soca. In Africa, of Peter, Eusebius, Justus, Siria, Saturninus, and Marcus.

### Day 6

On the day before the Ides Victorinus rejoices, and Victor,  
Together with those shut in prison,  
Who soared to the stars in lofty flight.

At Nicomedia, of Victor, Claudianus, Perpetua, Felicity, Jocundus, and Revocatus.

### Day 7

On the Nones Felicity and Perpetua shine,  
Who dedicated chaste lives to Christ through a blessed death.

In the city of Mauritania, the passion of Saints Perpetua and Felicity.

### Day 8

On the eighth day before the Ides, the martyr Cyril  
And, together with him, Rogatus, worthy of equal honour,  
Are revered.

At Nicomedia, Quintilus the bishop.

### Day 9

On the seventh day before the Ides, among forty soldiers,  
The sacred festivals of Armenia the Minor  
Commemorate one feast.

In Armenia Minor, of Sebastian and forty thousand whose deeds are recorded. In Africa, of Philip and Rogatus.

### Day 10

On the sixth day, Gaius and Alexander are honoured;  
With them is joined a company of forty-two,  
Whom we likewise celebrate as slain by a cruel governor.

[Note: “Whom we celebrate as slain by a cruel governor.” Thus it is read in the Royal and Bigot manuscripts. The earlier edition has, incorrectly and contrary to the historical account, *saeva celebramus Perside* (“we celebrate them in savage Persia”).]

In Alexandria, of Heraclas, Zosimus, Alexander, and Agape the virgin.

### Day 11

On the fifth day Candidus and Valerius retain the day for themselves.

At Carthage, of Candidus, Valerius, Quirillus, and Marcianus. At Nicomedia, of Eunuchus and Gorgonius.

### Day 12

Soon, on the fourth day before the Ides, your end, blessed Gregory,

[Col. 0592A] **Day**

Consecrates the day on which through eternal praise you sought heaven.

At Rome, the burial of Saint Innocent the bishop.

And the birthday of Saint Felix.

### Day 13

The presbyter Macedonius completes the third day,  
With his honourable wife Patricia  
And his daughter Modesta accompanying him.

At Thessalonica, of Domicianus, Luke, Severinus, Silvanus, Concessus, and Marcialis.

### Day 14

On the day before the Ides, Euphrosius shines together with Peter the martyr.

In Africa, of Alexander, Mammerus, Fronto, and Nabor, martyrs.

### Day 15

The people of Thessaly preserve the Ides  
With Matrona the martyr.

In Cappadocia, Saint Longinus. In Jerusalem, the birthday of Saint James the Apostle, brother of the Lord. And of Luke the Evangelist.

### Day 16

The seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, coming according to custom,  
Shines with the honour of Cyriacus and Largus,  
And likewise flourishes with the precious blood of Smaragdus.

In Nicomedia, of Castor, Dionysius, Serenus, Cyriaca, Eugenia, and Julian.

### Day 17

The eighteenth day shines with your name, Patrick,  
Who, taking pity on the gentile worship  
Throughout the towns of the Scots.

These vows are also rendered to blessed Gertrude.

Of Alexander the bishop, and Saint Patrick.

### Day 18

Bishop Alexander possesses the fifteenth day;  
The presbyter Pigmenius purifies Rome with his lofty blood.

Here the ram opens the flourishing lights of the sun.

Here God, the high Creator of things, made the light  
And, in forming the world, brought forth this first day.

In Campania, of Quintus, Rogatus, Lucianus, Saturninus, Victor, and Maurus.

### Day 19

The fourteenth day shines with John, inhabitant of the desert.

In Caesarea, of Theodore the presbyter. In Africa, of Ammonius, and the burial of Saint Leontius the bishop and confessor.

### Day 20

On the thirteenth day Cuthbert, shining in praise,  
Leads peoples through the mystical joys of angels.

In Antioch, of Saint Joseph. In Syria, of Paul, Claudius, Exsuperius, Victuricus, and Valentinus.

### Day 21

Then the twelfth day shines with the faith and name of Benedict,  
The monastic glory under whose leadership the world rejoices.

[Col. 0593A] **Day 21**

(This makes night and day equal in their spans;  
It also saw, with the new sun, the moon and stars shine  
At their rising beneath the light on the fourth day of creation.)

In Alexandria, of Serapion the monk, Luke, and Amator.

## Day 22

Paul, bishop, bestows pious lights upon the eleventh [day],

By whose right Narbonne rejoices in its own master.

*(This first celebrates Easter with completed light.)*  
[Note: “This first.” This verse, which was absent from printed editions, was supplied by the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts; in the former, “SEDES EPACTARUM” is added.]

In Africa, Saturninus and nine others.

## Day 23

Felix here completes the tenth, and Theodorus together with Julian,

Adorning it, worthy of outstanding praise for their virtues.

In Provence, Paul and Julian. In Antioch, Theodorus the presbyter.

## Day 24

Romulus fills the ninth, and likewise Secundulus.

Here the concurrent [days] are found. In Africa, Agapitus and Rogatus. In Mauretania, Felix and Saturninus.

An angel announces the Lamb who is to come on the eighth.

## Day 25

The Lamb himself is raised upon the cross for the world’s death.

In Jerusalem, our Lord Jesus Christ was crucified. And the passion of Saint James the Apostle. And the Annunciation of Saint Mary.

*(Here almighty God fashions Adam from the dust,

And Adam assigns fitting names to all living creatures.)*  
[Note: “Here almighty God.” Baluzius found these two verses, absent from the earlier edition, in the Regius manuscript; the second read as follows:

“The father Adam gives names to all who love”; nor did we emend it in this way, as you see.]

And Isaac was sacrificed.

## Day 26

The seventh commemorates Montanus together with his holy wife,

And likewise the one who suffered with the forty martyrs.

In Antioch, Timothy, Diogenes and Maximus, and Theodorus the bishop. In Africa, Victor and Saturninus. In the city of Sebaste, the birthday of Saint Peter, bishop and confessor.

## Day 27

The sixth shines with the triumph of the rising Lamb.

The Resurrection of Our Lord Jesus Christ. And in Africa, Maurilius, Successa, Matutina and Donatus. And in Caesarea, the birthday of Mary.

## Day 28

On the fifth, Priscus, Alexander and Malchus are honored [Note: “Malchus are honored.” In the printed editions, “are placed”; in both manuscripts, Regius and Bigotian, as we have published it. In those same manuscripts, “Eustasius” is written where “Eustathius” is read.]:

## Day 28

The excellent King Guntramnus, departing this life, also adorns it.

In Caesarea, Rogatus, Dorotheus, Audacta and Alexander. In Tarsus of Cilicia, Castor. And the burial of the blessed monk Idilo.

## Day 29

Eustathius shines on the fourth with the praise of virtue,

He who rightly excelled under Abba Columbanus as his master.

In Nicomedia, Pastoralis, Victurinus, Saturninus, Juliana and three others. In Antioch, Theodorus the presbyter.

## Day 30

The third shines with Domninus [Note: “The third, with Domninus.” In the Regius manuscript, “Dominicus.] as companion and with Victor.

In the city of Thessalonica, Domnus and Palatinus; elsewhere, Victor, Marcellinus and Eulalia the virgin. At Orléans, the burial of Pastor.

## Day 31

Diodolus and blessed Anesus shine on the day before.

Thus the orbit of Mars, revolving, brings the month to its end.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Cornelius and Valerian.

# APRIL

Let us sing of April, whom spring consecrates to itself with purple flowers,

And of the festivals by which it raises its own joys.

## Day 1

The virginal crown of the illustrious Agape and Chionia [Note: “And Chionia.” So in the Regius manuscript; in the printed editions, “Schionia.”]

Rightly consecrates the Kalends of April as their companion.

In Lesser Armenia, the birthday of Saints Quintianus, Victor and Secundus.

## Day 2

On the fourth day before the Nones, Nicetus is sacred in the city of Lyon.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Quirianus and Regina. At Lyon in Gaul, Nicetus the bishop.

## Day 3

Evagrius shines on the third, and the martyr Benignus,

And the virgin Theodosia shines equally with radiant brilliance.

[Note: “And shines equally.” Baluzius found this verse, absent from the Bigotian manuscript, copied in the Regius manuscript under 2 April, after the verse beginning “Lugduni, etc.”]

In Sicily, the birthday of Saint Pancras. In Caesarea of Palestine, the birthday of Saint Theodosia the virgin, and the passion of Saint Evagrius and Benigna.

## Day 4

Ambrose penetrated heavenly honor on the day before.

The final setting of the Paschal moon. At Milan, the burial of Saint Ambrose, bishop. In Africa, the birthday of Saints Urbanus, Saturninus and Successus.

## Day 5

On the Nones, the pious virgin Herene shines forth from death.

In Nicomedia, the birthday of Saint Claudianus. In Egypt, the birthday of Saints Mary and Nicanor.

## Day 6

On the eighth day before the Ides, Sixtus, sacred martyr,

Takes precedence, having suffered death under the emperor Hadrian.

In Macedonia, Timothy and Diogenes. In Africa, Donatus and Epiphanius.

## Day 7

Diogenes and Eleusius are commemorated on the seventh.

In Antioch of Syria, the birthday of Saints Macharia and Maxima. In Alexandria, the birthday of Saint Pelusius the presbyter.

## Day 8

Maximus holds the sixth before the Ides, and the Liberator.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Timor and Conexus. And elsewhere, Concessus, Ammonius and Successus.

## Day 9

On the fifth before the Ides, the seventh lamp shines on high,

A virginal flower and beauty, radiating together in heaven.

In Sirmium, five virgins whose names God knows. And elsewhere, Demetrius.

## Day 10

The prophet Ezekiel consecrates the fourth with holy voice.

In Alexandria, Donatus, Concessus and Saturninus.

## Day 11

With Leo, the supreme bishop, radiating on the third,

They shine—the one who fed Christ’s flock with mouth and hand.

The birthday of Saint Leo the Pope. In Mauretania, the birthday of Maximus and Hilary. In Nicomedia, the birthday of Eustorgius the presbyter.

## Day 12

On the day before, Julius the bishop revisits the Roman

Walls, a shepherd renowned for the Catholic faith.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Cyprian and Donatus. In the city of Pavingo, Constantine the bishop.

## Day 13

On the Ides, O gracious king Ermenegild, you perceive your raging father,

And, proclaiming the truth, win a true triumph over death.

In Chalcedon, Saint Euphemia the virgin. At Pergamum in Asia, Polycarp the bishop.

## Day 14

When the eighth and tenth days before the Kalends of May have passed,

Valerian triumphs, and his brother Tiburtius [Note: “And his brother Tiburtius.” So in the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts. The earlier edition had “Tiburrus.”] himself,

The soldier Maximus accompanies them, pouring out his blood.

## Day 15

The seventh, joined to the tenth, displays the blessed Olympias,

And at the same time another Maximus defends her.

In Mesopotamia, Archelaus, Cyprian, Diogenes the deacon, with two brothers.

## Day 16

On the sixth and tenth, Charisius [Note: “The tenth, Charisius.” In the Regius manuscript, “Carisi”; and below, “Mappalicus.” Likewise, where “also a holy martyr” is read, Acherius notes that in one manuscript he found “mother.”] and Callistus shine.

The sea blessed them, submerged with the people on the seventh.

In Achaia, at Corinth, Crytianus. In Mauretania, Basilia, Faustinus and Lucianus.

## Day 17

Mappalicus, Hermogenes and Peter shine on the fifteenth,

Renowned in merit, virtue and blood.

In Antioch, the birthday of Saints Peter the deacon and Hermogenes.

## Day 18

On the fourteenth, Eleutherius and the holy martyr

Anthia excel, having pursued life by dying.

## Day 19

The thirteenth shines with Gaius, Aristonichus, Rufus, Hermogenes, Galata, Expeditus, and the martyr.

At the monastery of Lobbes, the burial of Saint Ursmarus, bishop and confessor.

## Day 20

Marcellinus, Domninus and Vincentius alike

Shine in name, in solemn festival and in faith,

And the festivals of the blessed martyr Synesius [Note: “And the festivals of Synesius.” This verse is absent from the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts; in them the following verse begins: “The bishops in title.”]

Are celebrated at the tomb of the blessed bishop, in teaching and in death.

At Rome, Victor the bishop. In the city of Auxerre, the burial of Saint Martin, bishop and confessor.

## Day 21

On the eleventh, Gaius and likewise Simeon are honored.

At Terracina in Campania, the passion of Saint Caesarius the deacon. And elsewhere, the burial of Aprunculus the bishop.

## Day 22

Three presbyters crown the tenth, together with the threefold palm: Parmenius [Note: “Palma and Parmenius.” This verse and the following, although absent from the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts, seemed nevertheless worth preserving.], Elimenes and Chrysotelus.

Here too, revealed by divine command,

The bodies appeared, cleansing the Church by a threefold martyrdom,

Those of blessed Dionysius, Rusticus and Eleutherius.

In Africa, in the city of Gerapolis, the birthday of Saint Philip the Apostle. In the city of Sens, the burial of blessed Leo, bishop and confessor; and of Ananias, Azarias and Misael.

## Day 23

The ninth teaches Felix, sacred and worthy of a twofold ministry,

And Fortunatus and Achilleus, joined together.

Here too, holy George, who with unconquered blood scorns the world,

Recounts infinite trophies.

In the city of Valencia, the birthday of Saint Felix the presbyter and Achilleus the deacon.

## Day 24

The martyr Alexander, joyful with a martyr on the thirtieth

And with a third, consecrates the walls of Lyon on the eighth.

In Alexandria, the birthday of Saints Corona the virgin, Victor, Zotica and Faustinus.

## Day 25

Soon the blessed Mark thunders with evangelical voice,

The seventh receives outstanding radiance, decked by death.

*(The final day celebrates the joys of Easter as a festival.)*

On the Greater Litany. And at the monastery of Lobbes, Saint Erminonius the bishop.

## Day 26

The sixth recalls the struggles of Pope Cletus,

And shines with Ricarius, the patron of the conquered blessed one.

In Africa, Honoratus, Paul and Felix.

## Day 27

On the fifth we celebrate Pope Anastasius; with him

The bishop Antimus is joined in worthy virtue.

In the city of Tarsus of Cilicia, the birthday of Saint Castor. In Nicomedia, Stephen the bishop and Antonius the presbyter.

## Day 28

The fourth commemorates Vitalis, slain for the name of Christ,

Who by death earned everlasting life.

In Pannonia, Eusebius the bishop. At Bourges, Saint Eutychus and Saint Vitalis.

## Day 29

On the third, the altar venerates the bishops

Agapius and likewise Secundinus, dedicated by merits.

And Saint Germanus the bishop. In Nicomedia, Prudentius, Martialis and Theodora the virgin.

## Day 30

The day before, James and Marianus obtain a similar honor

Having obtained a like honor of martyrdom, they bring April to its end.

At Rome, the burial of Quirinus the bishop, Clement, Lucianus and Saturninus.

# MAY

From here, let us recall May, the first month beneath the warming summer sun,

Which brings vows lasting through long days.

## Day 1

The teaching of Christ consecrates the first Kalends of May,

And on it his brother James, the Lord’s, shines, together with Philip;

Jeremiah too, an excellent prophet, is celebrated;

And King Sigismund reigns, having shed his blood.

And Androclus is honored as a martyr on the same day [Note: “Androclus on the same day.” This verse and the following, absent from the printed editions and also lacking in the Regius manuscript, were entered from the Bigotian manuscript.],

Whom Alpia raises up as great among the peoples of Gaul.

## Day 2

On the sixth before the Nones, great Athanasius, you shine,

By whose victory the Arian serpent first perished.

In the city of Armenia, the birthday of Hermogenes and Germanus. The dedication of Saint Peter.

## Day 3

Bishop Alexander and Eventius adorn the fifth,

And Theodolus, likewise slain for the name of God:

With them the lofty standards of the discovered cross shine [Note: “The standards of the discovered [cross].” So in the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts, and considerably better than the reading adopted in the earlier edition, “of the cross discovered.”]

And Saint Juvenal, Alexander, Eventius and Theodolus.

## Day 4

On the fourth, Sylvanus, Antonia and Florianus

Are girded with the adornment of meritorious virtue.

In Africa, the birthday of Felix and Urbanus. And in Caesarea, the birthday of Saint Silvanus.

## Day 5

On the third, Christ crosses the starry Olympus:

At Arles, Hilary prevails; at Vienne, Nicetus.

## Day 6

On the day before, the Roman temples celebrate the exalted John,

Who drew the word from his full heart.

## Day 7

By a pious death, holy Juvenal honors the Nones.

At Autun, the burial of blessed Placidus the presbyter.

## Day 8

On the eighth before the Ides, in the city of Milan, shines

The martyr Victor, to be revered with exceptional love.

And the birthday of Stephen and Eutychus.

## Day 9

Three hundred shine together on the seventh before the Ides,

At last adorned by blessed martyrdom [Note: “At last by martyrdom.” This verse is absent from the Regius manuscript and is hardly necessary.]

*(Then torrid summer rises with new crops.)*

At Rome, on the Latin Way, the birthday of Saint Beatus the confessor.

## Day 10

On the sixth, Gordianus and Epimachus are slain together

For one praise and faith of Christ:

Holy Job also honors these by the example of endurance.

## Day 11

On the fifth, Bishop Mamertus, with exceptional splendor,

Marks the solemn sacrifice offered to God,

Which he instituted as a fast for three days in the light of day.

And the bishop Martin.

## Day 12

Domitilla, virgin, we honor your companions on the fourth:

Nereus, Pancratius and the holy Achilleus,

Whom Primus taught and baptized with the apostolic washing,

Those whom Peter joined to the distinguished virgin at Rome.

## Day 13

On the Ides, we venerate gracious Servatius.

And the dedication of the church of blessed Mary. And at Maastricht, the burial of Saint Servatius the bishop.

## Day 14

On the day before, Pachomius, Victor and the crown

Shine—he, the powerful hermit, and they, having followed God

With joined virtue in blood and martyrdom.

In Asia, Saint Maximus. At Milan, Victor, Felix and Rusticus.

## Day 15

Seven bishops together adorn Hesperia on the Ides.

In Sirmium, the birthday of Timothy. At Autun, the birthday of Saint Projectus the bishop.

## Day 16

The seventh and tenth shine under the name of Timothy,

Whom blessed Paul taught with truthful voice.

In Heraclea, the birthday of Saints Aquilinus, Heraclius and Paulinus.

## Day 17

On the sixteenth, the martyr Peregrinus blossoms.

At Rome, Parthemis and Liberus the bishop. In Alexandria, Serapion.

## Day 18

The martyr Dioscorus completes the fifteenth.

*(Here Gemini join their stars to the summer sun.)*

## Day 19

On the seventeenth, Pudentiana shines as a virgin.

In Alexandria, the birthday of Saint Areneus the deacon. In Caesarea of Cappadocia, the birthday of Saint Paul.

## Day 20

With the tenth, Basilla holds and supports the earth,

And likewise Baudelius, clad in blood, blossoms.

And the burial of Faustus the bishop.

## Day 21

On the twelfth, Polius, Eutychius [Note: “Eutychius.” In the Regius manuscript, “Eutyhicus.” In both it and the Bigotian manuscript, the two verses that follow are absent.] and Timothy:

And the bishop and martyr Valens, venerable to God,

Augia leads you through joyful vows.

## Day 22

On the eleventh, sacred Castus and Aemilius consecrate it.

And the translation of the body of Saint Helena the virgin.

## Day 23

On the tenth, Desiderius consecrates the city of Langres,

A bishop and martyr armed by love of God.

## Day 24

On the ninth, Donatianus, together with Rogatianus of Nantes,

His brother, adorns it with the pious struggle of faith.

In the Roman harbor, the birthday of Saint Vincent. In the Gallic city of Nantes, the birthday of Saints Donatianus and Rogatianus.

## Day 25

On the eighth, Urbanus shines with the crown of merits,

Whom both the bishop’s mitre, teaching and blood made blessed.

At Milan, the burial of Dionysius the bishop.

## Day 25

Augustine, the seventh commends your name,

## Day 26

By whose leadership countless thousands of the English retain the milk of the word,

Under whom the subdued Britons came to know Christ.

## Day 27

From here Julius, soldier and martyr, beautifies the sixth.

In Alexandria, the birthday of Saints Aquilinus the presbyter and Evangelus.

## Day 28

On the fifth, the crowd at Paris gathers for Germanus;

Then Rome likewise celebrates its bishop John.

## Day 29

On the fourth, lofty Trier shines for you, Maximinus.

And the burial of Saint Maximinus the bishop.

## Day 30

The third is dedicated to Hubertus, the pope, and Felix.

In Antioch, the birthday of Saints Sicius and Palatinus, who suffered many torments.

## Day 31

On the day before, the holy virgin Petronilla, sprung from Peter’s stock,

Shines brightly, adorned with Christ’s military cloak [Note: “And adorned with Christ’s cloak.” So in the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts; the earlier edition had “adorned with Christ’s cloak of honor,” evidently referring to Petronilla.]:

Cantius and Cantianus, together with Cantianilla,

Shine with her. These solemn rites close the month of May.

At Rome, on the Aurelian Way, the birthday of Saints Processus and Martinianus.

# JUNE

June, burning beneath the heat of rain-banishing summer,

[Note: “June, rain-banishing.” In the Regius manuscript, “shade-banishing,” not inaptly. In it and in the Bigotian manuscript the verse beginning “And the martyr …” is absent.]

Let us sing of the festivals whose foliage covers the temples.

## Day 1

The beginning of June raises your radiance to the stars, Pamphilus,

A teacher venerable for blessed martyrdom.

The martyr Nicomedus also adorns this day with a festival.

On the Kalends of June, the dedication of Saint Nicomedus and Saint Claudius.

Here too the holy Jovinus ascends to the stars [Note: “Here too.” This verse, absent from the earlier edition, was entered from the Bigotian manuscript.]

## Day 2

Sacred Marcellinus, Peter and the exorcist, on the fourth

Before the Nones, offer a common and worthy sacrifice at the altar:

And at Lyon, Blandina is called with pious honor,

And, radiant with forty-eight others, she bore the shining crown with the people

Through flames and waters [Note: “Together with the people she carried away.” In the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts, “together with the people she joined.”]

## Day 3

Likewise Pergentius and Laurentius adorn the third

With the double brilliance of blood and lineage.

At Orléans, the people commemorate their Lifardus.

In Africa, Quirinus, Gaius and Donatus; at Rome, Marca and Saturninus.

## Day 4

On the day before, the martyr and bishop Quirinus,

Accumulating sacred vows, appeases Christ with his own blood.

At Rome, the birthday of Saints Expergentus and Philip.

## Day 5

On the Nones, the bishop Boniface shines, born among the English,

Who brought the children of the Ocean to Christ,

Submitting the necks of the Frisians to the pure washing.

In Egypt, Marcianus.

## Day 6

On the eighth before the Ides, Bishop Ceratus adorns it,

He who supports the city named under the emperor Gratian.

In the city of Nevers, Amantius and Lucius. And the burial of blessed Claudius the bishop.

## Day 7

On the seventh, your bishop Paul, lofty Byzantium.

## Day 8

Those whom lineage, pious merit and the altar joined,

Gildardus and likewise Medardus honor on the sixth.

In Caesarea of Cappadocia, Lucianus the martyr.

## Day 9

Primus holds the fifth, with Felicianus joined to him.

The passion of Saint Vincent the martyr.

## Day 10

On the fourth, Basilides and twenty martyrs blossom.

In Nicomedia, the birthday of Saint Zacharias. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Censurius the bishop.

## Day 11

The apostle Barnabas adorns the third before the Ides.

At Rome, the birthday of Saint Restitutus [lacuna]. And elsewhere, Nabor and Felix.

## Day 12

On the day before, Cyrinus shines, and Nazarius and Nabor:

With these we celebrate Basilides [Note: “With these, Basilides.” In the Regius manuscript, “with these, Basilides” is masculine, as though a woman named Basilides were being mentioned. Below, we have printed “whom he joined” from that manuscript and from the Bigotian, where “he joins” was read.]

On the same festival.

## Day 13

On the Ides, the virgin Felicula illuminates it with blood,

And Petronilla, whom the milk, the word and age joined to you.

In Africa, Lucianus, Fortunatus and Crescentianus.

## Day 14

On the eighteenth day before the beginning of July,

The prophets Elisha and Obadiah shine together:

Here too he rejoices with the martyr Valerius and Rufinus.

At Orléans, the burial of Saint Anianus the bishop. And of Elisha the prophet, and Felicula.

## Day 15

On the seventeenth, Vitus shines with the illustrious virgin

Margaret, radiant with the splendor of martyrdom.

And the gracious virgin Crescentia shines with Modestus [Note: “And Modestus.” This verse appears neither in the Regius nor in the Bigotian manuscript.].

In Sicily, the birthday of Saints Modestus and Crescentia.

## Day 16

On the sixteenth, Cyricus shines with his mother Julitta,

In the true piety and faith of Christ.

And four hundred other holy martyrs.

## Day 17

On the fifteenth, with seven, fifty and two hundred,

He sends a joyful crown of martyrdom to the stars.

*(Through this, Phoebus also penetrates the stars of burning Cancer.)*

Of Avitus the presbyter.

## Day 18

On the fourteenth, the brothers Marcellianus and Marcus

Consecrated themselves with precious blood:

Here too Balbina purifies their merit and honor.

## Day 19

On the thirtieth, Gervasius and Protasius crown it.

## Day 20

On the twelfth, Vitalis follows his children, the father.

*(At the center here the solstice flashes at the middle and highest point.

Then, Caesar Louis, having completed your bloody age,

You leave behind scepters destined to pass into many parts.)*

## Day 21

On the eleventh, the martyr Rufinus and Marcia are honored.

## Day 22

On the tenth, Albanus defends the Britons with praise:

And Paulinus cleanses Nola by merit and by name.

And eight hundred seventy-nine martyrs.

## Day 23

On the ninth, Ediltrudis shines, sprung from the English.

## Day 24

On the eighth, the Baptist John is honored as having been born.

## Day 25

On the seventh, Luceia adorns Rome with love [Note: “Rome, Luceia.” We have printed this verse and the next two as they are written in the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts. In the earlier edition: “Lucena … Scampio twice ten … concerning whom Accias.”]

The holy woman rejoices in the pious twenty-two martyrs:

Among whom King Aceias shines with associated honor.

And the birthday of Saint Amandus the confessor.

## Day 26

On the sixth, the martyr Paul and likewise John possess it,

Brothers in origin, love, faith, virtue and blood:

With them Constantia shines in a noble crown.

In the city of Thessalonica, Lucia the virgin and Avieta the queen. And Saint Salvius the martyr.

## Day 27

On the fifth, the bishop and martyr Zoelus adorns Hesperia,

Joined to nineteen martyrs.

In Spain, Crescentius, Julianus, Clement and Marcellinus.

## Day 28

On the fourth, he triumphs with the bishop and teacher of the word, Leo.

And the vigil of the Apostles Peter and Paul.

## Day 29

On the third, he raises golden Rome to heaven

Through the blessed martyrdom of Peter and Paul alike.

## Day 30

On the day before, the Limoges people honor Martial [Note: “On the day before, Martial.” In the Regius manuscript this verse reads:

“On the day before, the apostle Martial adorns Limoges.”]

June brings the lofty cycle to its end with these festivals.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Timothy and Zoticas.

# JULY

From here, let us recall July, crowned on its shoulders with golden ears of grain,

Let us recall those whom it reverently honors at the altars.

## Day 1

Aaron, who was first priest of the ancient people and law,

Who first offered incense and first sacrificed at the altar,

Begins July and consecrates its Kalends.

The contemptor of the world, Carilefus, also honors them:

And Saint Salvius visits the shores of the Scheldt.

In the city of Angoulême, the burial of blessed Eparchius the confessor, and of Saint Gallus.

## Day 2

Processus holds the sixth with Martinianus

Before the Nones, radiant with the joyful splendor of martyrdom.

And Saint Amatus the confessor. And Saint Monegundis.

## Day 3

On the fifth, the bishops Anatolius and Eulogius.

In the city of Edessa, the translation of the body of Saint Thomas the Apostle, who suffered in India.

## Day 4

Laurianus, by the renown of your merits, you hold the fourth:

And Martin’s bones, transferred to a tomb, adorn it.

## Day 5

Domitius dedicates the third, and the most illustrious Zoe,

Who rightly increased the blessed company through martyrdom.

In Sicily, Agatho. And in the city of Tonis, the birthday of Secundinus. And of the prophet Isaiah, and Tryphon.

## Day 6

Isaiah, the outstanding prophet, shines on the day before,

A martyr through martyrdom, virtue and voice, after his end in the world.

Tranquillinus, you shine with a double brilliance,

Father of saints, escorting the saints who were slain [Note: “Escorting the saints.” We judged this to be the reading, since the reading in the earlier edition, “with the one escorting,” admitted no suitable sense.]

And then Goar, Christ’s servant, is honored, both servant and saint.

And the eighth of the Apostles Peter and Paul.

## Day 7

On the Nones, Pantaenus shines in merit and faith.

In Alexandria, Apollonius. And the octave of Saint Martial the Apostle.

## Day 8

On the eighth before the Ides, Cilianus and Procopius,

Outstanding, follow Christ in virtue and conduct.

In Sicily, Pancratius. In Heraclea, John and Primolus.

## Day 9

Audax and likewise Anatona shine on the seventh:

And no less does the holy despiser of wealth, Ephrem, stand forth.

In the city of Tonis, the birthday of Saints Vitalis and Fraternus the bishop. Of Theodosius the bishop and Generosus.

## Day 10

On the sixth, the blessed Felicitas dedicates to Christ

A crown for her seven brothers, whom she bore,

And sent beforehand as an offering pleasing to God at the altar.

At Rome, Priscilla and the birthday of the seven brothers. And Saint Petrosa.

## Day 11

On the fifth, Januarius consecrates it through martyrdom,

And holy Pelagia adorns it with similar brilliance.

Then the transferred remains of the blessed Father Benedict,

Transported from the Beneventan mountains [Note: “The righteous remains of the Father.” In the Regius manuscript, “the grave of the Father,” which in my judgment is less correct], are now honored by the lofty Loire.

And Saint Arnulf the confessor, Rusticus the presbyter, and Saint Sabinus.

## Day 12

On the fourth, suppliant Aquileia repeatedly honors Hermagoras,

The bishop who supports the people and city by his prayers.

And the birthday of Saints Fortunatus, Armigerus and the holy father Arsenius.

## Day 13

On the third, Serapion is presented to Egypt:

And Atialus, a martyr, grows green with heavenly blossom [Note: “Grows green with blossom.” So the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts; the earlier edition had “shines with blossom.”]

In Alexandria, Serapion, Evangelus and Zeno. The virgin Trophina. And Saint Praxedis the virgin.

## Day 14

On the day before, the bishop and martyr Phocas seeks the heavens.

At Lyon in Gaul, the birthday of Justus the bishop. Of Saint Mary Magdalene. And of Saint Symphorosa with her seven sons.

## Day 15

On the Ides, Cassianus and Cyricius shine:

And James the bishop is celebrated for his abundant merits.

In Sirmium, the birthday of Saints Agrippinus and Secundus.

## Day 16

With the tenth and seventh marking out August,

Hilarinus, martyr, shines on your excellent festival [Note: “Marking out August.” Here we have followed the Regius and Bigotian manuscripts, since the printed editions had “marks out Augusta.”]

In Caesarea, Saint Paul. And Saint Mammes. And the translation of Saint Justinian.

## Day 17

On the sixteenth, Carthage looks toward it with splendid vows,

Joyfully welcoming a people of twelve martyrs,

The Scillitan martyrs whom their homeland sent to the executioner [Note: “The Scillitan martyrs together.” So the Regius manuscript, correctly; the earlier edition had “Sullitan,” corruptly.]

At Milan, the birthday of Saint Marcellus. At Auxerre, the burial of blessed Theodosius the bishop.

## Day 18

On the fifteenth, the mother dedicated herself with seven offspring,

Symphorosa, who with her pious offspring was slain together.

*(Here the blazing sun seeks the signs of the burning lion.)*

## Day 19

On the fourteenth, the hermit Arsenius adorns it.

In Spain, the birthday of Saint Justus. At Lyon in Gaul, the birthday of Saint Rusticus the presbyter.

## Day 20

And on the thirteenth, Saint Philibert adorns it [Note: “And on the thirteenth.” In place of this verse, the following is written in the Regius manuscript:

“Sabinus and Lucianus seek the thirteenth,” which I think is spurious.]

And the birthday of Peter and Amabilis.

## Day 21

On the twelfth, Praxedis the virgin shines, and likewise

The prophet Daniel, in name, in end and in faith.

## Day 22

On the eleventh, blessed Mary, whom Christ showed mercy,

Adorns it; she who was freed from seven demons,

Whom her origin marks by the surname Magdalene.

For you, Vandregisilus, the vows of the monks return here.

And the birthday of Saint Mary Magdalene.

## Day 23

From here, the illustrious Apollinaris honors the tenth.

At Rome, on the Tiburtine Way, the birthday of Saint Vincent. On the Aculan Way, the birthday of Saint Primitivus.

## Day 24

Soon, on the ninth, Christina, Aquila and Nicetas consecrated it.

In the city of Armenia, the birthday of Saint Victor.

## Day 25

On the eighth, James, son of Zebedee, adorns it,

The first who gave apostolic blood for the true King:

Cucufas and Christopher follow him.

## Day 26

On the seventh, Hadrian holds it, and blessed Aemilius;

Marcianus likewise triumphs with similar virtue.

In Laodicea of Phrygia, the birthday of Saints Julian, Felix, Maximus and Saturninus.

## Day 27

The presbyter Hermolaus [Note: “The presbyter Hermolaus.” In both manuscripts, “Hermelaus.”] and the martyr shine on the sixth.

In Syria, the assumption of Saint Simeon the monk. And the burial of Saint Aetherius the bishop.

## Day 28

On the fifth, Nazarius possesses it with Celsus; and Pantaleon

The martyr consecrates it to himself with honor:

The Roman bishop Stephen then consecrates an altar

Distinguished by the blessed merits of Peter and Paul,

Which shines, adorned with the temple of Dionysius,

With signs of martyrdom, admonished by visions and faith.

## Day 29

Felix, Simplicius, Faustinus and gracious Beatrix,

And Lupus of Troyes together gild the fourth.

At Rome, on the Puerine Way, the birthday of Saints Simplicius, Faustinus and Beatrix. And the birthday of Saint Felix.

## Day 30

The third marks Abdon and Sennen as saints,

Persians whom Rome received as being of royal stock.

## Day 31

On the day before, pious glory covered Fabius with martyrdom.

July, departing from the world, leaves these solemn rites behind.

In Africa, the birthday of Saints Secundus and Dionysius. At Auxerre, the burial of Germanus the bishop.

# AUGUST

At last August, already filled with abundant grain,

Let us show in verse the saints who bring new sacred observances.

## Day 1

The Maccabees rightly hold the Kalends of August,

Whom the savage Antiochus drove to death with their mother,

And who willingly dedicated their blood to Christ who was to come.

Rome celebrates Peter, restored from prison and chains:

And Vercelli rightly repeatedly honors its own Eusebius.

In the city of Bourges, blessed Arcadius the bishop.

## Day 2

On the fourth before the Nones, Stephen, martyr and blessed pope,

Gives Rome pious joys for the festival.

## Day 3

Soon, on the third, the solemn festival of the discovery of Stephen is celebrated,

The first who followed Christ’s death by dying:

Gamaliel, Nicodemus and Abibon likewise,

Discovered with him, shine with vow and unending praise.

## Day 4

On the day before, Justinus is celebrated with his own honor,

A presbyter who adorned countless saints slain by massacre

By seeking out their cruelly buried bodies.

The dedication of Saint John the Evangelist.

## Day 5

On the Nones, Cassianus, Memmius and Oswald,

The pious king of the English, hold it by merit and virtue.

In the city of Autun, the passion of Saint Affra. And Saint Cassianus the bishop. And the dedication of Saint Mary.

## Day 6

On the eighth before the Ides, the holy flesh of Christ,

About to suffer death and the cross, gave an image of heaven beforehand:

And Bishop Sixtus, a martyr to be honored at Rome;

Nearby, Felicissimus and Agapitus also triumph.

*[Here too the joyful season of autumn rises.]*

And the birthday of Saint Androsius the martyr.

## Day 7

On the seventh, Donatus and Afra together bore it.

In Tuscia, in the city of Arezzo, the birthday of Saint Donatus the bishop. And the birthday of Saint Faustinus.

## Day 8

On the sixth, Cyriacus penetrates heavenly honor.

And in Nicomedia, the birthday of Saints Julian and Nazarius.

## Day 9

On the fifth, Romanus shines as martyr and soldier.

The fast of Saint Laurence. At Rome, in the cemetery, the burial of Saint Dionysius the bishop. And of Saint Martin of Brive.

## Day 10

On the fourth, Laurence, you shine with splendid merit,

You who, having endured fire, overcome the wicked torturer.

And on the Appian Way, Felicissimus and Januarius.

## Day 11

On the third, you seek the stars, Tiburtius, flower and pious glory;

And gracious Gauricus possesses them.

Rusticus and Firmus cleanse Verona with blood [Note: “Rusticus and Firmus.” This verse was added from the Bigotian manuscript.].

## Day 12

On the day before, Euplus receives the palm of martyrdom forever:

And his fellow martyr Gallus rejoices with Andreolus [Note: “And his fellow martyr Andreolus.” This verse, together with the following, was copied by R. P. Martène from the Bigotian manuscript. Since neither appears in the printed editions nor in the Regius manuscript, and since they are certainly recent, I have little doubt; they plainly do not sound like Wandalbert.];

Smyrna produced him, but the shores of the Rhône preserve him.

At Rome, the birthday of Saints Chrysanthus and Daria.

## Day 13

On the Ides, Laurence receives Hippolytus as his companion in the stars,

Hippolytus having suffered for Christ in an equal struggle.

Then Aquitaine, honoring Queen Radegund,

Frequently venerates her as worthy in merit, virtue and faith.

## Day 14

Since it is the nineteenth day before the Kalends of September,

Rome consecrates and celebrates blessed Eusebius.

In Africa, the birthday of Saint Demetrius.

## Day 15

On the eighth and tenth, Mary, the light and flower of the world,

The virgin, accompanied by an angelic choir, seeks the heavens.

## Day 16

On the seventeenth, you hold it, priest Arnulf.

In Alexandria, the birthday of Saints Orion and Agnatius.

## Day 17

On the sixteenth, Mammes shines as a blessed martyr.

And the octave of Saint Laurence the Martyr.

## Day 18

On the fifteenth, Agapitus consecrates it through struggle.

*(Here the virgin Erigone joins her stars to Phoebus.)*

## Day 19

Magnus and Andreas shine on the fourteenth,

And five hundred ninety-seven accompany them,

All likewise saints; twice a thousand follow them together.

And Saint Magnus the martyr. The apparition of the holy cross. And the birthday of Alpinianus the confessor.

## Day 20

And on the thirteenth, Saint Philibert adorns it [Note: “And on the thirteenth.” This verse, absent from the printed editions, was copied from the Regius manuscript.]

On the third after the tenth, Samuel excels, whom

His devoted mother consecrated to the Lord from the cradle.

In Alexandria, the birthday of Saint Dioscorus. And at the fortress of Toron, Saint Maximus the confessor.

## Day 21

From here, on the twelfth, the martyr Privatus blossoms in blood.

In the province of Lucania, the birthday of Saints Valentinus and Leontius.

## Day 22

On the eleventh, Timothy honors Rome by his suffering:

And the people of Edua celebrate their own Symphorianus,

Whom his mother dedicated to Christ, destined likewise to die.

## Day 23

Lucius and Ptolemaeus adorn the tenth with virtue:

At Rheims, Timothy and Apollinaris are honored.

## Day 24

Blessed Bartholomew adorns and holds the ninth,

By whose teaching India came to know the honor of God,

Scarcely rescued from the insane rites of Hercules and Bacchus;

Now, it is said, according to the varied fate of his tomb,

He occupies Aeolian Lipara and the temples of Benevento.

Then Rome too shines with the martyr Genesius:

And Rouen honors the pious Audoenus.

And Saint Genesius. And Saint Apptatus the presbyter.

## Day 25

From here, on the eighth, holy Genesius, Arles celebrates you.

In Spain, the birthday of Saints Justus and Pastor.

## Day 26

Irenaeus and Abundius adorn the seventh through martyrdom.

At Rome, in the cemetery, the birthday of Saints Basilla and Maximus. Of Quintinus the martyr.

## Day 27

On the sixth, Rufus, remembering your triumphs, displays them.

In Campania, at Capua, the birthday of Saint Rufus. In Gaul, in the city of Arles, the burial of Saint Caesarius the bishop.

## Day 28

On the fifth, Hermen shows him blessed by a happy death.

The light of the Church, a sacred and faithful standard for peoples,

By whom Africa shines under its shepherd and the world under its teacher,

Father Augustine, you are celebrated on the same festival;

The golden temples that now guard him buried in Italy.

At Saintes, this shines with the high honor of its own Vivian.

The city of the Alemanni, Constance, commemorates the holy man,  
who here too is renowned for the blood he shed, Pelagius.

[Note: [Col. 0609D] “City of the Alemanni.” This verse and the following occur neither in the Royal manuscript nor in Bigot.]

And the feast of Saint Augustine, bishop. In Africa, of Faustinus. At Rome, the feast of Saint Hermes the martyr. At Avernus, of Julian the martyr.

The herald of God, the voice of the Word, and John the Baptist,

## Day 29

whom the savage commands of a dancing girl bestowed,  
shines on the fourth day with everlasting praise for his merits.

The virgin Sabina likewise revisits her own temples at Rome.

## Day 30

On the third day Felix and Adauctus shine through their blood.

[Note: [Col. 0609D] “And Adauctus.” Both manuscripts read *Audactus*.]

Paulinus on the preceding day traverses the walls of Trier,  
a bishop renowned for the true doctrine for which he suffered exile.

And the deposition of Saint Eladius, bishop.

With these festivals August finally closes its gates.

## SEPTEMBER

Gentle September, tasting in advance the cups of Bacchus—  
we shall sing of those whom it venerates at the altars and remembers.

## Day 1

The bishops Sixtus, Sinicius, and Nivardus shine at Rheims,  
illustrious in name, merits, and life.

Joshua, the bearer and receiver of the law, whom the Lawgiver left as heir to his own honor—  
he who by his courage, through the stars, through places, high mountains, and cities,  
marked out the land promised to the people—  
holds and begins the September Kalends.

Priscus, clothed in blood, also purifies this day as a martyr.

The bishop Lupus likewise shines in the lofty church of Sens.

These solemnities of the holy Verena also glow.

[Note: [Col. 0609D] “These also, of Verena.” This verse is absent from the Bigot manuscript.]

In Campania, the feast of Saint Priscus the martyr. And elsewhere, the feast of Saints Sisinnius and Victor, bishop.

## Day 2

From here Justus honors the fourth Nones at Lyon.

At Nicomedia, the feast of Saints Zeno, Gurgonius, and Theodora.

## Day 3

On the third day you triumph, young Antoninus, both boy and martyr;  
then also Bishop Aristeus is blessed by death.

## Day 4

Moses, bearer, receiver, and author of the divine law,  
granted frequent converse and vision with God,  
is buried on the lofty mountain on the preceding day;  
after him no one was permitted to know where his tomb was.

Then also Cavaillon grows green with the blood of Marcellus.

[Note: [Col. 0609D] “Then also Cabilon.” The Royal manuscript has *Cabalon*, that is, the city which we call Cavaillon in French.]

And the feast of Arestus, bishop.

## Day 5

On the Nones Ferreolus shines together with Ferrucio;  
Donatus and likewise Arcontius adorn Capua.

At Porto Romano, the feast of Saints Taurinus and Aristus.

## Day 6

The prophet Zacharias occupies the eighth Ides.

At Rome, on the Salarian Way, the feast of Saint Eleutherius, bishop.

## Day 7

The bishop Evortius keeps the seventh day, and Clodoaldus,  
a priest distinguished by royal descent.

And the feast of Saint Regina the martyr, whose acts are preserved.

## Day 8

On the sixth day the birth of Mary, the Virgin through whom God assumed human form, shines with its light.

The martyr Adrianus also accompanies Rome with his blood.

## Day 9

Gorgonius retains the fifth day through his fame and merits,  
him whom Gaul now seeks to honor in reverence, having suffered at Rome.

[Note: [Col. 0610D] “Whom, having suffered at Rome.” Acherius observes that this verse is also transcribed as: “Whom Gaul now seeks, in worship, having suffered at Rome.”]

## Day 10

On the fourth day Sosthenes and Victor are commemorated,  
having received and won the same crown in the kingdom and praise of Christ.

At Rome, the deposition of blessed Hilary, pope, through whom Victorius composed the paschal cycle.

## Day 11

Protus and his brother Hyacinthus honor the third day,  
they who together taught Eugenia the sacred law.

Together with these, Felix too consecrated the day by a happy death,  
and the holy martyr Regula likewise.

[Note: [Col. 0610D] “Together with these,” etc. This verse is absent from the Bigot manuscript; the following one is absent from it and from the Royal manuscript.]

## Day 12

The martyr Syrus soon seeks the lofty heavens on the preceding day.

[Note: [Col. 0610D] “Syrus to the heavens.” The Royal manuscript reads *Sinus*.]

At the city of Lyon, the deposition of blessed Sacerdos, bishop.

## Day 13

On the Ides the abbot Amatus shines in merit and by name.

At the city of Angers, the deposition of Saint Maurilius, bishop. In Alexandria, the feast of Saint Theodore, bishop.

## Day 14

With the eighteenth day naming the October to come,  
the standards of the exalted cross shine, restored  
by Heraclius, who victoriously carried it away from Persia.

Cornelius, the bishop, strengthens his Rome  
by courage and blood; Carthage rejoices  
in Cyprian, its distinguished teacher and martyr,  
whose sacred writings the churches record throughout the world.

Here too the merit of Bishop Eparchius is celebrated.

## Day 15

On the seventeenth day Nicomedes the presbyter adorns the calendar;  
Petronilla, your virgin companion, and blessed martyr.

The bishops worthy of veneration for altar, merits, and life—  
Leobinus of Chartres, Aper, and Leucus—protect these days.

And the deposition of Albinus, bishop, and of Saint Nicomedes.

## Day 16

From here Martin, the pope, is blessed on the sixteenth day.

And we venerate the holy Euphemia with devout love.

On this day Lucius likewise excels together with Geminianus;  
the laurel of Christ jointly adorns those who suffered.

And the feast of Saints Lucia and Geminianus.

## Day 17

Lambert crowns the fifteenth day with his courage;  
the ever-trembling faction fears him, slain though he was.

And of Saint Paulinus, bishop.

## Day 18

Methodius, a bishop in speech and faith, and a martyr in signs and blood,  
honors the fourteenth day, which must be celebrated.

Soon the balancing scales join together, making the day equal to the customary one.

In Alexandria, the feast of Saint Trophimus.

## Day 19

Eustachius triumphs on the nineteenth day,  
a model of courage in suffering and a glory and ornament of martyrdom.

In Gaul, at the city of Vienne, the feast of Saint Ferreolus the martyr.

## Day 20

The virgin Fausta and Evilasius adorn the twenty-second day.

([Note: [Col. 0611D] “The scales make the hours of daylight and sleep equal.” We have added this verse from the Royal and Bigot manuscripts.])

And the vigil of Matthew the apostle.

## Day 21

Matthew, who abandoned the profits of the world when Christ called him,  
consecrated the eleventh day with evangelical speech.

The passion of Saint Matthew the apostle.

## Day 22

Mauritius crowns the tenth day together with his allied legion,  
which likewise conquered death by the blood it shed.

And of the Theban saints: Mauritius and his companions, six thousand six hundred and sixty-six in number.

Emmeramus is accompanied by his companion in honor,  
whom distinguished Britain calls back by name.

[Note: [Col. 0611D] “Emmeramus.” This verse and the following are absent from the Royal and Bigot manuscripts. Below, where the text has “and Liberius,” the Royal manuscript reads “and Viberius.”]

## Day 23

On the ninth day Thecla, drenched in rosy blood, holds her place;  
Pope Liberius consecrates the day throughout the city of Rome,  
and Socius the Levite shines with deserved honor.

Of Thecla the virgin, and of Januarius the bishop, and of Socius the deacon.

## Day 24

On the eighth day John, conceived in a barren womb,  
and the kindly martyr and presbyter Andochius consecrate the day;  
Tyrsus and Felix accompany him with equal devotion.

## Day 25

On the seventh day Bishop Lupus revisits Lyon’s walls,  
a pastor worthy of remembrance to the devoted city.

The people of Amiens shine through the martyr Firminus.

In Asia, of Saint Eucarpius. And elsewhere, the deposition of Saint Mark.

## Day 26

On the sixth day the martyr Cyprian triumphs; the blessed virgin Justina,  
after abandoning mad arts and pagan rites,  
made him recognize the kingdom of God.

And the deposition of Saint Eusebius, bishop.

## Day 27

On the fifth day Cosmas excels together with his brother Damianus;  
Antimus follows them, and Leontius and Euprepius,  
who dedicated a fivefold garland to you, Christ, through death.

[Note: [Col. 0612D] “A fivefold garland to you, Christ.” Thus correctly in the Royal and Bigot manuscripts; the earlier edition had “a single one,” incorrectly.]

And of Saint Eleutherius.

## Day 28

Faustus, Martialis, and Januarius adorn the fourth day,  
distinguished alike by the robe and struggle of martyrdom.

[Note: [Col. 0612D] “Faustus.” In the Royal manuscript, *faustum*, so that the word refers to the following word *quartum*, “the fourth day,” and the name of one saint is consequently lost.]

## Day 29

Mighty in heavenly virtue, Michael, prince of the heavenly host,  
consecrated temples to himself on the third day.

The deposition of Saint Salonius, bishop.

## Day 30

Jerome, approved interpreter of the old and new law,  
teacher of doctrine and condemner of wicked heresy,  
closes the rejoicing September on the preceding day.

## OCTOBER

October, laden with foaming must and fruits—  
let us recall those for whom sacred cups and baskets are brought.

## Day 1

Remigius, who first taught and subdued the savage Franks,  
marks October with his own worthy honor.

Germanus likewise, distinguished in doctrine and deed,  
fortifies his own Auxerre with merits—  
he who drove back the deserters from the faith and the impious doctrine,  
and whom Pictish Britain protected by miracles.

Bavo accompanies these men in virtue and sacred honor.

[Note: [Col. 0613D] “Antisiodorum.” It is useful to observe here that in the Royal manuscript *Autisioderum* is written everywhere, without exception.]

And of Saint Vedastus.

## Day 2

Soon Leodegarius adorns the sixth Nones,  
whom the leader and people killed when he was powerful amid sedition.

In Gaul, at the city of Arras, the passion of Saint Leodegarius the martyr.

## Day 3

The Ewalds, equal in merits, nation, surname, altar,  
and teaching, dedicated the fifth day to themselves through death.

And the feast of Saints Eusebius, Pontius, and Leo.

## Day 4

Marcus and Marcianus fill the fourth day with their service,  
brothers in birth, martyrdom, nature, and death.

## Day 5

On the third Nones Bishop Apollinaris honors the day,  
whose shrines populous Ravenna crowns.

In Egypt, the feast of Fortis the deacon and Flaviana the virgin.

## Day 6

The virgin Faith triumphs on the preceding day through a blessed death.

In Africa, of Rogata, Saturnina, Faustina, and Saint Pardulfus the confessor.

## Day 7

The bishops Linus and Marcus retain the Nones.

The feast of Saints Marcellus and Apuleius, and the feast of Saint Mark, bishop.

## Day 8

On the eighth day before the Ides you are blessed, holy Demetrius,  
having suffered unjust torturers for the sake of Christ’s name.

## Day 9

Abraham, an example of faith, obedience, and wholesome discipline,  
first called by the name of the exalted Father,  
then called Father of the nations by heavenly destiny,  
sanctifies and holds the seventh day in blessedness.

On this day too Dionysius shines with distinguished and threefold martyrdom,  
whose temples illuminate the whole world  
with their light, and who shines with heavenly honor.

Gaul received the teacher whom Paul established, blessed,  
adorned and joined with a twofold minister.

And they shine together with Domninus, the renowned Italian martyr.

[Note: [Col. 0613D–0614D] “With Paul establishing him.” Here Wandalbertus follows the common opinion that the first apostle of the Parisians was none other than the Dionysius mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles. When the most learned men of our own age attempted to uproot this opinion from people’s minds, they held that our Dionysius was contemporary with the emperor Decius. Yet I readily believe that Dionysius the Areopagite never came to Gaul, since Saint Dionysius, bishop of Corinth, almost his contemporary, testifies that he was the first bishop of Athens, in Eusebius, *Ecclesiastical History*, book III, chapter 4. But the claim of Fortunatus of Poitiers, and later of the bishops of Gaul in the year 823, that Dionysius was sent to Gaul by Clement, bishop of the city of Rome, does not seem to me capable of being overturned solely by the authority of Gregory of Tours.]

## Day 10

Holy Lot adorns the sixth day with titles of justice.

Cassius, Gereon, Victor, and Florentius, together with the people joined to them,  
triumph as companions of martyrdom.

In Africa, of Eusebius and Heraclius; and elsewhere, of Serenus and Crescentius; and the translation of the body of the most blessed Martialis.

## Day 11

On the fifth day Taracus, Probus, and Andronicus crown the calendar,  
whom glory makes equal in virtue and death.

At Acerno in Sicily, the feast of Saints Faustus and Januarius.

## Day 12

On the fourth day before the Ides Edistius increases the honor by his merits,  
the city of Ravenna, which possesses this celebrated martyr.

In a city of Campania, the feast of Saints Fortunatus and Priscianus.

## Day 13

Marcellus, Faustus, and Januarius fill the third day.

Then also a temple sacred to you, Peter, and to Dionysius shines;  
an altar also gleams for Chrysanthus and Daria,  
at Tulpia, where a fortress rises above the level plain.

In Spain, at the city of Córdoba, of Saints Faustus and Marcia. At Limoges, the dedication of Saint Salvator, and of Saint Geraldus the confessor.

## Day 14

On the preceding day Bishop Callistus, a martyr outstanding in triumph,  
shines accompanied by a great number of martyrs.

At Rome, on the Via Aurelia, in the city, the feast of Saint Callistus, bishop.

## Day 15

From here, on the Ides, the crowd of the Moors is summoned to you,  
and Agrippina, rejoicing together in blessed spirits,  
dedicated their service to Christ through courage and death.

At Capua, on the Via Aurelia, the feast of Saint Fortunatus.

## Day 16

Gallus the confessor is honored on the seventeenth day,  
which marks the approaching November.

And two hundred and seventeen are remembered together,  
whom wicked fury slaughtered for Christ with equal honor.

In Africa, the feast of Saints Nereus and Saturninus.

## Day 17

The holy bishop Florentius adorns the sixteenth day.

In Mauretania, the feast of Saints Donatus and Des[...].

## Day 18

Luke, dedicated to the festival and service on the fifteenth day,  
shows Christ speaking through your words, Paul.

Triphonia too shines beside her, a trampler of dominion.

([Note: “From here Scorpio governs the pleasant seasons of autumn.”])

In the East, the translation of the body of Saint Luke the evangelist.

## Day 19

Beronicus and Pelagia shine on the fourteenth day;  
forty-nine others accompany them together.

In Antioch of Syria, the feast of Saint Pelagia and forty-eight others.

## Day 20

On the thirteenth day you honor the martyr Caprasius.

## Day 21

The presbyter Asterius shines on the twelfth day,  
an outstanding teacher who taught many saints to conquer  
the wars threatening the devout everywhere with harsh death.

The good inhabitant of the desert, Hilarion, also accompanies him.

Then, in great number, along the banks of the Rhine, shine  
the trophies raised to Christ by virgin battalions  
for the city of Agrippina, whose impious fury once slaughtered  
thousands under the leadership of illustrious holy women.

## Day 22

Bishop Philip increases the eleventh day with his festival.

On this same day Hermes shines, and blessed Eusebius.

[Note: [Col. 0615D] “Hermes on this same day.” In the Royal and Bigot manuscripts, *Ermas*.]

In a city of Thrace, the passion of Saint Leodegarius and of Saint Philip, bishop.

## Day 23

Holy Severinus, from the summit of the first temple,  
look upon your colonists on the tenth day, shining.

At Trajanopolis, of Severus and Donatus.

## Day 24

On the ninth day, forty-six shine in triumph,  
renowned at Rome for military service and sacred struggle.

Vertanus adorns and celebrates his own Martinus.

[Note: [Col. 0616D] “And Martinus.” We have added this verse from the Royal manuscript.]

At Nicomedia, of Saints Vitalis, Felix, and Victor.

## Day 25

On the eighth day Crispinus and Crispinianus hold their place,  
who, having suffered the flames, conquered the savage tyrant.

On the same day we venerate the twin gems of martyrdom,  
Chrysanthus and Daria, whom Rome, newly brought there  
through Christ’s gift, adorns with tombs at Nova Cella,  
where the waters of the Rhine succeed the lofty forests.

Here too Hilary shines with the high honor of a bishop.

On the same day, the feast of Saint Fronto, bishop and confessor.

## Day 26

The seventh day displays bishops radiant in fame, signs, and tombs:  
Amandus, as his true name indicates,  
and Vedastus, joined alike in merits and time.

In Nicomedia, the feast of Saints Lucianus and Marcianus. The translation of the body of Saint Amandus.

## Day 27

From here the martyr Vincent, fighting, adorns the sixth day.

Christeta likewise triumphs, together with the virgin Sabina.

And the vigil of the apostles Simon and Jude.

## Day 28

Simon and Jude excel on the fifth day in honor,  
whom wealthy Persia, when God sent them, received;  
it deserved to bury them, faithful patrons,  
in martyrdom and signs, if afterward it had been a cultivator of faith.

Here Cyrilla, born under Decius, shines as a virgin  
of blessed spirit, and whose father Decius was not.

Here too Matrona is honored along the shores of the Faro.

## Day 29

From here the presbyter Zenobius, holding the fourth day, adorns it.

In Luciana, the feast of Saints Quintinus and Felicianus.

## Day 30

On the third day Marcellus, armed with Christ’s love,  
consecrated a company worthy of heaven,  
accompanied by two hundred and twenty martyrs.

And the translation of the body of Saint Saturninus, bishop.

## Day 31

On the preceding day they celebrate Quintinus as blessed for his deeds;  
a victor distinguished by varied and illustrious struggle for Christ,  
he sets October, collapsing, in the closing circle.

And of Saint Foillanus the martyr.

## NOVEMBER

Now too, in the long night, who will keep vigil for November?  
Let us bring forth in song the saints whom people celebrate by keeping watch.

## Day 1

Caesarius marks November at its very beginning,  
and Rome rejoices in his exceptional triumph.

This month too, surpassing the others with its starry crown,  
joins all the saints in a single honor,  
those whom the kingdom of heaven alike retains and cherishes.

On the fourth day, holy Victorinus, martyr, you are blessed.

[Note: [Col. 0617D] “And you are blessed as a martyr.” In the Royal manuscript, “and blessed in merits.”]

## Day 2

On the Nones, Julianus and Benignus also shine;  
the presbyters shine, distinguished in virtue and blood.

## Day 3

On the third day Germanus, Vitalis, and Caesarius,  
and Theophilus, shine with equal festive light.

At Trajectum, the deposition of Saint Hubertus, bishop.

## Day 4

From here, on the preceding day, Bishop Amantius adorns the Rutheni.

In Africa, the feast of Saints Primus, Perpetua, and Victor.

## Day 5

On the Nones the prophet Zacharias, priest of the temple,  
stands out; having had his voice taken away,  
he received the prophet’s office again according to ancient custom.

The holy Felix and the monk Eusebius also increase the day.

And of Saint Mary and Saint Secunda.

[Note: [Col. 0617D] “He stands out, having had it taken away.” We corrected this from the Bigot manuscript; previously it was read corruptly as “having forgotten it.”]

## Day 6

On the eighth Ides the martyr Felix is celebrated.

In the city of Rennes in Gaul, the deposition of Saint Melanius, bishop, and of Saint Leonard the confessor.

## Day 7

On the seventh day you consecrated Amarantus through a blessed death.

Willebrordus also holds this day, through whom, as leader of the people,  
many of the Frisian people perceived Christ calling them.

At Nicomedia, of Rogatus, Donatus, Primus, and Julia.

## Day 8

On the sixth day, distinguished by merit and blood,  
Claudius, Castor, Simplicius, Symphorianus,  
and Nicostratus shine with the equal light of a crown.

[Note: [Col. 0617D] “Symphorianus.” The Royal and Bigot manuscripts read *Sempronianus*.]

In Nicomedia, the feast of Saints Eusebius and Eustasius.

## Day 9

Soon the fifth Ides bloom through Theodore the martyr.

## Day 10

On the fourth day Modestus, Florentia, and Tiberius  
shine through threefold martyrdom for the threefold name.

In Antioch, the feast of Saint Demetrius, bishop. At Rome, the deposition of Saint Leo, bishop.

## Day 11

The holy Menas triumphs on the third day in courage and faith.

Martin, a confessor by merit, office, and speech,  
a priest, and a martyr through faith, famous throughout the wide world,  
is called upon with the same prayers and festival.

Domitilla likewise triumphs, having endured exile, scourges, threats, tortures, and death for Christ.

In a city of Gaul, the falling-asleep of Saint Martin, bishop. And of Saint Menna.

## Day 12

Your Cunibertus, Agrippina, excels on the preceding day;  
the banks of the Seine also remember Saint Leonius.

In Caesarea of Cappadocia, the feast of Saints Germanus and Eusebius.

## Day 13

Then your Ides, O Martin, is held by your heir Bricius,  
approved by exile, tears, and signs.

And at Malbodium, the translation of the body of Saint Aldegundis.

## Day 14

On the eighteenth day before the December Kalends,  
Clementinus, Theodotus, and Philominus hold the day,  
having suffered together the commands of a bloody torturer.

In the city of Heraclea, the feast of Saints Clementinus and Heraclius. On the same day, the passion of Saint Justus.

## Day 15

Eugenius shines on the seventeenth day as a martyr.

In a city of Africa, the feast of Saints Saturninus and Demetrius, and of Saint Caesarius.

## Day 16

Eucherius and Gregory fill the sixteenth day,  
the former a priest of Lyon, the latter of Neocaesarea.

In Capua, the feast of Saints Vitalis and Januarius.

## Day 17

On the fifteenth day, along the banks of the Loire and among the festive peoples,  
Anianus shines with eternal praise, merit, signs, prayer, and counsel;  
he redeemed his own city from hostile ruin.

([Note: [Cols. 0617D–0618D] “Among the festive peoples.” I can scarcely doubt that ignorance of a word, not altogether uncommon, has disfigured this passage. Since “festive peoples” does not fit well here, it is probable that the name of some people lies hidden beneath the word *festivos*. It may have been the Belsivori, or certainly the Belsini—that is, those who inhabit Belsia, commonly called Beauce. The name of this province is found in the writings of Fortunatus from before Wandalbertus’s time; for that reason I would gladly read here “the Belsini peoples.”])

([Note: [Col. 0618C] “From here the Archer darkens the sky with icy light.”])

In the city of Hierapolis, the feast of Saints Victor, Alpheus, and Romola.

## Day 18

Hesychius crowns the fourteenth day as a martyr,  
and Romanus, whose city Antioch rejoices, returns.

In Caesarea, of Victor, Maximus, and Marcianus.

## Day 19

On the thirteenth day Felicianus, Severinus,  
and Exuperius consecrate the day through the struggle of faith.

In Caesarea, of Januarius, Vitalis, and Marcianus. At Autun, of Simplicius, bishop.

[Note: [Col. 0619D–0620D] “At Autun.” Here we shall make several observations which may perhaps seem neither unwelcome nor useless to the reader. First, in the Royal manuscript the name is everywhere written *Agustidunum*, and although this spelling is incorrect, it was long in use; this is established both by other evidence and by coins, on which Justinian, Justinus, and Tiberius are generally called *Augusti*, but not rarely *Agusti*. Secondly, in the same manuscript, whenever Auxerre is mentioned, the city is always called *Autisioderum*. This deserves all the more attention because it is clear that the modern name Auxerre was derived not from *Autisiodorum*. Finally, whenever the names Eufemia and Foca occur, they are written in the same manuscript exactly as you see them, not in the customary forms *Euphemia* and *Phoca*. We have retained this spelling as well, since the coins themselves, the best witnesses of antiquity, reject the common form, as may be seen in the work entitled *Coins of the Roman Emperors from Trajan Decius onward*, and so forth.]

## Day 20

Pontianus, blessed bishop and martyr,  
to you Rome dedicates and consecrates the twelfth day in service.

In Spain, the feast of Saint Maximus the presbyter.

## Day 21

The abbot Columbanus keeps the eleventh day for himself,  
he who spread the teachings of holy life from the very Ocean among many people,  
through pious religious devotion, word, and hand.

And the vigil of Saint Cecilia.

## Day 22

Soon holy Cecilia illuminates the tenth day with perpetual radiance,  
ever to be proclaimed through glorious trophies,  
a virgin supported here by her kinsman, there by her holy husband.

At Rome, the passion of Saint Cecilia the virgin.

## Day 23

On the ninth day Pope Clement holds his place through struggle  
and through the lofty titles of his virtues. Having suffered death in the waters,  
he found a temple built by divine gift.
