For ever and ever. Amen.

*(Here numbers II, III, and IV are missing. They do indeed appear in the table of contents, but only to refer the reader elsewhere.)*

## V. The First Sunday after Christmas Day

[Note: [Col. 0802D] Although only the Cologne manuscript contains this second book, nevertheless the two manuscripts of Saint Bavo of Ghent and Utrecht contain almost all the prayers found in this book.]

God, who through the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary bestowed the rewards of eternal salvation upon the human race, grant, we ask, that we may perceive her interceding for us, through whom we were deemed worthy to receive the author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ.

### Secret

[Col. 0802C]

Having received our gifts and prayers, Lord, cleanse us also through the heavenly mysteries, and mercifully hear us. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, that we who rejoice in celebrating the nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ may, by worthy conduct, be found deserving to share in his fellowship. Through our Lord.

## VI. The Second Sunday after Christmas Day

Almighty and everlasting God, direct our actions according to your good pleasure, so that in the name of your beloved Son we may be found abounding in good works. Through the same Son.

[Col. 0802D]

### Secret

Grant, we ask, that the gift offered before the eyes of your majesty may obtain for us both the grace of devotion and the attainment of blessed eternity. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Through the working of this mystery, Lord, may our vices be cleansed and our righteous desires fulfilled. Through Christ.

[Col. 0803A] [Over the People

Merciful God, be favorable, etc., as above among the Daily Prayers.]

## VII. The First Sunday after the Theophany

Follow with heavenly kindness, we ask, Lord, the vows of your suppliant people, so that they may both see what must be done and be strengthened to fulfill what they have seen. Through Christ.

### Secret

May the sacrifice offered to you, Lord, always give us life and protection. Through the Lord.

### Preface

D. And it is right, up to “eternal God.” For when your only-begotten Son, etc., as above on the day of the Epiphany.

### After Communion

We humbly ask you, almighty God, to grant that those whom you refresh with your mysteries may also serve you graciously with conduct pleasing to you. Through our Lord.

[Over the People

Preserve your family, we ask, Lord, etc., as above among the Daily Prayers.]

## VIII. The Second Sunday after the Theophany

Almighty and everlasting God, who govern heavenly and earthly things together, mercifully hear the supplications of your people and grant your peace in our times. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Sanctify the gifts offered, Lord, and cleanse us from the stains of our sins. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May the working of your power increase in us, Lord, we ask, so that, nourished by the divine mysteries, we may by your gift be prepared to receive their promises. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Help your people, Lord, etc., as above among the Daily Prayers.]

## IX. The Third Sunday after the Theophany

[Col. 0803D]

Almighty and everlasting God, mercifully look upon our weakness and extend the right hand of your majesty to protect us. Through the Lord.

### Secret

May this offering, Lord, we ask, cleanse our offenses and sanctify the bodies and minds of your subjects for the sacrifice that is to be celebrated. Through Christ.

### After Communion

We ask you, Lord, to make those whom you grant to share in such great mysteries truly conform to their effects. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Be present, Lord, we ask, etc., as above in the cited place.]

## X. The Fourth Sunday after the Theophany

God, who know that, placed amid such great dangers, we cannot endure because of human frailty, grant us health of mind and body, so that, with your help, we may overcome what we suffer because of our sins. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the gift offered in this sacrifice may always cleanse and protect our frailty from every evil. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May your gifts, God, release us from earthly pleasures and always furnish us with heavenly nourishment.

[Over the People

The voice of the Church crying out, etc., as above in the place already mentioned.]

## XI. The Fifth Sunday after the Theophany

Guard your family, we ask, Lord, with continual compassion, so that those who rely on the hope of heavenly grace alone may always be protected by you. Through Christ.

### Secret

[Col. 0804C]

We offer you, Lord, offerings of reconciliation, so that, in your mercy, you may absolve our sins and direct wavering hearts. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may receive the effect of that salvation whose pledge we have received through these mysteries.

[Over the People

The voices of your Church, Lord, etc., as above in the same place.]

## XII. The Sixth Sunday after the Theophany

Preserve your people, God, and make them devoted to your name, so that, subject to divine service, they may receive both temporal things courageously and eternal gifts. Through Christ.

### Secret

May this offering, God, cleanse, renew, govern, and protect us, we ask. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Having been fed with heavenly delights, Lord, we ask that we may always desire those same things through which we truly live. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Grant, we ask, almighty God, etc., as above in the same place.]

## XIII. The First Sunday after the Octave of Easter

[Col. 0805A]

God, who raised up the fallen world through the humility of your Son, grant perpetual joy to your faithful, so that those whom you have rescued from the dangers of everlasting death you may cause to enjoy eternal joys. Through the same Lord.

### Secret

May the sacred offering always confer your saving blessing upon us, Lord, so that what it performs in mystery it may accomplish in power. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Grant us, almighty God, that, having received the grace of your vivifying power, we may always glory in your gift.

[Col. 0805B] [Over the People

Your family, etc., as above.]

## XIV. The Second Sunday after the Octave of Easter

God, who show the light of your justice to those who stray so that they may be able to return to the way, grant to all who are reckoned among those professing Christianity both to reject what is hostile to this name and to pursue what is suited to it. Through Christ.

### Secret

May these mysteries grant us, by moderating earthly desires, to learn to love heavenly things. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May the sacraments we have received, Lord, we ask, both instruct us with spiritual nourishment and protect us with bodily assistance. Through our Lord.

[Over the People

Let it rejoice, etc., as above.]

## XV. The Third Sunday after the Octave of Easter

God, who make the minds of the faithful of one will, grant your peoples to love what you command and to desire what you promise, so that amid the changing things of the world our hearts may be fixed where true joys are found. Through our Lord.

### Secret

God, who through the venerable exchange of this sacrifice make us participants in the one supreme divinity, grant, we ask, that just as we know your truth, so we may attain it through worthy conduct. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Be present, Lord our God, so that through what we have faithfully received we may both be cleansed from vices and stripped of every danger. Through Christ.

## XVI. The Fourth Sunday after the Octave of Easter

God, from whom all good things proceed, grant to those who supplicate you that, with you inspiring us, we may think what is right, and, with you governing us, do the same. Through Christ.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, the prayers of the faithful together with the offerings of sacrifices, so that through these acts of pious devotion we may pass into heavenly glory. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Grant us, Lord, filled by the power of the heavenly table [alternatively: “by the satiety of the heavenly table”], both to desire what is right and to receive what we have desired. Through our Lord.

## XVII. The Sunday after the Ascension of the Lord

[Col. 0806B]

Almighty and everlasting God, make us always bear a will devoted to you and serve your majesty with a sincere heart. Through Christ.

### Secret

May the immaculate sacrifices purify us, Lord, and give vigor from heavenly grace to our minds. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Filled with sacred gifts, Lord, grant, we ask, that we may always remain in thanksgiving. Through Christ.

[Over the People

God, life of the faithful, glory of the humble, and blessedness of the righteous, mercifully receive the prayers of those who supplicate you, so that the souls that thirst for your promises may always be filled from your abundance. Through the Lord.]

## XVIII. The First Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0805D] Although the manuscript calls these Sundays by this heading, several Missals have “The First Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost.” Berno asserts that this is a better way of establishing agreement with the antiphon and reading for the twenty-third Sunday, in his *Book on the Mass*, chapter 5; he expressly explains the prayer and indicates its agreement with the Gospel concerning Lazarus and with the Introit “Lord, in your mercy,” which are found above in the Lectionary and Antiphonary for the First Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost. Therefore I judge that it should also be read this way here, and correspondingly in the twenty-three Sundays, especially since the three manuscripts mentioned above also give these Sundays the same headings.]

God, the strength of those who hope in you, mercifully be present to our invocations; and because mortal weakness can do nothing without you, grant the help of your grace, so that in carrying out your commandments we may please you both in will and in action. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Mercifully receive our offerings dedicated to you, Lord, and grant that they may bring us perpetual assistance. Through Christ.

### After Communion

[Col. 0806D]

Filled with such great gifts, Lord, grant, we ask, that we may both receive saving gifts and never cease from your praise. Through our Lord.

[Over the People

May the desired blessing confirm your faithful, Lord; may it make them never depart from your will, and may it always allow them to rejoice in your benefits. Through the Lord.]

## XIX. The Second Sunday after Pentecost [Octave of Pentecost]

[Col. 0807A]

Grant that we may always possess both fear and love of your holy name, Lord, because you never abandon those whom you establish in the firmness of your love. Through Christ.

### Secret

May the offering to be dedicated to your name, Lord, purify us and transfer us day by day to the practice of heavenly life. Through our Lord.

### After Communion

Having received your gifts, Lord, we ask that the effect of our salvation may increase through our frequent participation in the mystery. Through Christ.

[Col. 0807B] [Over the People

God, who declare that you remain in upright and sincere hearts, grant us by your grace to become such persons in whom you may deign to dwell. Through Christ.]

## XX. The Third Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0807D] This office seems to be omitted here and placed on the octave of Pentecost, because it is clearly superfluous in the total of twenty-four Sundays, since only twenty-three Sundays are established as arranged in the Antiphonary and Sacramentary, especially since the same point is emphasized by the *Micrologus*, chapter 61.]

Mercifully hear our petition, we ask, Lord, and to those to whom you grant the disposition to petition, grant the assistance of protection. Through Christ.

### Secret

Sanctify the gifts offered, Lord, so that they may become for us the body and blood of your only-begotten Son. Through the same Son.

### After Communion

May this communion, Lord, cleanse us from guilt and make us sharers in heavenly healing. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Always turn the hearts of your people toward you, Lord, we ask, so that those whom you cause to be helped by such great protections you may not cease to govern with perpetual safeguards. Through the Lord.]

## XXI. The Fourth Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0808D] I think it should be read: “The Third Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost,” and likewise in what follows.]

God, protector of those who hope in you, without whom nothing is strong and nothing is holy, multiply your mercy upon us, so that, with you as our ruler and guide, we may pass through temporal goods in such a way that we do not lose eternal ones. Through Christ.

### Secret

[Col. 0807D]

Look upon the gifts of your supplicant Church, Lord, and grant that they may be received for the perpetual sanctification of believers. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May your holy gifts, Lord, which we have received, give us life and prepare us, once purified, for everlasting mercy. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Be favorable to your people, Lord, and absolve them from every [Col. 0808A] sin, so that what we deserve through our offenses may be driven away by your indulgence. Through the Lord.]

## XXII. The Fifth Sunday after Pentecost

Grant us, Lord, we ask, that the course of the world may be directed peacefully for us according to your ordering, and that your Church may rejoice in tranquil devotion.

### Secret

Having mercifully received the offerings, Lord, compel our rebellious wills also to turn toward you. Through our Lord.

### After Communion

May the holy mysteries, Lord, purify us and protect us by their gift. Through the Lord.

### Over the People

Be present to your people, Lord, and in ineffable compassion come to the aid of those who presume on nothing from their own conscience, so that what confidence in merits does not possess may be supplied by the unconquerable abundance of your gifts. Through the Lord.

## XXIII. The Sixth Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0808D] See in Berno, *Book on the Mass*, chapter 5, the agreement of this office with the reading for the Fifth Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost.]

God, who have prepared invisible good things for those who love you, pour the affection of your love into our hearts, so that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may attain your promises, which surpass every desire. Through the Lord.

### Secret

[Col. 0808C]

Be favorable to our supplications, Lord, and mercifully receive these offerings of your male and female servants, so that what each has offered for the honor of your name may benefit all for salvation. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Those whom you have satisfied with a heavenly gift, Lord, grant, we ask, that we may be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Give your people, Lord, we ask, a mind by which they may remain devoted to you; understanding by which they may ask for what is right; and your favor, by which you may bring to completion what will benefit those who devoutly desire it. Through the Lord.]

## XXIV. The Seventh Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 0808D]

God of hosts, to whom belongs everything that is excellent, implant the love of your name in our hearts and grant increase in devotion within us, so that you may nourish what is good and, with watchful diligence, preserve what has been nourished. Through Christ.

### Secret

Be favorable to our supplications, Lord, and mercifully receive these offerings of your people; and, so that no one’s vow may be fruitless and no one’s petition empty, grant that what we faithfully ask we may effectively obtain. Through Christ.

### After Communion

We have been filled with your gifts, Lord; grant, we ask, that by their effect we may be cleansed and by their assistance protected. Through our Lord.

[Over the People

Absolve the sins of the peoples, Lord, we ask; and by your kindness let us be freed from the bonds of the sins we have contracted through our frailty. Through the Lord.]

## XXV. The Eighth Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 0809B]

[Note: [Col. 0809D] See in the same author, and in the *Micrologus*, chapter 61, the agreement of this office with the reading and the Offertory for the Seventh Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost.]

God, whose providence is not deceived in its ordering, we humbly entreat you to remove all harmful things and grant us everything that will benefit us. Through the Lord.

### Secret

God, who established the distinction of the legal sacrifices through the perfection of one sacrifice, receive a sacrifice from servants devoted to you; and with equal blessing sanctify it, as you did the gifts of Abel, so that what each has offered for the honor of your majesty may benefit all for salvation. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May communion in your sacrament, Lord, grant us purification and bestow unity. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Be present to your peoples, Lord, etc., as above among the Daily Prayers.]

## XXVI. The Ninth Sunday after Pentecost

Mercifully grant us always the spirit of thinking what is right, Lord, we ask, and of doing it, so that we who cannot exist without you may be able to live according to you. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts that we bring to you from your own generosity; and may these sacred mysteries, through the working of your grace, sanctify us by the conduct of our present life and lead us to everlasting joys. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May the heavenly mystery be for us, Lord, the restoration of mind and body, so that we may experience the effect of the action whose celebration we perform. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Your blessing, etc., as above in the cited place.]

## XXVII. The Tenth Sunday after Pentecost

[Col. 0810A]

May the ears of your mercy, Lord, be open to the prayers of those who supplicate you; and, so that you may grant the things desired to those who ask, make them ask for what is pleasing to you. Through Christ.

### Secret

Grant us, we ask, Lord, to celebrate these mysteries frequently, because whenever the commemoration of this offering is celebrated, the work of our redemption is performed. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

May your medicinal working, Lord, mercifully release us from our perversities and lead us to what is right. Through the Lord.

[Another

May communion in your sacrament, Lord, grant us purification and bestow unity. Through the Lord.]

[Over the People

Mercifully look upon us, Lord, etc., as above.]

## XXVIII. The Eleventh Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0809D] See in the same author the agreement of this office with the Gospel for the Tenth Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost. [Col. 0810D]]

God, who manifest your omnipotence especially by sparing and showing mercy, multiply your mercy upon us, so that, running toward your promises, you may make us sharers in heavenly goods. Through Christ.

### Secret

[Col. 0810C]

May the sacrifices dedicated to you, Lord, be rendered; you have granted that they be brought to the honor of your name, so grant that they may become remedies for us. Through Christ.

### After Communion

We ask, Lord our God, that you may not in your kindness deprive of your assistance those whom you never cease to restore through the divine sacraments. Through the Lord.

[Over the People

Your faithful, Lord, etc., as above.]

## XXIX. The Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0810D] Berno likewise gives there the agreement of this prayer with the reading for the Second Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost, as does the *Micrologus*, chapter 61.]

Almighty and everlasting God, who in the abundance of your compassion surpass both the merits and the vows of those who supplicate you, pour your mercy upon us, so that you may forgive what conscience fears and add what prayer does not presume to ask. Through Christ.

### Secret

Mercifully look upon our service, Lord, we ask, so that what we offer may be an acceptable gift to you and a support for our frailty. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May we experience, Lord, we ask, through receiving your sacrament, assistance of mind and body, so that, saved in both, we may glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Protect your people, Lord, etc., as above.]

## XXX. The Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0811D] The agreement of this office with the reading and antiphon for the Twelfth Sunday after the Octave of Pentecost.]

Almighty and merciful God, from whose gift it comes that you are worthily and laudably served by your faithful, grant us, we ask, to run without stumbling toward your promises. Through Christ.

### Secret

Mercifully regard the offerings we present upon the holy altars, Lord, so that, by granting us forgiveness, they may give honor to your name. Through Christ.

[Col. 0811B] ### After Communion

May participation in this holy mystery give us life, Lord, we ask, and likewise grant us expiation and protection. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Mercifully look upon us, Lord, etc., as above.]

## XXXI. The Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost

[Note: [Col. 0812D] Also the agreement of this office with the Gospel for the Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost.]

Almighty and everlasting God, grant us increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, so that we may deserve to attain what you promise, make us love what you command. Through Christ.

### Secret

[Col. 0811C]

Be favorable to your people, Lord; be favorable to the gifts, so that, appeased by this offering, you may both grant us forgiveness and grant what we ask. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Having received the heavenly sacraments, Lord, may we advance, we ask, toward the increase of eternal redemption. Through Christ.

[Over the People

May the Lord protect, we ask, etc., as above.]

## XXXII. The Fifteenth Sunday after Pentecost

Guard your Church, Lord, with perpetual favor; and because all mortality slips without you, may it always be drawn away from harmful things by your assistance and directed toward salvation. Through Christ.

### Secret

Grant us, we ask, Lord, that this saving offering may become both the cleansing of our sins and the propitiation of your power. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

May your sacraments always purify and protect us, God, and lead us to the effect of perpetual salvation. Through Christ.

[Col. 0812A] [Over the People

Preserve the hearts of your own, etc., as above.]

## XXXIII. The Sixteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May continual compassion cleanse and protect your Church, Lord; and because it cannot stand safe without you, may it always be governed by your gift. Through Christ.

### Secret

May your sacraments guard us, Lord, and always protect us against the assaults of the devil. Through Christ.

### After Communion

May the working of the heavenly gift possess our minds and bodies, Lord, we ask, so that not our own sense but the effect of the age to come may continually precede within us. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Preserve your people, we ask, Lord, etc., as above.]

## XXXIV. The Seventeenth Sunday after Pentecost

May your grace, Lord, always both precede and follow us, and continually make us intent upon good works. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Cleanse us, Lord, through the effect of the present sacrifice, and mercifully perfect us, so that we may deserve to share in it. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

[Col. 0812C]

Mercifully purify our minds, Lord, we ask, and renew them through the heavenly sacraments, so that thereafter we may receive both present and future assistance for our bodies. Through our Lord.

[Over the People

Your family, etc., as above.]

## XXXV. The Eighteenth Sunday after Pentecost

Grant your people, we ask, Lord, to avoid demonic contagions and to follow you alone, the Lord, with a pure mind. Through Christ.

### Secret

We humbly beseech your majesty, Lord, that these holy rites which we perform may strip us both of past sins [Col. 0812D] and of future ones. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Through your sanctifications, almighty God, may our vices be healed and eternal remedies come to us. Through Christ.

[Over the People

Hear us, God, etc., as above.]

## XXXVI. The Nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost

May the working of your compassion direct our hearts, Lord, we ask, because without you we cannot please you. Through our Lord.

### Secret

God, who through the venerable exchange of this sacrifice make us participants in the one supreme divinity, grant, we ask, that just as we know your truth, so we may attain it with worthy minds and conduct. Through Christ.

### After Communion

We give thanks to you, Lord, strengthened by the sacred gift, and beseech your mercy to make us worthy participants in it. Through Christ.

[Over the People
Graciously attend upon our times, we beseech you, O Lord, with pious favor, and to those to whom you grant a longer course, kindly provide continual assistance. [Col. 0813B]

### XXXVII. THE TWENTIETH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

[Note: Also for this prayer, see Berno, in the often-cited place, concerning its agreement with the reading and the antiphon of the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost.]

Almighty and merciful God, graciously remove from us every adversity, so that, freed alike in mind and body, we may carry out what belongs to you with unencumbered minds. Through.

**Secret.**

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that these gifts which we offer before the eyes of your majesty may be salutary for us. Through.

**After Communion.**

May your healing work, O Lord, graciously free us from our perversities and make us cleave to your commands. Through the Lord.

[Over the people.

With your right hand, O Lord, [protect] your household, etc., as above.]

### XXXVIII. THE TWENTY-FIRST SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

[Note: Likewise, see the agreement of this prayer with the reading and antiphon of the Twentieth Sunday after the octave of Pentecost.]

Be gracious, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant your faithful forgiveness and peace, so that they may alike be cleansed from every offense and serve you with a secure mind. Through.

**Secret.**

May these mysteries, we beseech you, O Lord, provide us heavenly medicine and cleanse the faults of our heart. Through our Lord.

**After Communion.**

[Col. 0813D] Make us worthy, O Lord, of the sacred gifts, we beseech you, and cause us to obey your commands. Through the Lord.

[Over the people.

Protector of those who hope in you, etc., as above.]

### XXXIX. THE TWENTY-SECOND SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

[Note: This prayer likewise agrees with the reading and antiphon of the Twenty-First Sunday after the octave of Pentecost.]

Guard your household, we beseech you, O Lord, with continual loving-kindness, so that, with you as its protector, it may be free from every perversity and devoted to your name in good works. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Graciously receive, O Lord, the offerings by which you have willed to be appeased and, by your powerful loving-kindness, to restore salvation to us. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

Having received the nourishment of immortality, we beseech you, O Lord, that we may pursue in mind what we have received with our mouth. Through.

[Over the people.

Give to your people, we beseech you, O Lord, etc., as above.]

### XL. THE TWENTY-THIRD SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

[Note: Finally, Berno discusses this prayer’s agreement with the reading and antiphon of the Twenty-Second Sunday in the place cited.]

O God, our refuge and strength, be present to the devout prayers of your Church, as their very author of loving-kindness, and grant that we may effectively obtain what we faithfully ask. Through.

**Secret.**

Merciful God, grant that this saving offering may continually free us from our own offenses and protect us from every adversity. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

We have received, O Lord, the gifts of the sacred mystery, humbly beseeching you that what you have commanded us to do in remembrance of you may advance as an aid to our weakness. Through the Lord.

[Over the people.

Hear us, O Lord our God, and govern your Church, which is tossed amid the storms of the world, with compassionate direction. Through the Lord.]

### XLI. [Note: I read “the Twenty-Third Sunday after the octave of Pentecost,” as was also noted above.] THE TWENTY-FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

Stir up, O Lord, we beseech you, the wills of your faithful, so that, more eagerly carrying out the fruit of the divine work, they may receive greater remedies from your loving-kindness. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Be gracious to your supplicants, O Lord, and, having received the offerings and prayers of your people, turn all our hearts toward you, so that, freed from earthly desires, we may pass to heavenly longings. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0814D] **After Communion.**

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, that through the gift of the medicine itself whatever is faulty in our mind may be healed by the sacraments we have received. Through the Lord.

### XLII. MASS FOR ORDINARY DAYS

Guard in perpetual peace those whom you have granted to hope in you, we beseech you, O Lord. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0815A] **Another.**

Be present to us, merciful God, and graciously grant us the gifts of your loving-kindness. Through.

**Secret**

Be present to us, O Lord, we beseech you, and kindly hear our prayers, so that what confidence in our merits does not possess may be obtained through the appeasement of the offerings. Through.

**After Communion.**

May the holy mysteries, O Lord, both fill us with spiritual nourishment and protect us with bodily assistance. Through.

### XLIII. ANOTHER MASS

Hear us, compassionate and merciful God, and graciously grant us the gifts of saving self-restraint. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings**

Graciously receive, O Lord, the offerings presented, so that by sanctifying us they may also become salutary for us. Through.

**After Communion.**

May your holy gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, strip us of our sins and strengthen us with the vigor of heavenly life. Through.

### XLIV. ANOTHER MASS

We beseech you, almighty God, that your people, serving you with their whole heart, may continually merit both your benefits and peace. Through.

**Over the offerings.**

[Col. 0815C] Graciously receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the offering of human redemption, and work salvation of mind and body for us. Through.

**After Communion.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, satisfied by the power of the mysteries, our life may be strengthened. Through.

### XLV. ANOTHER MASS

Graciously govern our wills, O Lord, so that they may neither be entangled in their own iniquities nor subjected to those of others. Through.

**Secret.**

May your sacraments, O God, surround and renew us, and likewise confer upon us both a temporal remedy and an eternal one. Through.

[Col. 0815D] **After Communion.**

May your holy gifts, almighty God, which we have received, grant us forgiveness and provide the aid of perpetual protection. Through.

### XLVI. ANOTHER MASS

Always restrain, we beseech you, O Lord, harmful assaults, and graciously grant peaceful security in our times. Through.

**Secret.**

Before your sight, O Lord, we beseech you, may our gifts be such that they can both appease you and perfect us so that we may please you. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0816A] **After Communion.**

Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that the daily gifts of the sacrament may increase perpetual salvation for us. Through the Lord.

**ANOTHER MASS**

Defend us, we beseech you, O Lord, from every adversity, and always protect us with continual safeguards. Through.

**Secret.**

We offer you, O Lord, the gifts which you have given, so that they may testify to the assistance of your creation concerning our mortality and work for us the remedy of immortality. Through.

**After Communion.**

May we grasp with our mind what we have received with our mouth, O Lord, [Col. 0816B] and may the temporal gift become for us an everlasting remedy. Through the Lord.

**Another.**

May your gifts preserve us, we beseech you, O Lord, and grant eternal life to us who implore you. Through the Lord.

### XLVII. ON THE FEAST OF ONE APOSTLE

The Prayer, Secret, and After Communion are as above, in the Vigil of Saint Andrew.

[Over the people.

Hear, O Lord, your people supplicating with the patronage of your holy apostle N., so that they may always be able to serve you with secure devotion through your help. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0816C] **At Vespers.**

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your blessed apostle N., graciously grant that we may imitate in our conduct the one whose feast we celebrate. Through the Lord.]

### XLVIII. ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL APOSTLES

O God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of your apostles N. and N., grant, we beseech you, that we who rejoice in their merits may be instructed by their examples. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Secret.**

Graciously receive, O Lord, the gifts which we bring for the solemnity of your apostles N. and N., and avert all the evils which we deserve. Through.

[Col. 0816D] **After Communion.**

We beseech you, O Lord, that, filled with saving mysteries, we may be aided by the prayers of those whose solemnities we celebrate. Through.

[Over the people.

O God, who granted your apostles the authority to bind and loose, grant, we beseech you, that through them we may be freed from earthly vices and, set free, be able to take part in the heavenly mysteries. Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**

Be the sanctifier and guardian of your people, O Lord, so that, fortified by apostolic protection, they may please you in their way of life and serve you securely. Through the Lord.]

### XLIX. ON THE FEAST OF ONE MARTYR

[Col. 0817A]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the feast of your blessed martyr N. may, through his intercession, be strengthened in the love of your name. Through.

**Over the offerings.**

Having received our gifts and prayers, O Lord, cleanse us with heavenly mysteries and graciously hear us. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord our God, that just as we rejoice in the temporal observance through the commemoration of your saints, so we may rejoice in their perpetual vision. Through the Lord.

[Over the people.

[Col. 0817B] May your people, O Lord, magnify you by glorifying your holy martyr N., and, with him always praying, may they merit to have you as their ruler. Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**

O God, who surround and protect us with the glorious confession of your blessed martyr N., grant us, we beseech you, to advance by imitating him and to rejoice in his prayer. Through the Lord.]

### L. ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL MARTYRS

O God, who grant us to celebrate the feasts of your holy martyrs, N. and N., grant us to rejoice in their fellowship in eternal blessedness. Through.

**Secret.**

[Col. 0817C] We offer you, O Lord, the gifts of our devotion; may they be pleasing to you in honor of your righteous ones and, by your mercy, be made salutary for us. Through.

**After Communion.**

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, through the intercession of your saints N. and N., that we may receive with a pure mind what we touch with our mouth. Through.

[Over the people.

Be present, O Lord, to your people supplicating with the protection of your saints, so that what they do not presume upon through their own confidence they may obtain through the merits of those who intercede. Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we may share in the rewards of your holy martyrs N., whose victories we celebrate. Through the Lord.]

### LI. ON THE FEAST OF ONE CONFESSOR

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed confessor N. may increase both devotion and salvation in us. Through.

**Secret.**

May your saints, O Lord, gladden us everywhere, so that, while we recall their merits, we may experience their protection. Through.

**After Communion.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, giving thanks for the gifts we have received, we may receive greater benefits. Through.

[Over the people.

May your people, O Lord, always rejoice in honor of your saints, so that through their intercession they may receive the desired assistance by whose protection they are raised up.

**At Vespers.**

Protect us, we beseech you, O Lord, by the safeguards of your holy confessor N., and may we always be aided by his intercessions. Through the Lord.]

### LII. ON THE FEAST OF SEVERAL CONFESSORS

O God, who surround and protect us with the glorious confessions of your saints N. and N., grant us to advance through their imitation and to rejoice through their intercession. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**

Receive, O Lord, the prayers and gifts; so that they may be worthy in your sight, may we be aided by the prayers of your saints. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

Filled with the nourishment of the sacred Body and precious Blood, we beseech you, O Lord our God, that what we undertake with devout faith we may receive with certain redemption. Through.

[Over the people.

Guard, we beseech you, O Lord, your people, continually renewed by participation in the mysteries and protected by the constant supplication of your holy confessors. [Col. 0818C] Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**

May the precious confession of your holy confessors, O Lord, warm us, and may their devout intercession continually protect us. Through the Lord.]

### LIII. ON THE FEAST OF ONE VIRGIN

O God, who, among other things, etc., as above on the feast of Saint Agatha.

**Another**

May your blessed martyr N. implore forgiveness for us, for she was always pleasing to you both by the merit of chastity and by her profession of your virtue. Through.

**Secret.**

[Col. 0818D] Receive, O Lord, the gifts which we bring on the solemnity of your blessed martyr N., by whose protection we know ourselves to be delivered. Through.

**After Communion.**

May the mysteries we have received aid us, O Lord, and, through the intercession of your blessed martyr N., strengthen us with everlasting protection. Through the Lord.

[Over the people.

May the supplication of your blessed virgin N., almighty God, be present to your people, so that those who glory in her honors may be protected by her assistance. Through the Lord.

**At Vespers.**

Almighty and everlasting God, show your mercy to your suppliants, so that we who distrust the quality of our merits may, through the intercession of your blessed virgin N., experience not your judgment but your forgiveness. Through the Lord.]

### LIV. FOR SEEKING THE SUFFRAGES OF THE SAINTS

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the intercession of holy Mary, the Mother of God, and of all your holy apostles, confessors, and elect may gladden us everywhere, so that, while we recall their merits, we may experience their protection. Through.

**Secret.**

Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and, with all your saints interceding, defend us from every danger. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

[Col. 0819B] We have received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord, while celebrating the solemnities of your saints; grant, we beseech you, that what we undertake temporally we may attain in eternal joys. Through the Lord.

### LV. FOR MAKING A CLERIC

**Prayer.**

[Note: [Col. 0819D] You have this prayer in the Roman Order, page 86.]

Let us pray, dearly beloved brothers, to our Lord Jesus Christ for this servant of his, N., who hastens, for love of him, to remove the hair from his head: that he may grant him the Holy Spirit, who will preserve the habit of religion perpetually in him and defend his heart from the impediment of the world or from secular desire; so that, just as his appearance is changed, his right hand may grant him increase in virtue, open his eyes from every human blindness, and bestow upon him the light of eternal grace. He who lives and reigns.

**Another.**

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and deign to bless this servant of yours, N., upon whom we place the habit of sacred religion in your holy name, so that, by your gift, he may merit both to persevere devoutly in the Church and to receive eternal life. Through.

**While tonsuring him, say:**

**Antiphon:** You are, O Lord, who will restore my inheritance.  
**Verse:** The Lord is the portion of my inheritance.  
And: Glory be to the Father.  
**Antiphon:** This is the generation.  
And: Glory be to the Father.

[Col. 0819D] **Prayer after the tonsure.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that this servant of yours, N., whose head of hair we have removed today for divine love, may remain perpetually in your love, and guard him forever without blemish. Through.

### LVI. BLESSING OF THE GARMENTS OF A VIRGIN OR WIDOW

O God, who promised your faithful a saving garment and clothing of eternal joy, we humbly implore your mercy: graciously bless these garments, signifying humility of heart and contempt for the world, with which your servant N. is visibly to be formed according to a holy purpose; and may she, under your protection, preserve the habit of blessed chastity which she has received through your inspiration. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Another.**

O God, giver of good virtues and generous outpourer of every blessing, hear our prayers, and deign to bless and sanctify this garment which your servant N. asks to put on as a covering for preserving the sign of chastity.

[Note: [Col. 0819D] This blessing and consecration may also be found in the Roman Order, p. 142, as may most of what follows.] **BLESSING OF A VIRGIN, TO BE SPOKEN BY THE BISHOP.**

Graciously look upon this servant of yours, N., O Lord, so that she may preserve, under your guidance, the purpose of holy virginity which she has undertaken through your inspiration. Through.

[Col. 0820B] **Consecration.**

O God, gracious inhabitant of chaste bodies and lover of incorrupt souls, look upon this servant of yours, N., who offers her devotion to you, from whom she herself has received this same vow. In her, O Lord, through the gift of your Spirit, let there be prudent modesty, wise kindness, dignified gentleness, and chaste freedom; let her burn with charity and love nothing apart from you; let her live laudably and not desire to be praised. May she fear you and serve you with love. Be for her honor, joy, consolation in sorrow, counsel in uncertainty, defense in injury, patience in tribulation, abundance in poverty, food in fasting, and medicine in sickness. Through you, whom she desires to love above all things, may she preserve what she has professed, so that she may overcome the ancient enemy and cleanse away the filth of vices. Thus, by your gift, may she merit to be adorned with the fruit of a hundredfold harvest through virginity, adorned with the lamps of virtues, and joined to the company of your chosen virgins. Through.

### LVII. BLESSING OF AN ALTAR

We beseech your mercy, almighty and eternal God, that you sanctify with this present blessing this altar, which is to be consecrated for spiritual sacrifices, as you are entreated by the ministry of our voice; so that you may always deign to bless and sanctify upon it the offerings of your servants, placed there through the diligence of their devotion, and, appeased by spiritual incense, may stand ready to hear your praying household. Through.

### LVIII. CONSECRATION OF AN ALTAR

Almighty God, in whose honor we consecrate this altar under the invocation of your name, mercifully and graciously hear the prayers of our humility, and grant that upon this table libations may be acceptable, pleasing, and abundant to you, always drenched with the dew of your Holy Spirit; so that at every time and in this place you may relieve the anxieties of your supplicating household, cure its illnesses, hear its prayers, receive its vows, strengthen its desires, and grant its petitions. Through the Lord.

### LIX. FOR CONSECRATING A PATEN

We consecrate and sanctify this paten, for making upon it the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of all. Who with the Father.

Then make the sign of the cross with holy oil over the paten, and bless it with these words:

Deign, O Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this anointing and our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord. Who with you.

### LX. FOR BLESSING A CHALICE

[Col. 0821B]

Deign, O Lord our God, to pour over this chalice, formed through devout dedication for the use of your ministry, that sanctification with which you poured over the sacred chalice of your servant Melchizedek; and what cannot be made worthy of your altars by craftsmanship or metal, let it become precious and sanctified by your blessing. Through.

### LXI. PRAYER AT THE DEDICATION OF A FONT

Almighty and everlasting God, sanctify this baptistery, dedicated through heavenly visitation, by the illumination of your Spirit, so that all whom this font will wash, cleansed by a threefold washing, may by your gift obtain forgiveness of all their sins. Through.

[Col. 0821C] **Another.**

Multiply your blessing, O Lord, and strengthen our faith through the gift of your Spirit, so that those who descend into these waters may merit to be recorded in the book of life. Through the Lord.

### LXII. MASS ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE DEDICATION OF A BASILICA

O God, who each year renew the day of the consecration of this holy temple of yours and continually represent us unharmed in the sacred mysteries, hear the prayers of your people, and grant that whoever enters this temple to seek benefits may rejoice that he has obtained everything. Through.

**Secret.**

[Col. 0821D] Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, to our prayers, so that all of us who are enclosed within the bounds of this temple, whose anniversary of dedication we celebrate, may please you with complete and perfect devotion of body and soul; so that, while we render these present vows, we may, with your help, merit to come to eternal rewards. Through the Lord.

**For concluding.**

O God, who deigned to call your Church a bride, so that she might possess grace through devotion to the faith and also possess loving-kindness through the name, grant that all this people serving your name may merit to be worthy of sharing in this title; and may your Church, gathered to you in the temple whose anniversary of dedication is celebrated, fear you, love you, and follow you, so that, while continually walking in your footsteps, she may, with you as guide, merit to reach the heavenly promises. You who live.

**Over the people.**

O God, who build an eternal dwelling for your majesty from living and chosen stones, assist your supplicating people, so that what benefits your Church through bodily spaces may be enlarged through spiritual growth. Through the Lord.

### LXIII. FOR KINGS

O God, protector of all kingdoms and especially of the Christian empire, grant your servants, our kings N. and N., knowingly to cultivate the triumph of your power, so that those who are princes by your appointment may always be powerful through your gift. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Receive, O Lord, the prayers and offerings of your Church, which supplicates for the salvation of your servants N. and N.; and, for the protection of faithful peoples, work the ancient wonders of your arm, so that, after the enemies of peace have been overcome, Christian freedom may serve you securely. Through our Lord.

**Within the Canon.**

Receive graciously and kindly this offering of your servant N., which we offer to you in the ministry of priestly office, because you have deigned to confer imperial power upon him; and, having been entreated by our supplication, grant that, trusting in the protection of your majesty, he may increase in age and in kingdom. Through the Lord.

**After Communion.**

O God, who prepared the Roman Empire for proclaiming the Gospel of the eternal King, extend heavenly weapons to your servants N., our princes, so that the peace of the Churches may not be disturbed by any storm of wars. Through our Lord.

### LXIV. DAILY MASS FOR A KING

We beseech you, almighty God, that your servant N., who by your mercy has undertaken the governance of the kingdom, may also receive an increase of every virtue; adorned suitably with these, may he be able to avoid the monsters of vices and graciously reach you, who are the way, the truth, and the life. Through.

**Secret.**

Sanctify, O Lord, we beseech you, the gifts offered, so that they may become for us the Body and Blood of your Only-Begotten, and, by your gift, may benefit him everywhere for obtaining the salvation of soul and body and carrying out the office entrusted to him. Through.

**For concluding.**

May this saving prayer protect your servant N., O Lord, from every adversity, so that he may obtain the tranquility of ecclesiastical peace and, after the course of this time, reach the eternal inheritance. Through.

### LXV. MASS TO BE SAID FOR THE KING DURING A SYNOD

[Col. 0823A]

Almighty and everlasting God, who have deigned to exalt your servant N. to the height of kingship, grant him, we beseech you, to arrange the common salvation of all amid the multitude gathered here in such a way that he may not depart from the path of your truth. Through.

**Secret.**

Appeased by these saving sacrifices, grant, almighty God, that your servant N. may always be found fit to carry out the office of royal dignity and may be made acceptable to the joys of the heavenly homeland. Through our Lord.

**For concluding.**

May the reception of this saving sacrifice wash away the stains of sin from your servant N. and make him fit to govern the people according to your will, so that through this saving mystery he may be made invincible against visible enemies—the mystery through which the world was redeemed by divine dispensation. Through the Lord.

### LXVI. SPECIAL MASS OF A PRIEST

Almighty and everlasting God, I humbly and devoutly beseech the loving-kindness of your grace: loosen all the bonds of my evils, mercifully forgive all my crimes and sins, and, since you have deigned to call me, unworthy and sinful, to your ministry, make me such a suitable minister for you that you may receive the sacrifice from my hands peacefully and kindly, make me a participant with your chosen priests, and permit me to err in nothing concerning your commands. Through our Lord.

**Over the offerings.**

O God, who command that you be entreated by sinners and that a sacrifice of a contrite heart be offered to you, deign to accept this sacrifice which I offer with unworthy hands; and mercifully grant that I may myself merit to be an offering and sacrifice to you, so that through the exercise of this ministry I may receive forgiveness of all sins. Through.

**Preface.**

It is truly right and just, up to “eternal God.” You who, overlooking the sins of human frailty, grant the dignity of the priesthood to the unworthy, and not only forgive sins but also deign to justify the sinners themselves. It is your gift that existing things not only receive their beginnings, things begun receive nourishment, and things nourished receive fruit, but fruitful things receive help to persevere. You created me when I did not exist; once created, you enriched me with firmness of faith; faithful, although covered with the filth of sins, you endowed me with the dignity of the priesthood. Therefore I humbly entreat your omnipotence: cleanse me from past sins, strengthen me in good works during the course of this world, and confirm me in steadfast perseverance. And make me serve your altars in such a way that I may be able to reach the company of those priests who have pleased you. And through him may my vow be acceptable to you, who offered himself to you as a sacrifice, who is the maker of all and the one high priest without the stain of sin, Jesus Christ, our Lord; through whom is your majesty…

[Col. 0824A] **For concluding.**

May the reception of this sacrament, O Lord, be forgiveness of my sins and the desired appeasement of your loving-kindness, so that through these, with your help, I may be made worthy of the sacred mysteries, which, trusting in your loving-kindness, I, unworthy, presume to celebrate frequently. Through.

### LXVII. ANOTHER SPECIAL MASS OF A PRIEST

O God, source of goodness and origin of loving-kindness, who do not immediately judge the sinner but mercifully await repentance, I beseech you to wipe away the filth of my crimes and make me worthy to carry out the office entrusted to me; so that I, who unworthily undertook the ministry of your altar and carry it out with trembling, may be made diligent in performing it and be found justified among those who have pleased you. Through our Lord Jesus.

**Over the offerings.**

I beseech you, O Lord, that my offering of the present sacrifice may cleanse my crimes, through which you willed the sins of the whole world to be forgiven; and may I become worthy through frequent celebration of that which I undertook unworthily in order to celebrate frequently. Through our Lord.

**Preface.**

It is truly right and just, up to “eternal God.” While you gladly receive the satisfaction of our repentance, you yourself conceal by your judgment what we do wrong; and you overlook our past sins so that you may grant us the dignity of the priesthood. For it is yours to make me worthy to minister at your altar, whom you have deigned to promote to perform that office although I was unworthy. Forgetting the evils of my past actions, ordering the course of the present according to your will, and imposing a safeguard upon the future, may I through him be cleansed from the filth of vices, adorned with the nourishment of virtues, and joined to the company of those priests who have pleased you—him who is known to be the true and supreme high priest and the only priest without the contagion of sin, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through him.

**For concluding.**

[Col. 0824D] May the reception of this sacrament, O Lord, wipe away the stains of my sins and make me fit to carry out the office entrusted to me. Through.

**Another.**

O God, at whose command the order of all ages proceeds, look graciously upon me, your servant, whom you have deigned to promote to the order of the presbyterate; and, so that my service may please you, mercifully preserve your gifts in me. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Perfect in us, O Lord, we beseech you, in your kindness, that what we profess in the sacred mysteries we may carry out in devout actions. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0825A] **Within the Canon.**

Therefore, this offering of my service, which I, your servant and priest, offer to you because you have deigned to choose me in the order of the presbyterate to serve your sacrifices and divine altars—For this I render my vows to you, the true and living God, humbly imploring your majesty to guard in me the work of your hands and make me in every respect a suitable minister of your will. Through Christ.

**For concluding.**

Having received the abundance of your gifts, O Lord, we humbly beseech you to grant the power of your grace to those to whom you have given the service of carrying out this ministry. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0825B] **ANOTHER.**

Make me, I beseech you, almighty God, so clothed in righteousness that I may merit to rejoice in the exultation of your saints, so that, cleansed from every stain of sins, I may attain the fellowship of priests pleasing to you; and may your mercy strip me of all vices, me whom the guilt of my own conscience weighs down. Through.

**Secret.**

God of mercy, God of charity, God of forgiveness, forgive and have mercy on me, I beseech you. Graciously deign to receive the sacrifice which, through the grace of your loving-kindness, I humbly offer for my sins; and, kind, gracious, and merciful, forgive the sins which I have incurred through willingly embraced vices, so that, with a place for repentance and streams of tears granted, I may merit to receive forgiveness from you. Through.

**Preface.**

It is truly right and just, up to “eternal God.” And humbly to implore your clemency, so that you may not despise your handiwork or permit it to be afflicted by enemies. For I know that I have sinned gravely and have by no means obeyed your commands. Therefore I humbly beseech you, O Lord, always to apply your grace to me as a consolation and to appoint your mercy as a maker for kings. Hence I seek your great loving-kindness, that you may forgive my sins, because your mercy is more powerful for raising up than the enemy’s deceit is for deceiving. Have mercy on me, O Lord, according to your great mercy, so that what I am ashamed of you may forgive, and what I regret having done you may mercifully pardon. Through.

[Col. 0825D] **Within the Canon.**

Therefore, this offering which I, your servant, offer to you, may you, most merciful Father, gladly receive, I beseech you; and graciously attend to my prayers. Mercifully remove the tribulations of my heart; receive my acceptable vows; willingly fulfill my desires; graciously forgive my sins; kindly wipe away my crimes; favorably redeem me from scourges; in your mercy drive away my illnesses; with a serene face incline yourself to my petitions; increase your grace toward me in many ways; continually bestow your mercy; and [grant me] days…

[Col. 0826A] **After Communion.**

O God of charity and peace, who took up [endured] the gibbet of the cross for the salvation of the human race and poured out your blood for our redemption: graciously and kindly receive our prayers, and grant me your mercy, so that when you command me to depart from the body, the evil portion may have no power over me, but your holy angel may place me among your saints and elect, where light remains and life reigns. Through.

**ANOTHER.**

I humbly beseech you, most loving God, almighty Father, who are the creator of all things: while I confess that I, your servant, have sinned gravely before the omnipotence of your majesty, extend to me the hand of your mercy; so that, while I offer this oblation before the power of your majesty, you may deign most mercifully to absolve what I have wickedly committed. Through.

**Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah.**

In those days Jeremiah said: “Lord, all who abandon you shall be put to shame; those who depart from you shall be written in the earth, because they have abandoned the Lord, the source of living waters. Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my praise, O Lord my God.”

**Reading from the holy Gospel according to John.**

At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, whatever you wish you will ask, and it will be done for you.”

[Col. 0826C] **Over the offerings.**

To you, O Lord my God, I offer the sacrifices of my devotion. I pray and likewise beseech your clemency: receive me, made your sacrifice through the mortification of carnal life, as an offering of sweet fragrance, and form me according to the conduct appropriate to my profession. You have separated me from the purpose of other human beings through the ardor of holy compunction; distinguish me also from carnal conduct and from the uncleanness of earthly actions by the holiness poured into me from heaven, so that I may despise all earthly things and desire heavenly things. Through.

**Preface.**

It is truly right and just, up to “eternal God.” Who, out of love for human beings, was made in the likeness of sinful flesh: the Lord assumed the form of a servant, and in the appearance of one wounded the physician walked. This one is for us Lord and minister of salvation, advocate and judge, priest and sacrifice. Through him I humbly beseech you, holy Father: while I acknowledge the guilt of my conscience, that I have been a transgressor of your commands and through the crime of my offenses have fallen into ruin, raise me up, O Lord, whom the fall of sin has cast down; enlighten the blind man whom the darkness of earthly sins has obscured; release the prisoner whom the bonds of sins restrain. Grant this through our holy, glorious, and adorable Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, whom the angels praise, the dominions adore, and the powers tremble before.

[Col. 0827A] **Within the Canon.**

Therefore, this offering which I offer to you, O Lord, for my lesser sins and offenses, I humbly ask your majesty with all my strength, most loving God, graciously to receive; entreating you to forgive the crimes which through the frailty of the flesh and the temptation of wicked spirits I have wickedly committed. Do not permit me to return to them again, but strengthen me in your justifications and grant me perseverance in them; make me worthy to stand before your sight and to offer a sacrifice to you, the Lord, with a pure heart and chaste body; and [grant] our days…

**After Communion.**
Almighty and eternal God, Lord Jesus Christ, be propitious toward my sins, through the taking of your body [Col. 0827B] and blood, and through the intercession of your saint N. For you yourself, speaking, said: “Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him.” Therefore I suppliantly beseech you to create in me a clean heart, renew a right spirit within me, and graciously strengthen me with a steadfast spirit; cleanse me from all the snares of the devil and from vices, so that I may be worthy to share in the joys of heaven. Who, with the Father.

## Another

God, beneath whose eyes every heart trembles and all consciences are afraid, mercifully look upon the prayers and groanings of me, so that just as you made me, without any preceding merits, stand in the place of this your service at the sacred [Col. 0827C] altars, so, according to the multitude of your mercies, grant forgiveness of my sins, so that my frailty, which is of itself inclined to fall, may through you always be restored to forgiveness. Through.

### Secret

I, your unworthy servant, offer you, Lord, sacrifices of reconciliation and praise for the forgiveness of my offenses, begging your mercy to cleanse me graciously from hidden guilt and suitably purge me from manifest sins. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. Your omnipotence is to be praised, your loving kindness embraced, and your mercy entreated. We humbly implore your loving kindness [Col. 0827D] also to grant us forgiveness of all our sins, to direct our actions according to your will, and graciously to rescue us from every evil; so that, defended by your help from every adversity, strengthened in every good thing, and enabled to pass through this present life blamelessly under your governance, we may, by your generosity, happily reach eternal life. Through Christ.

### After Communion

God, who have graciously strengthened me, unworthy as I am, with the sacred mysteries, the body and blood of your most beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, I humbly beseech your mercy: let this not be for the judgment of my soul. Grant me, I beg you, Lord, a sinner, forgiveness [Col. 0828A] and grace, which my merits do not demand; extend to me, fallen as I am, the hand of your loving kindness, and open for me, a sinner, the door of your heavenly kingdom, through which, by your gift, I may be worthy to enter into everlasting rest. Through the same.

## Another

Almighty and eternal God, who have willed that I, a sinner, stand at the sacred altars and praise the power of your holy name, grant, I beg you, through the mystery of this sacrament, forgiveness of my sins, so that I may be worthy to minister suitably to your majesty. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Grant, we beseech you, most merciful Father, through the mystery of this offering, forgiveness of my sins, [Col. 0828B] so that this order of the presbyterate may benefit me, not for the judgment of my soul, but for everlasting forgiveness. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. You have adorned the sevenfold order of ecclesiastical dignity with the sevenfold gift of the Holy Spirit. Mercifully grant me, your servant, to merit that same Paraclete Spirit in holiness of life, whom your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, promised that he would send to your faithful. May he graciously inspire in me, a sinner, steadfastness in the catholic faith and the sweetness of your holy charity; may he teach me to despise earthly things and love heavenly things. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0828C] ### After Communion

As we receive, Lord God, the sacraments of our salvation, grant, we beseech you, that their participation may benefit me, your servant, for everlasting salvation. Through.

### Another

Most gentle God, incline the ears of your loving kindness to my prayers, and illumine my heart with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that I may be worthy to minister suitably to your mysteries and to love you with everlasting charity. Through.

## LXVIII. Votive Mass for a Friend, or for Anyone You Wish

God, who justify the ungodly and do not desire the death of sinners, we suppliantly beseech your majesty [Col. 0828D] graciously to protect your servant N., who trusts in your mercy, with heavenly assistance, and to preserve him through continual protection, so that he may constantly serve you and not be separated from you by any temptations. Through.

### Over the Offerings

By the power of this mystery, Lord, we beseech you both to cleanse us from our own offenses and to absolve your servant N. from every sin. Through.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. We implore the mercy of your majesty: graciously grant your servant N. forgiveness of his sins, so that, freed from all the bonds of the enemy, he may cling to your commandments with his whole heart. May he always love you alone with all his strength [Col. 0829A] and merit at last to reach the vision of your blessedness. Through.

### After Communion

May the sacraments we have received purify us, Lord, we beseech you, and grant that your servant may be free from every fault, so that he who is bound by the guilt of conscience may rejoice in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through the Lord.

## LXIX. Another Mass

Almighty and eternal God, have mercy on your servant N. and, according to your clemency, direct him in the way of eternal salvation, so that, by your gift, he may desire what is pleasing to you and accomplish it with all his strength. Through the Lord.

### Reading from the Epistle of Blessed Paul the Apostle to the Galatians

[Col. 0829B] Brothers, if someone is overtaken in any offense, you who are spiritual should instruct such a person in a spirit of gentleness.

### Reading from the Holy Gospel according to John

At that time, Jesus lifted his eyes to heaven and said: “Father, now I am coming to you, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.”

### Secret

May this offering, which we, your simple servants, offer to your majesty, benefit the salvation of your servant N., we beseech you, Lord, so that your providence may direct his life everywhere amid adversity and prosperity. Through.

### After Communion

Having received the sacraments of everlasting salvation, we beseech your clemency, Lord, that through them you may protect your servant N. from every adversity. Through our Lord.

### Another

Keep your servant always under your protection, Lord, we beseech you, so that he may serve you with a free mind and, under your protection, be secure from every evil. Through.

## LXX. Another

Be present to our supplications, Lord, and graciously accept this offering of your servant N., so that he who implores the help of your mercy may receive the grace of sanctification and obtain what he devoutly asks. [Col. 0829D] Through.

### Secret

May this offering of your servant N., which we offer to you in honor of your blessed martyr N., be pleasing to you, Lord; we beseech you to let it benefit him for salvation. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, we beseech you, graciously accept this offering which we offer for your servant N., so that he may merit to obtain forgiveness of all his sins. By the generosity of your mercy grant that it may bring him forgiveness of offenses and amendment of actions, so that he may live well here and happily reach eternal blessedness. And our days.

[Col. 0830A] ### For Completion

By the power of this mystery, Lord, we beseech you, may we be cleansed from our own hidden faults, and absolve your servant N. from every sin. Through.

## LXXI. Mass for the Well-Being of the Living

Extend the right hand of heavenly assistance, Lord, to your male and female servants N., so that they may seek you with their whole heart and obtain what they rightly ask. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Be favorable to our supplications, Lord, and graciously accept these offerings of your male and female servants, which we offer to you for their safety. Grant, we beseech you, that no vow may be fruitless and no petition empty, so that we may effectively obtain what we faithfully ask for. [Col. 0830B] Through.

### For Completion

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, steadfastness in your faith and sincerity to your male and female servants, so that, formed in divine charity, they may not be torn away from its integrity by any temptations. Through the Lord.

## LXXII. Another Mass for Relatives

God, who have poured the gifts of charity through the grace of the Holy Spirit into the hearts of your faithful, grant your servants, for whom we implore your clemency, health of mind and body, so that they may love you with all their strength and accomplish with complete love whatever is pleasing to you. [Col. 0830C] Through our Lord.

### Reading from the Epistle of Blessed Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Brothers, the Spirit also helps our weakness.

### Reading from the Holy Gospel according to John

Jesus lifted his eyes to heaven and said: “Father, those whom you have given me, I desire that where I am, they also may be with me.”

### Over the Offerings

Have mercy, we beseech you, Lord God, on your servants, for whom we offer this sacrifice of praise to your majesty, so that through these holy gifts they may obtain the grace of heavenly blessedness and acquire the glory of blessedness. Through the Lord.

### Preface

[Col. 0830D] It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. We earnestly implore your clemency, so that you may make your servants, whom you have joined to us in the familiarity of sacred love, subject to you with their whole heart. Filled with the spirit of your charity, may they be cleansed from earthly desires and, by your gift, be made worthy of heavenly blessedness. Through Christ the Lord.

### After Communion

As we partake of the divine mysteries, we beseech you, Lord, that these salutary sacraments may benefit for prosperity and peace those for whose love we have offered them to your majesty. Through.

### Another

God, who graciously receive the vows of your suppliants through works of charity, grant your servants N. and N. to progress in your love, so that they may serve you with a secure mind and merit always to stand in your peace. Through our Lord.

## LXXIII. Mass for an Abbot or Community  
### [For a Bishop or the People Entrusted to Him]

Almighty and eternal God, who alone work great wonders, extend over your servant N., the abbot, or over the community entrusted to him [the bishop or over the people entrusted to him], the spirit of saving grace, and pour upon them an everlasting dew of your blessing, so that they may please you in truth. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Graciously regard, Lord, the offerings of your servants, and may they perceive that those which we celebrate for them with devoted mind in honor of your name benefit them for healing. Through.

### After Communion

Accompany with perpetual protection, Lord, those whom you continually refresh with a heavenly gift; and grant that those whom you never cease to cherish may be made worthy of everlasting redemption. Through.

## LXXIV. Prayer in a Monastery of Monks

God, who prepare a dwelling in heaven for those who renounce the world, enlarge the temporal dwelling of this holy community with heavenly goods, so that they may be held together [Col. 0831C] by the bond of fraternal charity, unanimously observe the precepts of continence, and, sober, simple, and peaceful, recognize that grace has been freely given to them; may their life agree with their name, and may their profession be perceived in their conduct. Through.

## LXXV. Prayer for Brothers Being Sent on Their Way

God, who always bestow your mercy on those who love you and are near in every region to those who serve you, direct the way of your servant according to your will; with you as protector and guide, may he walk without offense along the paths of justice. Through.

## LXXVI. Prayer for Those Returning from a Journey

[Col. 0831D] Almighty and eternal God, disposer of our times and our life, grant your servant N. the support of continual tranquility, so that him whom you have restored safely to his own labors you may make secure through your protection. Through the Lord.

## LXXVII. Prayer at the Arrival of Brothers Who Come to Us

God, visitor of the humble, who console us with fraternal love, extend your grace over our fellowship, so that through those in whom you dwell we may perceive your coming among us. Through the Lord.

## LXXVIII. Mass for Travelers

Be present to our supplications, Lord, and arrange the way of your servant N. in the prosperity of your salvation, so that amid all the changes of this road and of this life he may always be protected by your help. [Col. 0832A] Through the Lord.

### Secret

Be favorable to our supplications, Lord, and graciously accept these offerings which we offer to you for your servant N., so that you may direct his journey with your preceding grace and deign to accompany it with your following grace, so that we may rejoice in his actions and safety according to the supports of your mercy. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. From you, to depart is to die; before you, to walk is to live. You lead your faithful along your way and, in your exceedingly great mercy, bring them into truth. You willed to be the guardian, guide, and companion of Abraham, Isaac, and [Col. 0832B] Jacob throughout the course of their present life and journey, and you gave your servant Tobiah an angel to go before him. We implore your immeasurable mercy with most humble prayers: direct the journey of your servant N. with his companions in prosperity, and deign to guard him amid all the changes of this journey and life; so that, supported by the protection of your angels and fortified also by the intercession of the saints, defended by your mercy from every adversity, and granted a successful departure and return, he may obtain the fulfillment of righteous desires and rejoice in the forgiveness of his sins and those of his companions. Through Christ the Lord.

### For Completion

God of infinite mercy and immeasurable majesty, whom neither distances of place nor intervals of time separate from those whom you protect, be present to your servants N. and N., who trust in you everywhere, and deign to be their guide and companion along every road they are to travel. Let no adversity harm them and no difficulty obstruct them; let everything be healthful and everything prosperous for them, and, under the help of your right hand, may they quickly obtain whatever they seek with righteous desire. Through the Lord.

### Another

Having received the mysteries of the heavenly sacrament, we beseech you, Lord, that they may benefit the journey of your servant N. for prosperity and lead him to every salutary outcome. Through the Lord.

## LXXIX. Mass for Those Traveling by Sea

[Col. 0832D]

God, who carried our fathers across the Red Sea and transported them through the great waters as they sang the praise of your name, we humbly beseech you to protect your servants on this ship, with adversities driven away, in a much-desired harbor and on a tranquil course. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, we beseech you, the prayers of your servants together with the offerings of sacrifices, and defend those who celebrate your mysteries from every danger. Through the Lord.

### For Completion

Sanctified by the divine mystery, we humbly beseech and ask your majesty, Lord, that those whom you make participants in heavenly gifts [Col. 0833A] may, through the wood of the holy cross, be drawn away from sins and, in your mercy, rescued from every danger. Through the Lord.

## LXXX. Mass for Sins

Hear, Lord, we beseech you, the prayers of your suppliants, and spare the sins of those who confess to you, so that in your kindness you may grant us both forgiveness and peace. Through the Lord.

### Reading from the Prophet Jeremiah

If our iniquities contend against us, Lord, deliver us, we beseech you; do this for the sake of your name.

### Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Luke

[Col. 0833B] At that time, Jesus said to his disciples: “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.”

### Over the Offerings

We offer you sacrifices of reconciliation, Lord, so that in your mercy you may absolve our offenses and direct wavering hearts. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. Save us from the mouth of the most savage lion, who prowls about roaring, seeking someone from the unity of your Church to seize and devour. But you, most mighty Lord from the tribe of Judah, crush the wickedness of the opposing power; preserve us in body, delivered from its fiery attacks, and purify us in heart. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0833C] ### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, we beseech you, accept this offering which we offer for our sins and offenses, so that it may merit to obtain forgiveness of all our offenses. Lord, grant this.

### For Completion

Grant us, eternal Savior, that, having received forgiveness of sins through this gift, we may henceforth avoid sins. Through the Lord.

### Another

God, whose characteristic it always is to have mercy and spare, receive our supplication, so that your merciful loving kindness may absolve those whom the chain of offenses binds. Through the Lord.

## LXXXI. Prayer in Time of War

[Col. 0833D]

Almighty and merciful God, we beseech you, make us quiet amid the turmoil of wars, for you will provide us with every good thing if you grant peace of mind and body. Through the Lord.

## LXXXII. Mass in Time of War

God, ruler of all kingdoms and sovereigns, who both heal by striking and preserve by forgiving, extend your mercy to us, so that, with the tranquility of peace strengthened by your power, we may use the remedies of correction. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0834A] ### Over the Offerings

Regard the sacrifice that we offer, Lord, so that it may strip us of every evil of wars and establish us in the security of your protection. Through the Lord.

### Preface
