It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. Under whose authority the power of all kingdoms is contained, we humbly beseech you graciously to be present to our rulers, so that those who seek to be defended by your protection may be stronger than all their enemies. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Strengthened by the nourishment of the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, we humbly ask you, almighty God, that by this saving remedy you may purify us from the contagion [Col. 0834B] of all sins and guard us from the assault of every danger. Through the same.

## LXXXIII. Another Mass

Almighty God, we beseech you, restrain the enemies of the Christian name by the power of your majesty, so that your people may rejoice in the integrity of faith and always exult in the tranquility of the times. Through the Lord.

### Secret

By the power of this mystery, Lord, we beseech you, may we be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through the Lord.

### For Completion

May participation in your holy mystery give us life, Lord, and at the same time grant us expiation and protection. Through the Lord.

## LXXXIV. Another Mass

God, who by your providence govern heavenly and earthly things alike, be favorable to the affairs of Christians and to their rulers, so that, while you fight on our behalf, every strength of the enemies may be broken. Through the Lord.

### Over the Offerings

Be favorable, Lord, to the prayers and sacrifices of your servants, and for the sake of your name defend the leaders of the Christian people, so that the peace of the rulers who serve you may be the salvation of your peoples. Through the Lord.

[Col. 0834D] ### After Communion

Protect your servants, Lord, with the supports of peace and bodily well-being, and, nourishing them with spiritual food, make them secure from all enemies. Through the Lord.

## LXXXV. Mass for Peace

God, from whom come holy desires, right counsels, and just works, grant your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that our hearts, devoted to your commandments, and freed from fear of enemies, may enjoy tranquil times under your protection. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0835A] ### Over the Offerings

God, who permit peoples believing in you to be shaken by no terrors, deign to receive the prayers and offerings of the people dedicated to you, so that the peace granted by your loving kindness may make the borders of Christians secure from every enemy. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

God, author and lover of peace, to know whom is to live and to serve whom is to reign, protect your suppliants from every attack, so that we who trust in your defense may fear the weapons of no hostility. Through the Lord.

## LXXXVI. Mass for Any Tribulation

Mercifully show us your unspeakable mercy, Lord, [Col. 0835B] so that you may at once free us from sins and rescue us from the punishments that we deserve for them. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May the offering of this gift purify us, Lord, we beseech you, and make us worthy to share in the sacred things. Through.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. You rightly punish those who go astray and mercifully refresh those who have been chastised, so that you may draw us away from evil works and turn us to do good. You do not wish to find what you may condemn, but rather what you may crown. Although for our merits we continually deserve to be afflicted, you nevertheless temper judgment [Col. 0835C] for correction and do not exercise it as everlasting punishment. For you correct justly and forgive mercifully, truthful in both and merciful in both. You have also arranged us under the law, so that by restraining us you do not permit us to perish forever, and by sparing us you grant time for correction. Therefore you scourge us with present evils so that you may lead us to future goods; therefore you console us with temporal goods so that you may make us more certain of eternal ones, so that in prosperity and adversity alike we may always praise you with devout confession. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that, purified through earthly effects, we may strive toward the fullness of the heavenly sacrament, whose holy gifts we have tasted. Through our Lord [Col. 0835D].

## LXXXVII. Mass against the Pestilence of Animals

God, who have provided human labors with assistance even from mute animals, we humbly ask you not to allow those without which human society cannot be sustained to perish from our use. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Having been appeased by the sacrifices offered, Lord, mercifully grant your help in our times.

### After Communion

May the faithful people receive your blessing, Lord, so that, saved in body and mind, they may offer you fitting service and always find the benefits of your reconciliation. Through the Lord.

### Another

In your mercy, Lord, we beseech you, turn away from your faithful every error and drive off the destruction of raging diseases, so that those whom you justly scourge as strayers you may cherish when corrected through your mercy. Through the Lord.

## LXXXVIII. Mass for Discord

Almighty and eternal God, who resist the proud and grant grace to the humble, grant, we beseech you, that we may not, in our arrogance, provoke your indignation, but, subjected to you, may receive the gifts of your reconciliation. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0836B] ### Secret

May the holy things we handle absolve us, Lord, from every guilt and also protect us from the assault of every perversity. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Those whom you have refreshed with the heavenly mystery, Lord, graciously absolve, we beseech you, from their own and others’ offenses, so that, with minds purified by the divine gift, we may enjoy it. Through the Lord.

### Another

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, always meditating on what is reasonable, we may carry out what is pleasing to you both in word and in deed. Through the Lord.

## LXXXIX. Mass against Judges Who Act Wickedly

[Col. 0836C]

Graciously receive the prayers of your Church, Lord, so that, with every adversity removed, she may serve you in secure freedom. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Protect us, Lord, we beseech you, as we serve with your mysteries, so that we may minister to divine things in body and mind. Through our Lord.

### After Communion

We beseech you, Lord our God, that you may not allow those whom you grant to rejoice in participation in divine things to be subject to human dangers. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## XC. Mass against Slanderers

[Col. 0836D]

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that we may not care about the slander of corrupt minds, but, having trampled down that perversity, we ask that you neither permit us to be terrified by unjust attacks nor entangled by deceitful flatteries, but rather teach us to love what you command. Through the Lord.

### Secret

May the offering, Lord, which is to be sacrificed in your sight, powerfully absolve us from every vice and defend us from all enemies. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that through these holy things which we have received, while disregarding the attacks of the wicked, we may, under your guidance, carry out more carefully the things that are right. Through the Lord.

## XCI. Prayer for Requesting Rain

Pour heavenly waters upon your land, Lord, which we have seen wasting away through our iniquities, and irrigate it with the benefits of everlasting grace. Through the Lord.

### Another

Grant us, Lord, we beseech you, saving rain, and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry face of the earth. Through our Lord.

### Another

[Col. 0837B] Almighty and eternal God, who save all and desire no one to perish, open the fountain of your loving kindness and graciously pour heavenly streams upon the dry earth. Through our Lord.

## XCII. Mass for Requesting Rain

God, in whom we live and move and have our being, grant us suitable rain, so that, sufficiently supported by present aids, we may seek eternal things with greater confidence. Through.

### Another

In your mercy, Lord, we beseech you, absolve the offenses of our frailty and provide the support of heavenly waters, by which our earthly condition may be nourished and endure. [Col. 0837C] Through our Lord.

### Secret

Be appeased, Lord, by the gifts offered, and grant us the timely help of sufficient rain. Through.

### For Completion

Guard us, Lord, we beseech you, as we receive your holy things, and graciously absolve us from every sin. Through.

## XCIII. Prayer for Requesting Clear Weather

Lord God, who in the mystery of water have consecrated for us the sacraments of your salvation, hear the prayer of your people and command the terrors of overflowing rains to cease. Turn the scourge of this element toward the effect of your mystery, so that those who rejoice to have been reborn through waters of regeneration may rejoice to have been corrected by these chastising waters. Through the Lord.

### Another

We beseech you, almighty God, to restrain the abundance of rains and deign to impart to us the brightness of your countenance. Through the Lord.

## XCIV. Mass for Requesting Clear Weather

Hear us, Lord, as we cry to you, and grant clear air to us who implore you, so that we who are justly afflicted for our sins may, with your mercy going before us, experience your clemency. Through.

[Col. 0838A] ### Secret

May your grace, Lord, go before us and always follow us, and graciously accept these offerings which we bring to be consecrated to your name for our sins, so that through the intercession of your saints they may benefit us all for salvation. Through.

### For Completion

May your people, Lord, receive an increase of sacred blessing and be raised up by abundant aids of your benefits, as they are helped by such earnest prayers of intercession. Through the Lord.

## XCV. Mass for Driving Away a Storm

[Col. 0838B] God, who establish the nature of all things that serve you for the worship of your majesty through the very movements of the air, with terrors removed mercifully grant us the tranquility of your mercy [variant reading: “may your mercy grant us tranquility”], so that we may experience the clemency of him whose anger we have expiated. Through.

### Another

From your house, Lord, we beseech you, may spiritual wickedness be driven away, and may the malignity of aerial storms depart. Through the Lord.

### Secret

We offer praises and gifts, Lord, giving thanks for benefits granted and always humbly imploring you for those yet to be granted. Through.

[Col. 0838C] ### For Completion

Almighty and eternal God, who heal us both by chastising and preserve us by forgiving, grant your suppliants that we may rejoice in the tranquility of this desired consolation and always make use of the gift of your loving kindness. Through.

## XCVI. Prayers and Intercessions over a Penitent Confessing His Sins in the Usual Manner, on Wednesday in Lent

Hear our prayers, Lord, and spare the sins of those who confess to you, so that your merciful forgiveness may absolve those whom the guilt of conscience accuses. Through.

May your mercy, Lord, go before this servant of yours, we beseech you, [Col. 0838D] so that all his iniquities may be erased by swift forgiveness. Through.

Be present to our supplications, and let your merciful compassion not be far from this servant of yours. Heal his wounds and forgive his sins, so that, separated from you by no iniquities, he may always be able to cling to you, Lord. Through.

Lord our God, who are not overcome by our offense but are appeased by satisfaction, look, we beseech you, upon this servant of yours, who confesses to you that he has sinned grievously. For it is yours to grant cleansing from crimes and to provide forgiveness to sinners—you who said that you preferred the repentance of sinners to their death. Grant, therefore, Lord, that he may celebrate vigils of repentance before you and, when his actions have been corrected, rejoice that everlasting joys have been conferred upon him by you. Through.

[Note: [Col. 0839D] Further prayers may be found in the Roman Order, pp. 28, 29, and 30. Alcuin also mentions them on p. 52.]

## XCVII. [Note: [Col. 0840D] The Roman Order, pp. 51 and following, mentions these prayers; Alcuin, p. 55; Amalarius, Book I, chapter 12.] Prayers for Reconciling a Penitent, on Holy Thursday at the Lord’s Supper

Be present to our supplications, Lord, and graciously hear me also, who am the first to need your mercy, so that you may grant me, whom you appointed minister of this work not through merit of election but by the gift of your grace, confidence to carry out your gift; and may you yourself work in our ministry what belongs to your loving kindness. Through our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to this servant of yours worthy fruits of repentance, so that, having obtained forgiveness, he may be restored innocent of his offenses to your holy Church, from whose integrity he had strayed by sinning. [Col. 0839B] Through our Lord.

God, most kindly creator and most merciful reformer of the human race, who redeemed the human being cast down from eternity through the envy of the devil by the blood of your only Son, give life to this servant of yours, whose death you by no means desire, and receive him, corrected, whom you do not abandon when he goes astray. May the tearful sighs of this servant of yours move your loving kindness, Lord, we beseech you. Heal his wounds; extend to the one lying prostrate your saving hand. Do not let your Church be devastated in any part of its body; do not let your flock suffer loss; do not let the enemy rejoice at the loss of your female servant; and do not let the second death take possession of one reborn through the saving washing. To you, therefore, Lord, we pour out suppliant prayers; to you [Col. 0839C] we pour out the tears of our heart. Spare him who confesses, so that, with your help, he may mourn his sins in this mortality, to the extent that on the day of the fearsome judgment he may escape the sentence of eternal condemnation and may not know what terrifies in the darkness and what crackles in the flames. Having returned from the path of error to the way of justice, may he never again be wounded by injuries, but may what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored be whole and everlasting for him. Through the same Lord.

## XCVIII. Prayers for Visiting the Sick

God, who granted your servant Hezekiah fifteen years of life, may your power likewise raise your servant N. from the bed of illness to health. Through our Lord [Col. 0839D].

Look upon your servant N., Lord, laboring under illness of the body, and refresh the soul you created, so that, cleansed by chastisements, he may immediately perceive himself saved by your healing. Through our Lord.

God, who always rule your creation with loving care, incline your ear to our supplications, and, graciously look upon your servant N. laboring under adverse bodily health; visit him with your salvation and grant him the healing of heavenly grace. Through.

[Col. 0840A] God, who have bestowed upon the human race both the remedy of salvation and the gifts of eternal life, preserve in your servant N. the gifts of your virtues, and grant that he may experience your healing not only in body but also in soul. Through.

God of the heavenly powers, who by the power of your command drive away every illness and every weakness from human bodies, mercifully be present to this servant of yours N., so that, his weaknesses driven away and his strength restored, he may immediately bless your holy name with renewed health.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who strengthen the frailty of our condition by the gracious infusion of your power, so that our bodies and limbs may be invigorated by the saving remedies of your loving kindness, mercifully regard [Col. 0840B] this servant of yours, so that, every necessity of bodily illness being removed, the grace of his former health may be perfectly restored in him. Through the Lord.

## XCIX. Mass for the Sick

Almighty and eternal God, eternal salvation of believers, hear us on behalf of your servants N., for whom we implore the help of your mercy, so that, health being restored to them, they may give thanks to you in your Church. Through.

### Secret

God, at whose command the moments of our lives pass, receive the prayers and offerings of your male and female servants, for whom we implore your mercy in their illness, so that we may rejoice at the recovery of those whose danger we fear. Through the Lord.

### Preface

It is truly right and just, …, eternal God. You scourge your servants bodily for this reason: that they may progress in mind, powerfully showing what the splendid salvation of your loving kindness is, while you grant that illness itself may work salvation for us. Through Christ our Lord.

### For Completion

God, the singular support of human weakness, show the power of your help upon our sick, so that, aided by the assistance of your mercy, they may merit to be restored to your holy Church. Through.

## C. Prayer for Restored Health

[Col. 0840D]

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who, by pouring the grace of your blessing into sick bodies, preserve your creation with manifold loving kindness, graciously be present at the invocation of your name, and raise up this servant of yours N., freed from illness and endowed with health, by your right hand; strengthen him by your power, guard him by your authority, and restore him to your Church and your holy altars with every desired prosperity. Through.

## CI. Reconciliation of a Penitent at the Point of Death

[Col. 0841A]

We earnestly implore your majesty, Lord, that you deign to grant this servant of yours N., worn down by the long misery of penance, the forgiveness of your compassion, so that, having received again the wedding garment, he may be worthy to enter the royal banquet from which he had been cast out. Through [Christ our Lord].

## CII. MASS TO BE CELEBRATED FOR OUR DEPARTED BROTHERS

God, giver of forgiveness and lover of human salvation, we ask your clemency: grant that the brothers of our community who have passed from this world may, through the intercession of blessed N., our patron, attain a share in everlasting blessedness. [Col. 0841B] Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

God, whose mercy is without number, graciously receive the prayers of our humility, and grant complete forgiveness of sins through these sacraments of our salvation to the souls to whom you have given confession of your name. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously regard this offering which we present to you for the souls of our brothers, for whom we pour out humble prayers before your majesty, that you may deign to enroll them among the number of your saints who please you. And dispose our days.

[Col. 0841C] ### After Communion

Grant, we ask, merciful God, that the souls for whom we offer this sacrifice of praise to your majesty may, through the power of this sacrament, cleansed from all sins, receive—by your mercy—the blessedness of perpetual light. Through.

### Another

God, life of the living, hope of the dying, salvation of all who hope in you, graciously grant that the souls of this community and of all resting here, freed from the darkness of our mortality, may, through the intercession of blessed N., our patron, rejoice in perpetual light with your saints. Through.

[Col. 0841D] [Note: [Col. 0841D] Amalarius, *On Ecclesiastical Offices*, book IV, chapter 42, seems to allude to this passage.]

## ON THE THIRD, SEVENTH, OR THIRTIETH DAY AFTER THE DEPOSITION OF THE DECEASED

Be present, we ask, Lord, for the soul of your servant N., for whom on the occasion of his deposition we perform the office of commemoration, that, if any worldly stain clung to him or any worldly vice defiled him, you may forgive and cleanse it through the gift of your goodness. Through.

### Another

We ask, Lord, that you grant the soul of your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day after his death we commemorate, fellowship with your saints and elect, and pour into it continually the dew of your mercy. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0842A] **Reading from the Epistle of Blessed Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians.**

Brothers, behold, I tell you a mystery. We shall all indeed rise again, but we shall not all be changed.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.**

At that time Martha said to Jesus: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”

### Over the Offerings

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and graciously or kindly receive this offering which we present to you on the third, seventh, or thirtieth day after the deposition, for the soul of your servant N. Through.

### Preface

**Deacon:** It is right and just, up to “Through Christ our Lord.” [Col. 0842B] Through him, the salvation of the world, through him, the life of humanity, through him, the resurrection of the dead. Through him we earnestly beseech you, Lord, to deign to grant perpetual forgiveness to the soul of your servant N., whose day of deposition we celebrate, and, stripped of the contagions of mortality, to restore it to a share in eternal salvation. Through him.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously receive this offering which we present to you for the soul of your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day after his deposition we celebrate. When his body had been laid down, he returned to you, his Creator, the soul which you had given him. For him we ask your divine clemency, that, released from the bonds of death, he may be worthy to pass into life. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 0842C] ### After Communion

Almighty and everlasting God, deign to place the body, soul, and spirit of your servant N., whose third, seventh, or thirtieth day, or whose deposition, we celebrate, in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that, when the day of your acknowledgment has come, you may command that he be raised among your saints and elect. Through.

## FOR ONE WHOSE SOUL IS IN DOUBT

Almighty and merciful God, incline, we ask, your venerable ears to our brief prayers, which we humbly offer before the sight of your majesty for the soul of your servant N. [*leg.* “for which”], so that, while we are uncertain about the quality of his life, we may be consoled by the abundance of your goodness; and, if we cannot obtain complete forgiveness for his soul, may we at least, amid the very torments which he perhaps suffers, experience the abundance of your mercies. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Most merciful Father, receive, for the commemoration of your servant N., a sacrifice of appeasement and praise, so that, by your mercy, the sacrifice of the offering now presented may reach the refreshment of his soul. Through.

### After Communion

We have received, Lord, the remedies of your body and blood, beseeching the clemency of your majesty, that they may be a protection to the living and obtain forgiveness for the dead. Through our Lord.

## CIII. MASS FOR ONE DECEASED PERSON

Almighty and everlasting God, to whom no one ever prays without hope of mercy, be favorable to the soul of your servant N., so that you may join him to the number of your saints, since he departed this life in confession of your name. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

We ask, Lord, be favorable to the soul of your servant N., for whom we offer you sacrifices of appeasement; and because he remained in the Catholic faith in this light, may his recompense be granted in the life to come. Through.

[Col. 0843B] ### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously receive this offering which we present to you for the repose of the soul of your servant N., and in your goodness grant that, freed from the bonds of mortality, he may be worthy to have a portion among your faithful. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that you may lead the soul of your servant N., [Col. 0843A] received by the angels of light, into the prepared dwellings of the blessed. Through our Lord.

## CIV. MASS FOR ONE RECENTLY BAPTIZED WHO HAS DIED

God, who open the entrance to the heavenly kingdom only to those reborn from [Col. 0843C] water and the Holy Spirit, multiply your mercy over the soul of your servant N.; and to him to whom you granted a heavenly and undefiled passage after the sacrament of baptism, grant the fullness of eternal joys. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications for the soul of your servant N., for whom we offer you a sacrifice of praise, that you may deign to join him to the fellowship of your saints. Through.

### Within the Canon

Graciously receive this offering which we present to you for the soul of your servant N., and deign to insert him among the number of the blessed spirits, cleansed by the font of regeneration and freed from the dangers of this life. [Col. 0843D] Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

Be favorable, Lord, to the soul of your servant N., so that you may bring him to the blessedness of the heavenly kingdom—the one whom at the end of this life you cleansed in the font of regeneration. Through.

[Col. 0843D]

## CV. MASS FOR THE DECEASED WHO DESIRED PENANCE BUT DID NOT AT ALL OBTAIN IT

If someone, while asking for penance, is deprived of the use of his tongue when the priest arrives, it is decreed that, if suitable witnesses attest this and he himself gives satisfaction through some movements, the priest should perform everything for the penitent.

[Col. 0844A] ### Prayer

Almighty and merciful God, in whose power the human condition rests, we ask you to absolve the soul of your servant N. from all sins, and let him not lose, through being overtaken by death, the fruit of penance which his will desired. Through our Lord.

### Over the Offerings

May the offering of this present sacrifice, we ask, satisfy you, Lord, on behalf of the soul of your servant N.; may he find the forgiveness of sins which he sought, and may he receive, by way of compensation for the penance he desired, what he could not fulfill through the use of his tongue. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, we ask you graciously to receive this offering which we present to you for [Col. 0844B] the soul of your servant N., whose day of deposition we celebrate, and, in your ineffable goodness, to grant that what, overtaken by mortal condition, he could not carry out through the ministry of his tongue, he may be deemed worthy to obtain through everlasting forgiveness. And ordering our days in your peace.

### After Communion

God, from whom every good thing for the human body is hoped, grant, we ask, through these holy gifts, that just as you granted the soul of your servant N. the desire for penance [*f.* “penance”], so, in your mercy, you may grant the forgiveness he desired. Through our Lord.

## CVI. MASS ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF ONE DECEASED PERSON

Grant, Lord, we ask, that the soul of your servant [Col. 0844C] N., whose anniversary day of deposition we celebrate, cleansed by these sacrifices, may receive both forgiveness and everlasting repose. Through.

### Over the Offerings

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications for the soul and spirit of your servant N., whose annual day is observed today, for whom we offer you a sacrifice of praise, that you may deign to join him to the fellowship of your saints. Through our Lord.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously regard this offering which we present to you for the soul of your servant N., whose annual day is observed today, and command that, [Col. 0844D] freed from the bonds of mortality, he may have a perpetual portion among your faithful ministers. This offering.

### After Communion

Receive, Lord, our prayers for the soul of your servant N., that, if any stains from earthly contagions have clung to him, they may be erased by the mercy of your forgiveness. Through our Lord.

## CVII. MASS FOR MANY DECEASED PERSONS

Be merciful, Lord, we ask, with everlasting mercy to the souls of your male and female servants, so that, freed from the bonds of mortality, eternal light may possess them. Through.

[Col. 0845A] **Reading from the Book of Maccabees.**

In those days, the very brave man Judas, after a collection had been made, sent twelve thousand drachmas of silver to Jerusalem, to be offered there for the sins of the dead.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.**

At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me.”

### Over the Offerings

We bring sacrifices to you, Lord, with humble appeasement, so that through these services of appeasement the souls of your male and female servants may obtain your mercy. Through.

### Preface

**Deacon:** It is right and just, up to “Through Christ our Lord.” [Col. 0845B] We undoubtedly celebrate his sacred passion for the immortal and peacefully resting souls, especially for those to whom you granted the grace of a second birth. By this example of Jesus Christ our Lord, they began to be confident of the resurrection. For since you made what did not exist, you can separate what once existed. And you gave us proofs of the future resurrection not only through prophetic and apostolic teaching, but also through the resurrection of that same only-begotten Son of yours, our Redeemer: so that what was announced through the prophets and handed down through the apostles might be confirmed by the example of his own resurrection. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously regard this offering which we present to you for the repose of the souls of your male and female servants, and grant [Col. 0845C] that what you have deigned to prepare as a remedy for all the living may benefit the dead for forgiveness. And dispose our days.

### After Communion

May the souls of your male and female servants, and of all who rest in Christ, find a share in eternal light—those who, placed in this light, have received your sacrament. Through.

## CVIII. ANOTHER MASS

God, creator and redeemer of all the faithful, grant the souls of your male and female servants forgiveness of all sins, so that through devout supplications they may obtain the forgiveness which they have always desired. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0845D] ### Secret

We ask, Lord, graciously to regard the sacrifices which we offer to you for the souls of your male and female servants, so that, to those to whom you have granted the merit of Christian faith, you may also grant the reward. Through our Lord.

### After Communion

May the prayer of those who supplicate benefit the souls of your male and female servants, we ask, Lord, so that you may both free them from sins and make them participants in your redemption. Through.

## CIX. ANOTHER MASS

Grant, we ask, Lord, perpetual mercy to the souls of your male and female servants, so that what they hoped for and believed in you may benefit them forever. Through our Lord.

**Reading from the Book of the Apocalypse of Blessed John the Apostle.**

In those days, I heard a voice from heaven saying to me.

**Continuation of the holy Gospel according to John.**

At that time Jesus said to his disciples: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man…”

### Over the Offerings

Graciously regard these gifts, we ask, Lord, and may what we offer in supplication to the praise of your name benefit the dead for forgiveness. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0846B] ### After Communion

We pour out humble prayers, we ask, Lord, for the souls of your male and female servants, hoping that whatever they contracted through human conduct you may mercifully forgive, and that you may establish them in the dwelling of your rejoicing redeemed. Through.

## CX. MASS IN CEMETERIES

God, by whose mercy the souls of the faithful rest, graciously grant forgiveness of sins to your servants N. and N. and to all resting here in Christ, so that, freed from every guilt, they may rejoice without end.

### Over the Offerings

Lord, graciously receive the sacrifice offered for the souls of your servants N. and N. and of all the Catholics sleeping here, [Col. 0846C] so that, released from the bonds of dreadful death by this singular sacrifice, they may be worthy to possess eternal life. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, Lord, graciously receive this offering which we present to you for the repose of your male and female servants N. and N., and of all the faithful Catholic and orthodox who rest in Christ in this basilica, and of those who rest around this church; we ask that through these means of human salvation they may be counted among the number of your redeemed with an everlasting portion. Through.

### After Communion

[Col. 0846D] God, light of the souls of the faithful, be present to our supplications, and grant your servants N. and N., or those whose bodies rest here, a place of refreshment, the blessedness of repose, and the splendor of light. Through our Lord.

## CXI. MASS FOR THE SALVATION OF THE LIVING OR TO BE CELEBRATED FOR THE DEAD

Through the intercessions of your saints, we ask, Lord, protect us also, and extend your mercy everywhere to your male and female servants whose commemoration we celebrate, or whose alms we have received, and also to those who are joined to us in friendship, so that, defended from every assault, they may be saved by your help; and deign to join to the fellowship of your elect the souls of your male and female servants, namely, all the faithful Catholic and orthodox, whose commemoration we celebrate, whose bodies rest in this monastery, or whose names appear to be written before your holy altar. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications, and graciously receive these offerings which we bring to be consecrated to your name for the safety of your male and female servants and for the souls of all the faithful Catholic and orthodox, whose names appear to be written before your holy altar, so that, by your mercy, the offering of this present sacrifice may reach the refreshment of their souls. Through.

[Col. 0847B] ### After Communion

May both the reception of the divine sacrament and the glorious prayer of your saints purify us, we ask, Lord, and grant the souls of your male and female servants whose commemoration we celebrate forgiveness of all sins, so that through devout supplications they may obtain the forgiveness which they have always desired. Through.

## CXII. EXORCISM OF SALT

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God, by the true God, by the holy God, by the God who commanded you through the prophet Elisha to be thrown into the water so that the barrenness of the water might be healed, so that you may become exorcised salt [Col. 0847C] for the salvation of believers, and may be health of soul and body to all who take you; and so that every phantom and wickedness, or every deceit of diabolical fraud, and every unclean spirit may flee and depart from the place where you have been sprinkled, adjured by him who is to come to judge the living and the dead.

## CXIII. BLESSING OF SALT

We humbly implore your immeasurable clemency, almighty and everlasting God, that in your goodness you may deign to bless and sanctify this creature of salt, which you have given for the use of the human race, so that it may be salvation of mind and body to all who take it, and so that whatever is touched or sprinkled with it may be free from uncleanness, [Col. 0847D] freed from harm; may no pestilential spirit dwell there, nor any corrupting breath. May every ambush of the hidden enemy depart, so that, if anything envies the safety or peace of the inhabitants, it may flee through the sprinkling of this water, and so that health, made effective through the invocation of your name, may be defended from every assault. Through.

## CXIV. EXORCISM OF WATER

I exorcise you, creature of water, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, his Son, our Lord, so that you may become exorcised water for driving away [Col. 0848A] every power of the enemy, and may be able to uproot and tear out the enemy himself with his apostate angels, through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come…

## CXV. BLESSING OF WATER

God, who established the greatest sacraments for the salvation of the human race in the substance of water, be graciously present to our invocations, and pour the power of your blessing into this element, prepared through many kinds of purification, so that this creature, serving your mysteries, may receive the effect of divine grace for casting out demons and driving away diseases; so that whatever this water sprinkles in the houses or places of the faithful may be free from uncleanness and freed from [Col. 0848B] harm; may no pestilential spirit dwell there, nor any corrupting breath. May every ambush of the hidden enemy depart, and, if anything envies the safety or peace of the inhabitants, may it flee through the sprinkling of this water, so that health, sought through the invocation of your name, may be defended from every assault. Through the Lord.

## CXVI. BLESSING OF SALT AND WATER TOGETHER

Here salt is put into the water.

God, author of unconquerable power, king of an inseparable [*f.* unsurpassable] dominion, and ever-glorious victor, who restrain the forces of hostile rule, who overcome the savagery of the roaring enemy, who powerfully conquer hostile wickedness: trembling and supplicant, we implore and ask you, Lord, to graciously receive this creature of salt and water, kindly illumine it, and sanctify it according to the manner of your goodness, so that wherever it is scattered, through the invocation of your holy name every assault of an unclean spirit may be cast away, and the terror of the poisonous serpent driven far off; and so that the presence of the Holy Spirit may deign to be everywhere with us as we ask your mercy. Through the Lord.

## CXVII. PRAYER WHEN WATER IS SPRINKLED IN A HOUSE

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and deign to send your holy angel from heaven, to guard, cherish, protect, visit, [Col. 0848D] and defend all who dwell in this dwelling. Through.

## CXVIII. BLESSING OF A HOUSE

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and illumine this house with the serene eyes of your goodness; may the abundant blessing of your grace descend upon those who dwell in it, so that, living in these dwellings made by human hands with soundness, they themselves may always be your dwelling. Through.

### Another

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, so that, if there are any adversities or oppositions in this house of your servant N., they may be driven away by the authority of your majesty. Through our Lord.

## CXIX. PRAYER AGAINST LIGHTNING

First let blessed water be sprinkled, and afterward let this prayer be said: [Col. 0849A]

Almighty and everlasting God, spare those who fear, and be favorable to those who supplicate, so that, after the harmful fires of the clouds and the force of storms, the threat of power may pass into material for praise. Through.

## CXX. PRAYER OVER VESSELS FOUND IN AN ANCIENT PLACE

Almighty and everlasting God, enter into our offices, and by the power of your sublimity deign so to cleanse these vessels fashioned by the skill of the gentiles that, with every uncleanness driven away, they may be used by your faithful in a time of peace and tranquility. Through.

## CXXI. BLESSING OF A WELL

We beseech, Lord, the clemency of your goodness, that you may sanctify the water of this well with heavenly blessing, grant it as healthful for common life, and deign so to drive from it every attack of diabolical temptation that whoever from now on draws and drinks from it, or uses water drawn from it for any necessary purpose, may enjoy the sweetness of complete strength and health, and may be worthy always to give thanks to you, Lord, sanctifier and savior of all. Through.

## CXXII. BLESSING OF GRAPES OR *FAVAE* [BROAD BEANS]

[Note: [Col. 0849D] Following ancient usage, I consider *favae* to be the reading in place of *fabae*.]

[Col. 0849C] Bless, Lord, these new fruits, grapes or beans, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and serene and tranquil seasons, so that we may receive them with thanksgiving, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives with you…

## CXXIII. BLESSING FOR NEW CROPS

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who created heaven and earth, the sea, and all things, we humbly ask you to deign to bless and sanctify this new fruit and to multiply it abundantly for those who offer it to you, so that you may fill their storehouses with the strength of grain and wine, and so that, rejoicing in them, they may offer praises and thanks to you, God almighty. Through [Col. 0849D] the Lord.

## CXXIV. BLESSING FOR ANYTHING YOU WISH

Bless, Lord, this creature, so that it may be a salutary remedy for the human race; and grant, through the invocation of your name, that whoever takes of it may receive health of body and protection of soul. Through.

## CXXV. BLESSING OF [NEW BREAD]

Bless, Lord, this creature of bread, just as you blessed the five loaves in the desert, so that all who taste [Col. 0850A] it may receive health of both body and soul. Through.

## CXXVI. PRAYER BEFORE FOOD

Refresh us, Lord, with your gifts, and sustain us by the abundance of your riches. Through our Lord.

### Another

Bless, Lord, your gifts, which by your generosity we are about to consume. Through our Lord.

## CXXVII. PRAYER OVER THE TABLE

May your gifts be blessed for us, Lord, which by your generosity have been brought to us as a remedy, for you are God, blessed forever.

### Another

Through the prayers of holy Mary, Mother of God, the glorious and undefiled virgin, may the Redeemer of all bless what has been set before us. Through our Lord.

### Another

Through the intercessions of blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, may Christ, the Son of God, bless what has been brought before us as a remedy.

## CXXVIII. PRAYER AFTER FOOD

Satisfied, Lord, with the gifts of your riches, we give you thanks for what, by your generosity, we have received, beseeching [Col. 0850C] your mercy that what was necessary for our bodies may not be burdensome to our minds. Through our Lord.

### Another

You have satisfied us, Lord, with your gifts and what you have given; fill us with your mercy, for you are blessed, who live and reign with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

## CXXIX. PRAYER IN THE SACRISTY

Almighty and merciful God, who deign to use the ministry of priests for serving and supplicating you, we ask your immense clemency that whatever we now visit, you may visit; whatever we bless, you may bless; and that, at the entrance of our humility, there may be, through the merits of your saints, a flight of demons and the entry of the angel of peace. Through the Lord.

## CXXX. PRAYER WHERE GARMENTS ARE KEPT

God, who mercifully bestow the supports of mind and body upon those who serve you, grant, we ask, that what your goodness has supplied through these things for the uses and necessities of the bodies of your servants you may graciously cause to abound and preserve; so that, using them outwardly, and inwardly clothed with the garment of righteousness, they may always be worthy to remain devoted to you. Through.

## CXXXI. PRAYER IN THE REFECTORY

[Col. 0851A]

Almighty and merciful God, who nourish your servants in this house with bodily refreshment, may they receive food or drink with thanksgiving, as you bless it, and may they through you always be worthy to be saved, both here and forever. Through the Lord.

## CXXXII. PRAYER IN THE DORMITORY

Bless, Lord, this dormitory of your servants—you who neither sleep nor slumber, who guard Israel—and guard your servants resting in this house after their labor from Satan’s illusory phantoms. While awake, may they meditate on your commandments; while asleep, may they perceive you through savor; and here and everywhere [Col. 0851B] may they be fortified by the help of your protection. Through our Lord.

## CXXXIII. PRAYER IN THE STOREHOUSE

Almighty and merciful God, who are present everywhere, we humbly beseech your majesty that your grace may deign to be present in this storeroom, repelling every adversity from it and lavishly pouring in the abundance of your blessing. Through the Lord.

## CXXXIV. PRAYER IN THE SCRIPTORIUM

Deign to bless, Lord, this scriptorium of your servants and all who dwell in it, so that whatever of the divine Scriptures is read here by them they may understand in mind and accomplish in deed. Through.

## CXXXV. PRAYER IN THE GUESTHOUSE

Almighty and merciful God, who are the physician of human hearts and the teacher of angels, we humbly ask you to deign always to be present in the hearts of your servants who frequent this place for the sake of offering hospitality; may their speech be aflame with your fear, seasoned with salt, and full of usefulness to their neighbor, so that when those who come here have departed, they may proclaim the glory of your name through their example. Through.

## CXXXVI. PRAYER IN THE HOUSE OF THE SICK

Almighty and merciful God, we ask your immense [Col. 0851D] goodness to deign, at the entrance of our humility, to visit these servants of yours who lie exhausted in this dwelling with saving aid, so that, just as you visited Tobias and Sarah, Peter’s mother-in-law, and the centurion’s boy, so these too, having recovered their former health of soul and body, may offer you thanksgiving in your church. Through the Lord.

## CXXXVII. PRAYER IN THE FARMYARD

Multiply your mercy over us, Lord, and deign graciously to hear our prayers; and just as you heard your servant King David, who appeased you by offering sacrifices in the farmyard, [Col. 0852A] so, we ask, may the abundance of hoped-for blessing come upon this farmyard, so that, filled with your crops, we may always glory in your mercy. Through.

## CXXXVIII. PRAYER IN THE GRANARY

Almighty and merciful God, who blessed Joseph’s granaries and Gideon’s threshing floor, and, greater still, cause seeds cast into the earth to rise with the profit of the harvest, we humbly ask you that, just as at the petition of your servant Elijah the widow’s flour did not fail, so, in aid of our sinfulness, the abundance of your blessing may not fail this granary of your servants. Through the Lord.

## CXXXIX. PRAYER IN THE BAKEHOUSE

[Col. 0852B]

May the place of this workshop be sanctified, Lord, and may every unclean spirit be driven from it through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ; and may health, brightness, and joy be given to all who dwell in it, while your majesty, almighty God, protects and preserves them. You who live…

## CXL. PRAYER IN THE KITCHEN

Eternal God, before whose sight angels stand and by whose command all things are governed, who also do not cease, through your goodness, to provide for the necessities of human frailty, we humbly implore you to pour that blessing over the dwelling of this workshop by which you [Col. 0852C] sweetened the bitterest tastes in the hermit’s pot through the hands of the prophet Elisha; and, with the abundance of your blessing always overflowing here, may your servants offer praises to you, who give food to all flesh and fill every living creature with blessing, Savior of the world. You who live and reign.

## CXLI. PRAYER IN THE LARDER

[Note: [Col. 0851D] A word borrowed from the French word *Lardier*.]

Almighty and merciful God, who, mercifully foreseeing the needs of the human race, have bestowed temporal provisions, we humbly implore you to deign to bless this larder of your servants, so that what your mercy has kindly supplied here may not perish through our negligence. Through.

## CXLII. PRAYER IN THE HEATED ROOM

[Note: [Col. 0852D] *Caminatam* is used in place of *camino*, “fireplace.”]

[Col. 0852D]

Almighty and everlasting God, whose wisdom taught human beings that this house should at times be free from cold through the nearness of fire, we ask you that all who dwell in it or gather in it may be free in their hearts from the cold of unbelief through the fervor of the Holy Spirit. Through.

## CXLIII. PRAYER AT THE ENTRANCE OF THE GATE

Lord Jesus Christ, who sanctified the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem when, through the splendor of gems, you [Col. 0853A] prefigured the names of the twelve Apostles, and who through the prophetic instrument promised: “Praise the Lord, Jerusalem, for he has strengthened the bars of your gates and blessed your children within you”—we ask you to establish peace at every boundary of this house of Saint Mary and Saint Peter, so that, swiftly running within, your word may satisfy them with the fatness of grain. May the Holy Spirit defend them, so that the enemy may never prevail against them; and may all who dwell within sing out with voice, heart, and deed, saying: “Great is our Lord Jesus Christ, and great is his power, and of his wisdom there is no number.” You who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, live and reign as God, forever and ever.

## CXLIV. MORNING AND EVENING PRAYERS

### Morning Prayers

[Col. 0853B]

Look graciously upon the morning vows of those who supplicate you, Lord; illumine the hidden places of our hearts with the remedy of your goodness, and let dark desires not hold those whom the heavenly light of grace has restored. Through.

Almighty and everlasting God, before whom nothing is ever obscure or dark, send forth, we ask, your light into our hearts, so that, having received the law of your commandments, we may walk in your way and suffer no error. Through.

God, who reward those keeping vigil in your praises with a heavenly recompense, deign to remove darkness from our hearts, so that we may always rejoice in the splendor of your light. Through our Lord.

[Col. 0853C] We give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who have deigned to lead us from the passage of the night to the morning hours; we ask you to grant us to pass this day without sin, so that at evening and always we may return thanks to you, God. Through our Lord.

Rising from our beds, Lord, we implore the help of your grace in our morning prayers, so that, when the darkness of vices has been scattered, we may be worthy to walk in the light of virtues. Through.

We beseech you, Lord, the true light and author of light, to deign to drive away from us the darkness of vices and illumine us with the light of virtues. Through.

May your truth shine, we ask, Lord, in our hearts, and may every falsehood of the enemy be destroyed. Through.

[Col. 0853D] Graciously pour holy light into our understanding, we ask, Lord, so that we may always be devoted to you, by whose wisdom we were created and by whose providence we are governed. Through our Lord.

May your truth, Lord, always illumine us and defend and guard us from every wickedness. Through.

[Increase your faith in us, Lord, and always kindle in us the light of the Holy Spirit. Through. In the unity of the same.]

We give thanks to your ineffable goodness, almighty God, who, having driven away the darkness of night, have led us to the beginning of this day, and, having cast away the blindness of ignorance, have recalled us to the worship and knowledge of your name. Enter our understanding, almighty Father, so that, walking in the light of your commandments, we may follow you as guide and ruler. Through.

God, who dispel the darkness of ignorance by the light of your word, increase in our hearts the power of the faith which you have given, so that the fire which your grace has caused to be kindled may not be extinguished by any temptations. Through.

Hear with your ears, we ask, Lord, the words of our heart, and, as a devout examiner, understand our morning cry, so that our devotion in praying to you may be steadfast, your contemplation may be granted to us at dawn, and the desired forgiveness of all sins. Through our Lord.]

### Evening Prayers

May the dawn of righteousness arise as darkness is born, so that, having completed the day and giving you humble thanks, you may also graciously receive us in the morning when we pay our vows. Through.

[Col. 0854B] The day is yours, Lord, and the night is yours; grant that the sun of righteousness may remain in our hearts, to drive away the darkness of wicked thoughts. Through.

We give you thanks, Lord, guarded through the day; we render you thanks, to be guarded through the night. Present us, we ask, Lord, unharmed in the morning hours, so that you may have us as your praisers at all times. Through.

Almighty and everlasting God, at evening, morning, and midday we humbly beseech your majesty that, after the darkness of sins has been expelled from our hearts, you may bring us to the true light, which is Christ. Through the same Lord our God.

God, who illumine the night and make light after darkness, grant us to pass through this night without Satan’s hindrance, and, returning to your altar in the morning hours, to give thanks to you, God. Through the Lord.

As we fulfill the offices of evening praise, we humbly ask your clemency, Lord, so that, with your protection, we may overcome the deceits of the nighttime ambusher. Through the Lord.

Hear, O Lord, your servants as they offer evening vows to your name, and graciously guard through the repose of night those whom you have preserved through each moment of the day. Through [Christ].

[Be merciful, O Lord, to our evening supplications, and make us appear before you in the morning with no guilt, to offer you praise. Through [Christ].

We ask, O Lord our God, that you sustain the burdens of the day by the repose of night, so that, as the necessary succession of times follows, our weakness may be restored. Through the Lord.]

## CXLV. THE LAYING ON OF HANDS OVER A DEMON-POSSESSED CATECHUMEN

Almighty, everlasting God, before whose face the heavens distill, the mountains melt like wax, the earth trembles, the abysses lie open, whom hell fears, and before whom every movement of anger is humbled when it beholds you: I suppliantly beseech you, Lord, that, at the invocation of your name, the enemy, confounded, may depart from vexing this servant of yours, and that, once this soul has been freed from his possession, it may return to the author of its salvation and follow its liberator, the diabolical stench having been driven away and the sweetest fragrance of the Holy Spirit having been received. Through our Lord.

## CXLVI. ANOTHER PRAYER FOR A CHILD POSSESSED BY A DEMON

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, with every groan I implore your power on behalf of the oppressed childhood of this servant of yours. You who grant protection even to the unworthy amid their distress, rise up for this child who has been overcome in battle, and do not long delay your vengeance. Let not the sins of the parents come before your sight, since you have promised that neither father is to be judged for son, nor son for father. We ask you to assist one tormented by the fury of the enemy, lest you allow his soul to be possessed by the devil without baptism; rather, once this tender age has been freed from malignant oppression, let it return eternal thanks to you. Through.

## CXLVII. OVER A BAPTIZED PERSON POSSESSED BY A DEMON

God of angels, God of archangels, God of prophets, God of apostles, God of martyrs, God of virgins, God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ: I invoke your holy name and suppliantly entreat the mercy of your glorious majesty, that you may deign to grant me assistance against this most wicked spirit, so that, wherever he lies hidden, upon hearing your name he may quickly depart or withdraw.

For it is he who commands you, devil, who commanded the winds, the sea, and the storms. It is he who commands you, who ordered you to be plunged from the heights of heaven into the lower regions of the earth. It is he who commands you, who ordered you to turn back. Hear, then, and fear, Satan; defeated and prostrate, withdraw in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

You, therefore, most wicked Satan, enemy of the faith of the human race, plunderer of death, deserter from righteousness, root of evils, fuel of vices, deceiver of human beings, destroyer of nations, instigator of envy, source of greed, cause of discord, arouser of sorrows, master of demons—you who stand and resist, although you know that he is destroying your powers—fear him who was sacrificed in Isaac, sold in Joseph, slain in the lamb, crucified in the human being, and thereafter triumphant.

Withdraw in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and give place to the Holy Spirit, through this sign of the cross of Christ our Lord, who is to come to judge.

### Another

God, creator and defender of the human race, who formed the human being in your image and likeness, look upon this servant of yours, who is assailed by the deceits of the envious serpent, whom the ancient adversary and age-old enemy circles about with the horror of dark fear, fixing the human mind’s understanding with stupor, disturbing it with terror, and driving it on with the dread of trembling fear.

Repel, Lord, the power of the devil, and remove his deceitful snares; let the wicked tempter flee far away. Let the sign of your name be upon your servants, wholly in their soul and body. Guard the inner parts of this breast; rule the inward being; strengthen the hearts. Let the empty assaults of the hostile power vanish.

Grant grace at the invocation of your name, so that he who until now inspired terror may depart terrified and withdraw defeated, and so that this servant of yours may render you the service he owes with a strengthened heart and sincere mind. Through the Lord.

### Another

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, Hosanna in the highest, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who consigned that fugitive tyrant to Gehenna, who sent your Only-Begotten into this world to crush that roaring lion: attend swiftly; hasten to rescue the human being created in your image and likeness from ruin and from the noonday demon.

Give, Lord, your terror to the beast that destroyed your vineyard. Give your servants confidence to stand firmly against the most wicked dragon, lest he despise those who hope in you and say, as he once said long ago to Pharaoh: “I do not know God, nor do I release Israel.”

May your powerful right hand, Lord, compel him to depart from your servant, lest he dare any longer hold captive the human being whom you deigned to make in your image.

I adjure you, therefore, ancient serpent, by the judge of the living and the dead, by the maker of the world, by him who has power to cast into Gehenna, that you may hasten to depart, with fear and the host of your fury, from this servant of God, who resorts to the stalls of the Church. I adjure you not by my weakness but by the power of the Holy Spirit to cease [variant: depart] from this servant of God, N., whom almighty God made in his image.

Yield, yield—not to me but to the mysteries of Christ. For the power of him who, afflicting you, subjected you to his cross presses you hard. Tremble before his arm, who, having conquered the groanings of hell, led souls into the light.

Let the human body be terror to you; let the image of God be fear to you. Neither resist nor delay in departing from the human being, since it pleased Christ to dwell in a human being.

And do not suppose that I, whom you know to be a very great sinner, should be despised as weak. The Lord commands you; the majesty of Christ commands you; God the Father commands you; the Son and the Holy Spirit command you; the faith of the apostles commands you—the faith of Saint Peter and Paul and of the other apostles. The forgiveness of confessors commands you; the blood of martyrs commands you; the sacrament of the cross commands you; the power of the mysteries commands you.

Come out, transgressor; come out, deceiver, wholly filled with every deceit and trickery, enemy of truth, persecutor of the innocent. Give place, most stubborn one; give place, most impious one; give place to Christ, in whom you found nothing of your works, who stripped you, who destroyed your kingdom, who bound you when defeated and shattered your vessels, who cast you into the outer darkness, where destruction has been prepared for you and your ministers.

But what are you now considering, savage one? What are you reconsidering, reckless one? You are guilty before almighty God, whose decrees you have transgressed. You are guilty before his Son Jesus Christ, whom you dared to tempt and presumed to crucify. You are guilty before the human race, upon which death came through your persuasion.

I adjure you, therefore, most wicked dragon, in the name of the spotless Lamb who walked upon the asp and the basilisk, who trampled upon the lion and the dragon, to depart from the human being; depart from the Church of God.

Tremble and flee when the name of that Lord is invoked whom those below tremble before, to whom the powers of heaven, authorities, and dominions are subject, whom cherubim and seraphim praise with tireless voices.

The Word made flesh commands you; he who was born of a virgin commands you; Jesus the Nazarene commands you, who, when you despised his disciples, ordered you to depart from the human being unharmed and prostrate. When he was present, after he had separated you from the human being, you did not even dare to touch the herd of pigs.

Withdraw, then, now adjured in his name, from the human being whom he himself fashioned. It is hard for you to wish to resist Christ; it is hard for you to kick against the goad. For the longer you delay in coming out, the greater your punishment increases, because you are not despising a human being but him who is ruler of the living and the dead, who is to come to judge the living and the dead.

[Note: This was the end of the Sacramentary of Abbot Grimold in the principal Cologne manuscript. Nevertheless, since in the prologue of this book he also mentions the Prefaces that he placed at the end of this codex, and the Blessings to be spoken by the bishop over the people, as well as the material concerning the establishment of the lower orders in the Church that is not found in the codex of Blessed Gregory, it is clear that the codex is mutilated.

As for the Prefaces, since no manuscript contained them separately, we refer the reader to the Prefaces placed at the end of the first volume [in our edition the episcopal Blessings immediately follow], as also to the Roman Order concerning the lower orders.

Furthermore, we copied the episcopal Blessings—of which a fragment, written in another hand, was also found near the end of the principal Cologne codex—from a Utrecht manuscript and another Cologne manuscript containing the Order of episcopal functions. This Cologne codex supplied twenty-four Blessings for Sundays after the octave of Pentecost. We therefore placed them first, also because they appeared to correspond with the Sunday Gospels. After these we placed the eleven that alone were found in the Utrecht codex.]

[Col. 0857]

# EPISCOPAL BLESSINGS THROUGHOUT THE CYCLE OF THE YEAR

## JACOBUS PAMELIUS’S PREFATORY NOTE

[Col. 0857C] “The episcopal blessing,” says Radulphus of Tongeren, *De Canonibus*, final proposition, “was handed down by Bishop Martialis, a disciple of the apostles, from the teaching of the apostles; Ambrose began to recite it, and from that time the custom grew strong everywhere. The Apostolic [See], however, says only the blessing that is given when Mass has ended.”

In these few words, this most diligent investigator of the divine offices has indeed beautifully summarized the entire sequence of the matter. That this blessing was customary in the earliest centuries is confirmed by passages drawn from the writings of the Doctors Damasus, Ambrose, Jerome, Augustine, the Fathers of the Council of Carthage, Leo the Great, and the Council of Agde. These cited passages, as the *Micrologus* rightly interprets them in chapter 21, indicate that bishops once gave these blessings before Communion, as was also established by the Council of Toledo. We still see this observed by the Bishop of Paris when he celebrates the public sacrifice of the Mass.

Grimald testifies in the aforementioned prologue that he appended a collection of examples of these blessings for the cycle of the year. “We have also added,” he says, “the blessings to be spoken by the bishop over the people.” Therefore we have placed them after his Sacramentary, for the benefit of those among whom this rite of blessings still flourishes, although it had not been observed at Rome by the supreme pontiff since the age of Radulphus.

# BLESSINGS FOR ADVENT

[Col. 0857D]

Almighty God, whose Only-Begotten’s coming you believe to have occurred in the past and await in the future, may he sanctify you by the illumination of that same coming and enrich you with his blessing. Amen.

May he defend you from every adversity in the course of this present life and show himself merciful toward you at the judgment. Amen.

Thus, freed from every contagion of sins, may you await without fear the day of that dread examination. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and is glorified as God, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

May the blessing of God the Father + and of the Son + and of the Holy Spirit +, and the peace of the Lord, be always with you. Amen.

[Col. 0858D] Another.

May almighty God look upon you with a peaceful countenance and pour into you the gift of his blessing. Amen.

And may he who made these days solemn through the incarnation of his Only-Begotten render you unharmed by all the adversities of the present and future life. Amen.

And may you who rejoice with devoted mind at the coming of our Redeemer according to the flesh, when he comes a second time in his majesty, be enriched with the rewards of eternal life. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing of God the Father.

Another.

May God, whose incarnate coming is believed to have occurred in the past and whose coming in judgment is awaited, cleanse you from every stain of sin before he comes. Amen.

[Col. 0859A] May he first wash away in you everything that he is going to punish at that future examination, so that, when the just judge comes, he may find nothing in you to condemn. Amen.

When he comes, may you not incur eternal punishment, but be rewarded with everlasting gifts. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

Another.

May God, who restored you by the grace of his first coming and promised that at his second coming he would give you a kingdom with the holy angels, sanctify you by the illumination of his coming. Amen.

May he dissolve your bonds before he comes, so that, freed from the bonds of sins, you may await his dread coming without fear. Amen.

And may you who believe that he came on earth for your salvation and await him as the one who will come to judgment deserve, without fear, to behold the glory of his coming.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

# BLESSING FOR THE SUNDAY BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

Stir up your power, Lord, and come for the salvation of your people, whom you acquired with your blood, lest that savage enemy exult in the destruction of the one whom you long ago freed through grace by the power of your coming. Amen.

May the strength of your right hand be for the protection of this family of yours, for which you deigned at this time to put on virginal flesh. Amen.

Since your mercy does not disregard our weakness, may you protect this entire Church of yours with the shield of your divinity. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

# ON THE VIGIL OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD OR OF THE EPIPHANY

God, who deigned to raise up the fallen world through the humility of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may he make you capable of receiving his blessing. Amen.

May you lay aside the old Adam with his deeds and live according to the conduct of him who was created according to God in righteousness and the holiness of truth. Amen.

And may you deserve to receive sanctification from him today, so that, as you prepare to celebrate the Savior’s birth tomorrow, you may be found acceptable through fitting acts of service. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

# B. ON THE NIGHT OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD, AT THE FIRST COCKCROW

Almighty God, who drove away the world’s darkness through the incarnation of his Only-Begotten and illuminated this most sacred night through his glorious birth, may he drive away from you the darkness of vices and illuminate your hearts with the light of virtues. Amen.

And may he who willed the great joy of his most sacred birth to be announced by an angel to shepherds pour over you the most welcome shower of his blessing, and, with that shepherd himself as your guide, lead you to the eternal pastures of everlasting joys. Amen.

And may he who through his incarnation joined earthly things to heavenly things fill you with the nectar of eternal peace and good will and make you companions of the heavenly host. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

# B. ON THE NIGHT OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD, AT FIRST MORNING

Almighty God, who today enlightened the whole human race, blinded by the darkness of unbelief, through the visitation of the true light, may he illuminate you inwardly and outwardly with the blessing of his grace. Amen.

May you cast away the ragged works of darkness and, adorned with the bright garments of righteousness, walk becomingly: shod, that is, with the examples of the fathers; your loins girded with chastity; clothed with Christ; armed with the shield of faith; equipped with the sword of the Holy Spirit; adorned with the helmet of hope; and covered with the cloak of charity. Amen.

Thus, passing unharmed and unscathed through the ranks of your enemies in this attire, may you reach with rejoicing the kingdom of heaven, to your king whom the shepherds found as a little child in the manger. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

The blessing.

# B. ON THE DAY OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

May almighty God bless you and lift your attention toward heavenly things—he who made this most sacred day solemn through the birth of his Son. Amen.

[Col. 0860C] And may he who made the one who is the bread of angels become food for the faithful animals in the manger of the Church grant you both to taste the sweetness of eternal joys in the present age and, in the future, lead you to the fullness [variant: fellowship] of eternal rewards. Amen.

And may he who willed his infancy to be clothed in humble garments lead you into the adornment of heavenly garments. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, whose kingdom…

# B. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT STEPHEN

God, who crowned Blessed Stephen the protomartyr both with the confession of faith and with the struggle of martyrdom, may he surround your minds in the present age with the crown of righteousness and lead you in the future to the crown of glory. Amen.

Through his intercession may he grant you always to abound in love of God and neighbor, which Stephen strove to preserve even amid the attacks of those who stoned him. Amen.

Strengthened by his example and protected by his intercession, may you deserve to be blessed by him whom he himself saw standing at God’s right hand. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who with the Father…

# B. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT JOHN

May almighty God deign to bless you through the intercession of Blessed John the apostle and evangelist, through whom he willed to reveal to the Church the mysteries of his Word. Amen.

[Col. 0861A] May he grant you that what John, inspired by the gift of the Holy Spirit, poured into your ears, you may be able to grasp in your minds through the gift of that same Spirit. Amen.

Thus, taught by his testimony concerning the divinity of our Redeemer, and loving what he handed down, proclaiming what he taught, and carrying out what he commanded, may you deserve to attain the gifts that the same Lord Jesus Christ promised. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE FEAST OF THE INNOCENTS

Almighty God, on whose account the savage cruelty of deadly Herod slaughtered the hosts of innocent children for the venerable infancy of his Only-Begotten, may he grant you the most welcome gifts of his blessing. Amen.

And may he who granted them to confess his only Son, our Lord, not by speaking but by dying, grant you that the true faith which your tongue confesses may also be confessed by upright conduct and blameless life. Amen.

And may he who received them as the first-fruit of his holy Church make you reach the joys of the eternal homeland with the fruit of good works. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE SUNDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

May God, who sent his Only-Begotten to save the world, make you sharers in that salvation and cause you to persevere in it. Amen.

May he remove from you the anger that remains over unbelievers and make you forever free from it. Amen.

[Col. 0861C] May he bestow upon you the Spirit of his Son and grant that you may abound abundantly in his gifts. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE OCTAVE OF THE LORD

Almighty God, whose Only-Begotten today, so as not to abolish the law that he had come to fulfill, received bodily circumcision, may he cleanse your minds by spiritual circumcision from every incitement to vice and pour his blessing into you. Amen.

And may he who gave the law through Moses, in order to give blessing through our Mediator, strip you of the deadening of vices and make you persevere in the newness of virtues. Amen.

[Col. 0861D] Thus, may you live in this age in the perfection of the number six, and rest among the hosts of blessed spirits in the number seven, so that, renewed in the resurrection on the eighth day and enriched by the remission of the jubilee, you may reach joys that will endure without end.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE EPIPHANY

God, true light, who today willed to reveal his Only-Begotten to the nations, with a star as guide, may he deign to enrich you with his blessing. Amen.

Following the example of the Magi, may you offer mystical gifts to the Lord Jesus Christ; rejecting the ancient enemy and rejecting the contagions of vices, may you be able to return to the eternal homeland by the way of virtues. Amen.

[Col. 0862A] And may he who willed the Holy Spirit to be shown over his Only-Begotten in the form of a dove grant you true innocence of mind; and by that power through which water at Cana of Galilee was changed into wine, may your minds be trained to understand the mysteries of the divine law. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE OCTAVE OF THE EPIPHANY

We suppliantly beseech the God who is the author of wonders and virtues, that he who then disclosed himself as the light of the world through the light of a star, and to whom the Magi came through the radiance of the heavenly body to pray, may by forgiving grant that you may recognize him. Amen.

And may he who today deigned to descend as the fountain of living water to the spring of the Jordan, in order through the washing of his holy body to cleanse the waters themselves, mercifully purify you inwardly and outwardly from every crime. Amen.

And may he who again on this same day, when asked to a wedding feast at Cana of Galilee, changed cheap water into excellent wine, cause the lowliness of your mortal bodies to be swallowed up forever by the glory of the resurrection. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, and so forth, whose kingdom…

# B. ON THE FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

May God, who made the temporal childhood of his Son wondrous, deign to illuminate and instruct your hearts with the spirit of wisdom. Amen.

And may he who willed him to be subject to his parents for a time, in mercy shape you through the gifts of humility and devotion. Amen.

And may he who granted him to advance in wisdom, age, and grace mercifully bestow upon you growth in spiritual progress. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE SECOND SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

May God, who by his wondrous power changed water into wine, transfer you, withdrawn from oldness, into the newness of blessed life. Amen.

And may he who willed to be present at a wedding in order to affirm its goodness by his presence grant you the gift of perpetual chastity and sobriety. Amen.

May he who, by changing water into wine, willed to signify this very thing, grant you spiritual understanding of the holy Scriptures. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE THIRD SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

May almighty God cleanse you from the stains of every sin, he who deigned to cleanse the supplicant leper by his own touch. Amen.

And may he who did not disdain to visit the centurion’s servant mercifully deign to enter the dwelling of your hearts. Amen.

And may he so form you through the fullness of his faith that you may strive to recline with his saints in the kingdom of heaven. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

[Col. 0863A]

May the Lord remove from you the dangers of every temptation and, in mercy, exclude the storms of disturbances. Amen.

May he dissolve the deceits and schemes of the tempter and make you cautious and unconquerable against him. Amen.

May he grant you the gifts of continual peace and, in his favor, establish you in the harbor of tranquility and security. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

May God, who is accustomed to sow good seed in his Church, never cease to preserve and multiply it in you. Amen.

[Col. 0863B] May he drive far from you the sower of weeds and continually refresh you with the nourishment of his word. Amen.

Thus, when the day of judgment has come, may you be separated from the rejected, stationed at the judge’s right hand, and placed in his most blessed kingdom. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER THE EPIPHANY

May God, who made the sea passable beneath his feet, himself place beneath you whatever is harmful. Amen.

May he restrain the hostile movements of unclean spirits and strengthen you in his peace. Amen.

May he guide you in the ship of his cross amid the waves of the world and lead you to the shore of blessed eternity. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE PURIFICATION OF HOLY MARY

[Col. 0863C]

Almighty God, who today willed his Only-Begotten to be presented in the temple in the flesh he had assumed, may he, supporting you with the gift of his blessing, cause you to be adorned with good works. Amen.

And may he who, in order to fulfill the law, willed to become a minister of the law instruct your minds with the spiritual teachings of his law. Amen.

Thus, may you be able to offer him, in place of turtledoves, the gifts of chastity and charity; and, in place of young pigeons, may you abound in the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON SEPTUAGESIMA

May he who invites laborers to cultivate his vineyard in the morning, at the third, sixth, ninth, and eleventh hours make you fruitful in his Church. Amen.

[Col. 0863D] Thus, working among the first and not envying the last, may you receive the reward of your labors without murmuring or rebuke. Amen.
