So that, with those who took care to assist the least of Christ’s members, you may deserve to be blessed on the last day of the great judgment and introduced into eternal dwellings. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, whose power is confined neither by beginning nor by end, throughout ages of ages. Amen.

# B. ON SEXAGESIMA

May Christ, the giver of all good things, deign to sow good seed in your hearts and bring it to suitable maturity. Amen.

Thus, neither eaten by demons, nor dried out by hardness of heart, nor choked by thorns, may it be able to yield a hundredfold fruit. Amen.

So that, at the final crisis, when many will be handed over on account of their crime, like weeds to be burned by fire, the heavenly granaries may be opened for you as you carry the sheaves of your harvest. Amen.

May the most high Trinity deign to grant this; although ministry is furnished outwardly by any persons whatever, it alone can give growth inwardly, throughout ages of ages. Amen.

# B. ON QUINQUAGESIMA

God, unfailing light, who for our illumination willed to send into this world the light begotten from himself in the flesh, may he deign to open the eyes of your hearts. Amen.

Thus, following him, may you kindle others to the praise of God, and may you yourselves reach the eternal house of God in heaven. Amen.

Into that house, introduced through him as both door and doorkeeper, may you remain attentive to divine praises throughout ages of ages. Amen.

May we ask that this be accomplished by his condescension—he who foreknew and predestined before the age those whom he called and justified before the end of the age, and at the end of the age will glorify them throughout ages of ages. Amen.

# B. ON THE FIRST SUNDAY OF LENT

May almighty God bless you, who consecrated the number forty in the fast of Moses and Elijah, as well as in that of our Mediator; and may he grant that you so pass through the dispensation of the present life that, having received from the master of the household the denarius of reward, you may attain remission of all sins and the glorious resurrection with all the saints. Amen.

May he give you the unconquerable [variant: victorious] weapons of spiritual virtues, with which, following the Lord’s example, you may overcome the exceedingly crafty temptations of the ancient enemy. Amen.

Thus, receiving spiritual nourishment not from bread alone but from every word that proceeds from his mouth, through observance of fasts and the performance of other good works, may you deserve to receive the unfading crown of glory. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE SECOND SUNDAY OF LENT

May almighty God, author and lover of fasting and of the other virtues, sanctify you with his blessing. Amen.

May he kindle in you the affection of holy devotion and, in his kindness, grant a gracious hearing to those who supplicate. Amen.

Thus, may your minds, purified by sincere fasts, abound in increase of every good thing [variant: of good works]. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE THIRD SUNDAY OF LENT

[Col. 0865A]

May almighty God mercifully accept the sacrifices of your fasts and make you worthy of his blessing. Amen.

May he so fortify your minds against vices with the good of frugality, educate them through the teachings of his commandments, and fill them with the gift of charity, that he may grant you to please him in all things. Amen.

Thus, having celebrated the days of the present Lent with the utmost devotion, may you be able to approach the Paschal feasts with purified hearts. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE FOURTH SUNDAY OF LENT

May God, who has deigned to bring you to the midpoint of these present Lenten days, deign in his mercy to bless you. Amen.

May he accept your past abstinence and make your future abstinence so pleasing to him that, just as he grants you to abstain from unlawful foods, he may also grant you to abstain from every vice. Amen.

Thus, giving thanks to him for the fruits of spiritual gifts, both past and future, may you be able to reach holy Easter unharmed. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE FIFTH SUNDAY OF LENT

May the Lord kindle in you the power of his love and, through observance of fasts, pour into you the gift of his blessing. Amen.

May you offer him the sacrifices of frugality in such a way that you please him with the sacrifice of a contrite heart and humility. Amen.

Thus, may your prayer, borne upward on the wings of fasting and almsgiving, rise to the ears of your Creator in such a way that he makes you heirs of eternal blessedness and companions of the citizens above. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE SUNDAY OF INDULGENCE

May almighty God bless you, whom you strive to please both by the mortification of fasting and by the observance of the present days. Amen.

May he grant that, just as you have striven to be presented to him with palm branches and other foliage, so you may be able to appear before him after death with the palm of victory and the fruit of good works. Amen.

And may you who believe with pure heart in the passion of his Only-Begotten Son and strive to venerate it with devoted mind, strengthened by his protection, reach the feasts of the resurrection and the rewards of your recompense. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON THE LORD’S SUPPER

May almighty God bless you, who through the passion of his Only-Begotten willed the old Passover to be changed into the new, and may he grant that, once the contagion of the old leaven has been purged, the new dough may persevere in you. Amen.

And may you who have gathered with devoted mind to celebrate the supper of our Redeemer carry away with you the banquet of eternal foods. Amen.

And, with his mercy helping you, may you be cleansed from the filth of sins—he who, to impress upon you an example of humility, willed to wash the feet of his disciples. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. OF THE PASSION OF THE LORD

May almighty God, who through the passion of his Only-Begotten granted you an example of humility, grant you through that same humility to receive the ineffable gift of his blessing. Amen.

May you share in his resurrection, whose lessons of patience you venerate. Amen.

Thus, may you receive from him the gift of eternal life, through whose temporal death you believe that you escape eternal death. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON HOLY SATURDAY

[Col. 0866B]

May God, who, bringing forth new peoples from the undefiled womb of his Church, continually makes her fruitful with new offspring while her virginity remains intact, fill you with the gift of faith, hope, and charity and pour the gifts of his blessing upon you. Amen.

And may he who willed to illuminate this most sacred night through the resurrection of our Redeemer cause your minds, cleansed from the darkness of sins, to shine with an abundance of virtues. Amen.

Thus, may you strive to imitate the innocence of those who have just been reborn and illuminate the vessels of your minds by the example of the lights present, so that with the lamps of good works you may enter with the prudent virgins the bridal chamber of this bridegroom whose resurrection you celebrate. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# B. ON HOLY EASTER DAY

May almighty God bless you as the Paschal solemnity of today intervenes, and, in his mercy, deign to defend you from every wickedness. Amen.

And may he who restores you to eternal life through the resurrection of his Only-Begotten clothe you, at his coming, with the joys of immortality. Amen.

And may you who, having completed the days of fasting and of the Lord’s passion, celebrate the joys of the Paschal feast, come, with his help and exultant hearts, to those feasts that are not yearly but perpetual. Amen.

May he deign to grant this: he who, having conquered death, lives and is glorified as God, equal to the Father and the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

# B. ON THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

May God, whose Only-Begotten today deigned to appear to his disciples with the doors closed, enrich you with the gifts of his blessing and deign to open for you the doors of the heavenly kingdom. Amen.

May he who removed the wound of doubt from their breasts through the touch of his body grant that, through the faith by which you believe that he rose, you may be free from every stain of sin. Amen.

And may you who believe in him with Thomas as God and Lord and invoke him with bowed voices be protected by him from every evil in this age and be admitted among the assemblies of the saints in the age to come. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

# ANOTHER B. OF THE RESURRECTION OF THE LORD

May almighty God bless you, who created you through gratuitous mercy and, in the resurrection of his Only-Begotten, granted you hope of rising again. Amen.

May he raise you from the tombs of vices, who raised him from the dead. Amen.

Thus, may you live happily with him without end, whom you truly believe to have risen from the dead. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

### Another

May God, who through the resurrection of his Only-Begotten bestowed upon you both the good of redemption and the dignity of adoption, confer upon you the rewards of his blessing. Amen.

And since through the one who redeemed you you received the gift of perpetual freedom, may you, through his generosity, become sharers in the eternal inheritance. Amen.

And since you rose with him in baptism by believing, may you deserve to be joined to him in the heavenly region by living well. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

### Another

May God, who for you endured the injury of the cross, renew you with the joy of his resurrection. Amen.

And may he who forgave the crime of the thief hanging with him on the cross absolve you from all the bonds of sins. Amen.

Thus, through the mystery of your redemption, may you both conduct yourselves worthily in your works and enjoy more abundantly the eternal reward. Amen.

May he deign to grant this.

### Another

May God, who washed you with the water of his side and redeemed you by the shedding of his blood, himself confirm in you the grace of the redemption you have received. Amen.

Through him by whom you were reborn from water and the Holy Spirit, may he associate you with the heavenly kingdom. Amen.

And may he who gave you the beginnings of holy faith also grant the perfection of works and the fullness of charity. Amen.

May he do this, etc., whose …

Another.

May our Lord God lead you to the tree of life, he who rescued you from the pit of misery. Amen.

May he open for you the gate of paradise, he who shattered the gates of hell. Amen.

May he rescue you from the scourge and lead you, trusting in him, into his kingdom—he who, innocent, deigned to suffer for the ungodly. Amen.

May he do this, etc., who with the Father …

Another.

May you be filled with the blessings of almighty God and of our Lord, by whose precious blood you were redeemed. Amen.

May his unfailing grace fill you, whose ineffable power fashioned you. Amen.

May he who granted you the condition of being born in this world grant you in the eternal kingdom a dwelling in which to live without end. Amen.

May he do this, etc., who with the Father …

Another.

May God, who, trampling underfoot the laws of hell, deigned to recall our captivity to the rewards of freedom by loosening the structure of its chains, grant you to pass through this life in such a way that, with him as your guide, you may enter that perpetual life. Amen.

May he grant you such fervor of Catholic faith that you may await his holy coming without fear. Amen.

May all who here have merited purification by the water of baptism be able there to appear before the merciful Judge as candidates clothed in white. Amen.

[Col. 0868B] May he do this, etc.

## B. ON THE HOLY CROSS

May almighty God bless you from heaven, he who by the cross and the blood of his passion deigned to redeem you on earth. Amen.

May he renew you from the oldness of sin, he who deigned to be crucified for you; and may he raise you to heavenly things, he who for you entered the underworld. Amen.

May the Lord grant you his life, he who accepted and destroyed your death. Amen.

May he do this, etc., whose …

Another.

May almighty God bless you, he who through the passion of his Only-Begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, and the gibbet of the cross, redeemed the human race. Amen.

[Col. 0868C] And may he grant you, together with all the saints, to comprehend with devoted mind the length, breadth, height, and depth of that same cross. Amen.

So that, denying yourselves and bearing the cross, you may follow our Redeemer through the course of this present life in such a way that after death you may merit to be joined to him among the choirs of angels. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE DAY OF THE LORD’S ASCENSION

May almighty God bless you, whose Only-Begotten Son on this day entered the heights of heaven and opened for you the way of ascent to where he is. Amen.

And may he mercifully grant that, just as after his resurrection he appeared openly to his disciples, so, when he comes for judgment, he may appear to you reconciled. Amen.

And may you perceive that he whom you believe to be seated with the Father in his majesty remains with you, according to his promise, until the end of the age. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE VIGIL OF PENTECOST

May almighty God bless you, for whose Paraclete’s coming you prepare your minds by observing the fast and honor the present day with solemn praises. Amen.

May you possess the innocence of newly born infants to such a degree that, by his granting it, you may be temples of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

[Col. 0969A] And may that same Spirit of truth today make you worthy of his dwelling in such a way that tomorrow he may pour himself into your minds, intending to dwell with you forever; and, when the course of this present life has been completed, may he lead you to the heavenly kingdoms. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who with the Father and the Son, one God, lives and reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

Another.

May God the almighty Father, who, after Christ his Son had been exalted, poured out upon his disciples the Paraclete Spirit as he had promised, deign to purify and console you by that same Spirit. Amen.

May he, dwelling in you in this age, lead you in the future to the vision of himself. Amen.

[Col. 0969B] And may he render his own Son, whom the ungodly will see in the judgment in the form of a man, visible to you in his majesty after the judgment. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE HOLY DAY OF PENTECOST

May God, who on this day deigned to enlighten the minds of the disciples by the outpouring of the Paraclete Spirit, make you filled with his blessing and overflowing with the gifts of that same Spirit. Amen.

May that fire which appeared above the disciples cleanse away the filth of your sins and, by the outpouring of its light, illumine your hearts. Amen.

And may he who deigned to unite the diversity of languages in the confession of one faith make you persevere in that same faith and through it attain to the vision [variant: “by the vision of his majesty”]. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May God, who today restored the apostles, made almost orphans by the departure of Christ his Son, to consolation through the coming of the Holy Spirit, make you strangers to every evil, with that Spirit ever dwelling in you. Amen.

And may he who endowed them with the gift of all languages enrich you with the grace of every virtue. Amen.

May you, honoring God here with one mind and one voice, reach the heavenly kingdoms together with them. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

[Col. 0969D] May the Lord pour out upon you the spirit of grace and prayer, the spirit of knowledge and love of him, and of holy hope. Amen.

May the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and piety, rest upon you; and may he fill you with the spirit of fear of the Lord. Amen.

May the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwell in you, so that you may rejoice through participation in his immortality throughout the endless ages. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May God, who regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit, establish you in his kingdom. Amen.

[Col. 0870A] So that, instructed invisibly by that same Spirit, you may become his adopted sons. Amen.

And, withdrawing from the power of darkness, may you continue to shine in his presence. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

May the Lord deign to fill you with his charity, so that he may bestow upon you a blessed inheritance. Amen.

So that, escaping the torment of Gehenna through his chaste fear, you may joyfully reach the paradise above. Amen.

So that, having seen there the punishments of the wicked from which his grace rescued you, you may render him due thanksgiving forever. Amen.

May he do this.

## SECOND SUNDAY

[Col. 0870B]

May God the almighty Father, who called you to his supper, lead you to it as you humbly serve him. Amen.

So that, while the wretched are held fast by earthly things, you may reach heavenly things happy and unencumbered. Amen.

And may God find in none of you anything deserving expulsion, but only what merits blessed reward. Amen.

May he do this.

## THIRD SUNDAY

May almighty God, who sent his Only-Begotten Son after the straying sheep, lead you through him to the heavenly dwelling. Amen.

And meanwhile may he defend you from the ambushes of lions and wolves [Col. 0870C], until you ascend to secure pastures. Amen.

May there be joy over you in heaven because through faith you conquered the devil on earth. Amen.

May he do this.

## FOURTH SUNDAY

May the merciful God make you merciful, so that he may graciously extend mercy to you. Amen.

And may he teach you to judge in such a way that he ought not justly condemn you. Amen.

But, having been made imitators of Christ’s patience, may he establish you secure forever in the glory to come. Amen.

May he do this.

## FIFTH SUNDAY

May the Lord make you obedient to apostolic teaching [Col. 0870D], so that you may become heirs of eternal blessing. Amen.

And, freed through their prayers from the depths of this world, may you rejoice with them as possessors of the heavenly kingdom. Amen.

So that, when those who do evil fear the Judge’s punishment, the Lord’s eyes may caress you as you rejoice. Amen.

## SIXTH SUNDAY

May you preserve unharmed in the world the baptism that you received in Christ, through his grace. Amen.

So that, having died to sins in him, you may always walk in newness of life. Amen.

And, avoiding every rashness of mind, tongue, and deed [Col. 0871A], may the offering of your devotion be acceptable to God the Father. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## SEVENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord make you cleansed from every sin and sanctified. Amen.

So that you may bear such fruits as will enable you to please him. Amen.

And, nourished here with spiritual food, may you come without fear to the marriage feast of the Lamb. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who, remaining truth and life, deigned to become for you the way and the food; and whose dominion remains without end for ever and ever. Amen.

## EIGHTH SUNDAY

[Col. 0871B] May almighty God grant you to mortify the deeds of the flesh in such a way that you may become worthy to reign with him. Amen.

And, justified here by his Spirit, may you appear in the future as sons of God. Amen.

So that, while the false and evil are justly condemned, you may shine like the sun through the grace of God. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## NINTH SUNDAY

May the Lord restore you, emptied of every evil desire, immaculate. Amen.

And, freed from temptations, may he grant you to flourish in virtues. Amen.

So that through innocence of life and generosity in almsgiving you may enjoy blessed eternity. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## TENTH SUNDAY

[Col. 0871C]

May the Lord separate you from the blasphemers of Christ and enroll you among his faithful confessors. Amen.

So that, enriched with the manifold gift of the Holy Spirit, you may be found perfect in every good thing. Amen.

And may you not merit eternal expulsion from the house of God, but dwell in it for ever and ever. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## ELEVENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord, having justified you through Christ’s passion, render you glorified through his resurrection. Amen.

So that by his grace you may be made worthy from unworthy and great from insignificant. Amen.

Yet, while glorying in holiness, may you not despise or condemn those who still sin. Amen.

[Col. 0871D] May he do this, who …

## TWELFTH SUNDAY

May the Lord make you suitable ministers for himself, instructed by the gift of his Spirit.

So that, devoted to Christ in ear and mouth, you may become worthy heralds of him. Amen.

So that you may live in such a way that you also kindle others to the praise of God. Amen.

## THIRTEENTH SUNDAY

May he who grants you to be participants in the promise of the fathers make you their co-heirs. Amen.

So that you who lament having been expelled from paradise in Adam may rejoice at having been restored through Christ. Amen.

[Col. 0872A] And through imitation of him may you win others for eternal life. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## FOURTEENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord grant you to crush the desires of the flesh, so that you may walk by the Spirit. Amen.

May he cleanse you from the contagion of inward leprosy, so that you may become worthy of the fellowship of the saints.

And, giving thanks here to your cleanser, may you reach the heavenly Jerusalem rejoicing. Amen.

May he do this.

## FIFTEENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord grant you to overcome vainglory, so that you may attain true glory. Amen.

And, sowing righteousness here, may you reap eternal life in the future [Col. 0872B]. Amen.

And, serving your Creator devoutly, may you reign with him rejoicing. Amen.

## SIXTEENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord make you patient in tribulation, so that you may merit to become his companions. Amen.

And, with Christ dwelling in you here through faith, may you be able to enter to behold his glory. Amen.

And, separated from you the bearers of the dead, may you praise him with the holy angels. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## SEVENTEENTH SUNDAY

May the Lord make you walk in unity of spirit, so that you may merit to reign with him. Amen.

And, keeping the baptism, may you be presented joyfully to the Father who is above all [Col. 0872C]. Amen.

And, when the pretenders have been confounded with due shame, may you rejoice in eternal glory. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## SATURDAY WITH TWELVE READINGS

May God make you worthy of his priesthood, he who did not spare his only-begotten Son for you. Amen.

So that, persevering in holy conduct, you may also turn the erring back to him. Amen.

And may you become suitable intercessors for the barren and the bowed down. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## EIGHTEENTH SUNDAY

May God, who enriched you in speech and knowledge, preserve you [Col. 0872D] in an undefiled life. Amen.

So that at the coming of his Son you may be found blameless, having been cleansed by his blood. Amen.

And, while the ungodly are placed beneath his feet like a footstool, may you, exalted with him, sit beside him. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## NINETEENTH SUNDAY

May almighty God renew you, so that he may be pleased with us. Amen.

And, having laid aside every vice, may you shine in all virtues. Amen.

And, bearing here the burdens of your neighbors, may you come with them to heaven rejoicing. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## TWENTIETH SUNDAY

[Col. 0873A]

May almighty God grant you that, walking cautiously here, you may reach the kingdoms of heaven unharmed. Amen.

And, enriched by the pledge of the Holy Spirit, may you one day appear as the body of the Son of God. Amen.

Entering eternal marriage with him, may you enjoy the fellowship of the saints with joy. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## TWENTY-FIRST SUNDAY

May almighty God strengthen you for waging battle, etc.

So that, armed with the shield of faith, the helmet of hope, and the belt of charity, you may be able to please the highest Trinity. Amen.

And through the examples of your faith, may others also learn to conduct themselves honorably. Amen.

[Col. 0873B] May he do this, who …

## TWENTY-SECOND SUNDAY

May the author and initiator of all good things make you companions of blessed rewards. Amen.

And, increasing more and more in his knowledge, may he lead you without offense to the day of Christ. Amen.

Moreover, forgiving the account of all debts, may he mercifully make you equal to the faithful servants. Amen.

May he do this.

## TWENTY-THIRD SUNDAY

May the Lord make you imitators of the saints, so that he may deign to be pleased with you. Amen.

And, persevering here as friends of Christ’s cross, may you become participants in the heavenly kingdom. Amen.

So that, recognizing his image in you, he may grant you infinite joys [Col. 0873C]. Amen.

May he do this, who …

## TWENTY-FOURTH SUNDAY

May the Lord fill you with knowledge of his will, so that you may merit to be heirs of eternal life. Amen.

And, by the long endurance of your patience, may souls be rightly nourished for God. Amen.

Moreover, may those weakened by vices or dead through crimes be found saved and alive through the visitation or touch of your holiness. Amen.

[Note: [Col. 0873] From the Utrecht manuscript, eleven other Blessings for the Sundays after Pentecost.]

## B. FIRST SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord bless you through the address of our mouth and join your heart in the perpetual bond of sincere love. Amen.

[Col. 0873D] May you flourish in the abundance of present things acquired through righteousness and rejoice forever in the fruits of the most sincere charity. Amen.

May the Lord grant you enduring gifts, so that, after times have been happily extended, you may receive everlasting joys. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. SECOND SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord cleanse your consciences from every evil and fill you with perpetual sanctification. Amen.

May he mercifully attend to your vows and, reconciled to you, forgive all your sins. Amen.

[Col. 0874A] May he mercifully grant what you piously desire; and may the merciful defender drive far away what you fear. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. THIRD SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord remove from you the stains of every hostility and imbue you with the gifts of pure love. Amen.

May he subdue in you the resistance of flesh and blood and grant the aid of perpetual chastity. Amen.

And may he make you love in this present age what does not separate you from the inheritance of the heavenly paradise. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the grace of the Lord sanctify you and guard you from every evil. Amen.

[Col. 0874B] May he keep from you everything that is evil and purify your spirits and bodies. Amen.

May he bind you to himself with the bond of charity, and may his peace abound in your hearts. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May God, who is the life of mortals and the salvation of sinners, remove from you every stain of wrongdoing. Amen.

May he clothe you with the beauty of virtues, sanctify your minds, purify your wills, and grant you the fellowship of the holy angels. Amen.

So that, approved in faith and immaculate in deed, you may reach the eternal inheritance of heavenly joys. Amen.

[Col. 0874C] May he do this.

## B. SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord enrich you with his grace and multiply you through heavenly blessing. Amen.

May he defend you from every adversity and always guard you with merciful compassion. Amen.

May he, reconciled to you, attend to your petitions and mercifully grant you forgiveness for all your faults. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. SEVENTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord’s blessing accompany you everywhere and always make you adhere to him. Amen.

May he himself save you through his blessing, he who deigned powerfully to fashion you. Amen.

[Col. 0874D] And may he grant you to live happily in such a way that he makes you co-heirs of heavenly blessedness. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. EIGHTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May almighty God cleanse away the stains of your sins and illumine you with his blessing. Amen.

May he fill you with the gifts of spiritual virtues and make you persevere in your good resolve. Amen.

And may the gracious one accept your humility in such a way that he enriches you with the reward of his mercy. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. NINTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

[Col. 0875A]

May the grace of the Lord’s blessing always protect you and defend you from every evil. Amen.

May he cleanse you from every charge of sin and make you pleasing to himself forever. Amen.

And may the Lord, reconciled to you, meet you there and graciously grant you the aid of his blessing. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. TENTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May almighty God open your heart to his law and humble your souls to receive the heavenly commandments. Amen.

Whatever the mouth of our mortality tells you for the salvation of your souls, may divine mercy make acceptable to you. Amen.

[Col. 0875B] So that, encouraged by divine words, you may merit to reach eternal blessedness unharmed, together with those who keep watch over you. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ELEVENTH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST

May the Lord grant you the reward of the most sincere charity, so that you may always live in peace with everyone. Amen.

May you overcome the ambushes of all enemies and conduct the present life with complete sincerity. Amen.

May you already be free from the guilt of conscience, so that you fear nothing on the day of the judgment to come. Amen.

May he do this.

[Note: [Col. 0875] Up to this point the Utrecht manuscript contained the Sunday Blessings after Pentecost.]

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST

May almighty God bless you through the intercession of Blessed John the Baptist [Col. 0875C], whose nativity you celebrate today, and grant that you may experience the patronage of him whose solemn feast you honor. Amen.

By his favor may you be protected from every adversity and enjoy every good thing—he who, before he was born, recognized the coming of the world’s Redeemer, by his birth removed his mother’s barrenness, and by his birth released his father’s tongue. Amen.

So that you may be clothed in the wool of virtues and able to imitate the innocence of that Lamb whom he pointed out with his finger and by whose immolation you were redeemed, in such a way that you may be joined to him in the happiness of the eternal homeland. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF THE APOSTLES PETER AND PAUL

[Col. 0875D] May almighty God bless you, he who founded you upon the solidity of ecclesiastical faith through the most salutary confession of blessed Peter. Amen.

And may he protect with his most gracious defense those whom the most holy preaching of blessed Paul instructed. Amen.

So that Peter by the key, Paul by his word, and both by their intercession may strive to lead you into that homeland which they reached today—one by the cross, the other by the sword. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MARY

May God, who through the childbirth of blessed Mary the virgin deigned to redeem the human race [Col. 0876A], deign to enrich you with her blessing. Amen.

May you always and everywhere experience the patronage of her from whose undefiled womb you merited to receive the author of life. Amen.

And may you who have gathered today with devoted minds to celebrate her feast carry away with you gifts of spiritual joys and eternal rewards. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE MARTYRDOM OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST

May God, who grants you to frequent the solemn feast of Blessed John the Baptist, grant you also to celebrate it with devoted minds and to receive the gifts of his blessing. Amen.

[Col. 0876B] And may he who was confined in the darkness of prison for proclaiming his law free you, through his intercession, from the impulses of works of darkness. Amen.

And may he who did not hesitate to lose his head for the truth, which is God, through his intervention bring you to your head, who is Christ. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. IN COMMEMORATION OF ALL THE SAINTS

May the Lord, through the intercessions of holy Mary, God’s mother, of the blessed spirits, and of all his saints, rescue you from dangers and guilt, protect you, and set you free. Amen.

So that you may imitate more devoutly the faith and deeds of those whose solemn feasts you venerate, in order that you may merit eternally to attain the blessedness of their rewards. Amen.

[Col. 0876C] Since no one merits this through a worthy suffering, may he whose mercy is bounded by no end bestow it upon you through multiplied intercessors. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God, for ever and ever. Amen.

Another.

Through the intercession of the citizens above, may the Lord, ruler of the angels, guard you. Amen.

So that, fortified by their protection against spiritual and bodily adversaries, you may merit to be counted among the sons of God. Amen.

They reached the heavenly kingdoms through every kind of conflict, by his ineffable grace. Amen.

[Col. 0876D] May he do this.

Another.

May the author and rewarder of all good things grant you fellowship with his saints. Amen.

They either remained, well created, in his love or, having fallen through their own fault, rose again through his immeasurable mercy. Amen.

So that, by imitating the perfected worshipers of Christ, you may become co-heirs of heavenly virtues. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May almighty God continually drench you with the dew of his blessing [Col. 0877A] and enrich you with the most abundant gifts of his grace. Amen.

May he also make you always attentive to the teachings of all his saints and fixed upon their examples, and likewise keep you safe through their continual intercessions. Amen.

So that you who today celebrate on earth, with devout minds and annual solemnity, the feasts of those saints may merit to be inseparably joined with them in their everlasting fellowships in heaven. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May almighty God, who embraces all things together, mercifully direct the course of your life. Amen.

So that through observance of his commandments you may reach the stability of the blessed spirits [Col. 0877B]. Amen.

And may he who made his saints worthy of the kingdom of heaven through martyrdom make you, through poverty of spirit, their companions. Amen.

May he do this.

May God, who grants you to stand upon apostolic foundations, deign to bless you through the merits of his blessed apostle N.’s intercession. Amen.

And may he who willed you to be adorned and rewarded by their examples and teachings defend you from every adversity through apostolic protection. Amen.

So that through their intercession you may reach the inheritance of the eternal homeland, through whose teaching you preserve the integrity of faith. Amen.

[Col. 0877C] May he do this.

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF ONE MARTYR

So that you may merit to have fellowship with him in heaven, whose triumph you celebrate on earth with devout minds. Amen.

May he do this.

[Col. 0877D] May their glorious intercession commend you, whose death is precious in his sight. Amen.

So that, just as they obtained the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom through diverse kinds of torment, you may likewise merit their fellowship through the performance of good works. Amen.

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF ONE CONFESSOR

So that, instructed by his examples and protected by his intercession, you may be joined in the heavenly realm to him whose day of deposition you celebrate [Col. 0878A]. Amen.

May he do this.

May he make you happy through their suffrage, whose feast day you celebrate rejoicing. Amen.

So that, imitating their examples, you may be able to reach the heavenly promises. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF ONE VIRGIN

May the Lord bless you, who granted blessed virgin N. both the beauty of virginity and the glory of martyrdom [Col. 0878B]. Amen.

And, by whose aid she merited to overcome both the frailty of her sex and the fury of her persecutors, may you be able to overcome both the allurements of your bodies and the stratagems of the ancient enemy. Amen.

So that, just as she, though physically fragile, bravely undertook the contest and after the contest triumphed over her enemies, so you, living in this mortality, may be able both to conquer the ancient enemy and to reach the heavenly kingdoms. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE NATIVITY OF SEVERAL VIRGINS

May almighty God deign to bless you through the intercession of his holy virgins, he who willed to triumph over the ancient enemy not only through men but also through women [Col. 0878C]. Amen.

And may he who willed to grant them the hundredfold fruit through the beauty of virginity and the struggle of martyrdom deign both to cleanse you from the filth of vices and to adorn you with the lamps of virtues. Amen.

So that the lamps of your hearts may be filled with the oil of virtues in such a way that you may be able to enter with them the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom. Amen.

May he do this.

## B. ON THE HOLY TRINITY

May God, from whom all things exist, inspire you with righteous desires. Amen.

May God, through whom all things exist, make you enter through his commandments. Amen.

[Col. 0878D] May God, in whom all things exist, sanctify you by his protection. Amen.

May he deign to grant this, who, threefold and one, begins, completes, and preserves all good things, and rewards what has been preserved without end for ever and ever. Amen.

Another.

May God the Father, from whom all things are, bless you; may God the Son, through whom all things are, bless you; may God the Holy Spirit, in whom all things are, bless you. Amen.

May the triune and one God bless you with every heavenly blessing and make you holy and pure in his sight. Amen.

[Col. 0879A] May the riches of his glory abound in you, and may he instruct you in the word of truth, educate you through the Gospel of salvation, and enrich you with the charity of all the saints. Amen.

# BLESSINGS TO BE SAID ON ORDINARY DAYS

May the Lord bless you and keep you. Amen.

May he make his face shine upon you and have mercy on you. Amen.

May he turn his countenance toward you and give you peace. Amen.

Another.

May almighty God bless you in his mercy and pour into you the understanding of saving wisdom. Amen.

May he nourish you with the teachings of the Catholic faith and make you steadfast in holy works [Col. 0879B]. Amen.

May he turn your steps away from error and show you the way of peace and charity. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May the Lord incline his ear to the prayers of your humility and grant you the grace of his blessing and the reward of eternal salvation. Amen.

Another.

Another.

May almighty God surround you with heavenly protection [Col. 0880A] and enrich you with the gift of his blessing. Amen.

And may he grant that you who rely upon the hope of heavenly grace alone may also be fortified by heavenly protection. Amen.

So that in the present age you may receive the comforts of mortal life and be able to grasp everlasting joys. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May almighty God perpetually surround you with the aid of his right hand and fill you with the gift of his blessings. Amen.

May he defend you from every depravity and grant you to abound in heavenly gifts. Amen.

So that, cleansed in body and mind, you may offer him such service as enables you to attain his reconciliation [Col. 0880B]. Amen.

Another.

May almighty God purify the hidden places of your hearts and grant you increase through his blessing. Amen.

May you be stripped of all the dangers of the present life and clothed with the adornments of spiritual virtues. Amen.

So that, supported by his help, you may serve him on earth in such a way that you may be able to be joined to him in heaven. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May almighty God mercifully exclude every adversity from you and pour upon you the gifts of his blessing [Col. 0880C]. Amen.

May he make your hearts attentive to sacred teachings, so that they may be filled with everlasting benefits. Amen.

So that, understanding what must be done and doing what you understand, you may be found unharmed amid the adversities of the world and become co-heirs of the blessed spirits. Amen.

May he do this.

Another.

May almighty God order your days in his peace and grant you the gifts of his blessing. Amen.

May he free you from every disturbance and strengthen your minds in the tranquility of his peace. Amen.

## B. IN SYNOD

May the Lord make you cautious concerning sins committed either by you or by your brothers. Amen.

Another.

## B. AT THE ORDINATION OF A BISHOP

## B. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF A BISHOP

## B. FOR THOSE UNDERTAKING A JOURNEY

May the Lord direct your journey according to his good pleasure, and may he, most kindly, remain inseparably with you as your guardian. Amen.

May he provide you with the archangel Raphael as your guide, and, in his mercy, remove from you every harm and obstacle. Amen.

May he mercifully fulfill the devout petitions of your desires, so that you may happily merit both to obtain good things here and to reach eternal blessedness. Amen.

May he himself do this.

## B. AT THE DEDICATION OF A CHURCH

Almighty God, who has deigned on this day to gather you together for the dedication of this hall, may he himself deign to enrich you with heavenly blessing. Amen.

May he grant that you become his temple and the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, he who chose his only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, to be sacrificed for you. Amen.

So that, purified in mind and body, you may always have God, your indwelling inhabitant, within yourselves, and may be able to possess with the saints and elect the inheritance of eternal blessedness. Amen.

May he himself do this.

## B. AT THE DEDICATION OF A PROFANED CHURCH

May almighty God bless and preserve you, and illuminate this house by the presence of his holy gift; may he deign to open over it the eyes of his loving-kindness by day and by night. Amen.

May he mercifully grant that all of you who have devoutly assembled here for the dedication of this basilica, through the intercession of all the saints, may merit to receive here the forgiveness of your sins. Amen.

So that, by the grace of God, you yourselves may become the temple of the Holy Spirit, and may continually delight in dwelling in God himself. Amen.

May he himself do this.

## B. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE DEDICATION OF A CHURCH

Almighty God, who has deigned to gladden you by the annual dedication of this temple, may he himself deign to sanctify you with eternal blessing. Amen.

May he grant that, purified in mind and body, you become his own temple and the everlasting dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

So that, rejoicing in such an inhabitant and burning with the Holy Spirit, you may always desire heavenly things amid worldly dangers, and may be able one day to attain possession of them. Amen.

May he himself do this.

## B. FOR A THREE-DAY FAST

### On the first day

God, who works in his saints both the willing and the accomplishing, according to his good will, may by his mercy stir up your devotion to carry out the healing practice of salutary abstinence, and strengthen it by his blessing. Amen.

And may he who chastises every son whom he receives not allow you, amid the scourges that we deserve, to stumble through the fault of impatience; rather, may he cause you to flee to his loving-kindness through humble supplication. Amen.

And may he who, as Creator, recognizes the frailty of human mutability accommodate his aid to your good beginnings, so that, with him as your guide and instigator, you may accomplish what pertains to true salvation. Amen.

May he himself do this.

### On the second day

Almighty God, who determined to strike the offenses of the Ninevites in such a way that he preferred to have mercy upon the converted, may he, having enriched you with his blessing, make you worthily repent of what you have done wrongly, and grant the rewards that you devoutly desire. Amen.

May he grant to your humility that your bodies, embracing moderation, abstain from the delights of banquets, so that your minds, hungering and thirsting for righteousness, may fast from the enticements of vices that flatter wickedly. Amen.

May your hearts draw near with chaste fear and perfect love, so that you may escape the evils that the guilty must fear and attain the everlasting goods for which the blessed hope. Amen.

May he himself do this.

### On the third day

The merciful and compassionate Lord, the most kindly lover of human salvation, may by his blessing confirm you in goodness and bring your petitions to the perfection of eternal blessedness. Amen.

And may he so moderate the injuries of temporal afflictions, which he inflicts for your offenses as a necessary discipline ordered toward correction, that you may be able both to endure adversity with strength of spirit and to turn prosperity into thanksgiving without weakening of mind. Amen.

May he turn your mourning into spiritual joy, and grant you to believe in him, hope in him, and love him in such a way that he may beatify and crown you in perfection by the beauty of his sacred [read: *sacrae*] and eternal vision. Amen.

May he himself do this.

# ANCIENT PREFACES THROUGHOUT THE YEAR

## PAMELIUS’S NOTICE

Abbot Grimaldus writes that he also added these Prefaces to the Sacramentary. “We have placed these Prefaces,” he says, “at the end of this codex, so that they may be received and sung in charity by those who like them. But from those who understand them and nevertheless take no delight in them, and likewise from those who want them but nevertheless do not understand them, we ask that they neither be adopted nor sung.”

Nevertheless, in my judgment, most of these Prefaces are older than Grimaldus and even than Saint Gregory himself; indeed, many are Gelasian and Ambrosian. This belief was encouraged by the fact that I found some of them among the Ambrosian Prefaces, to such an extent that I am persuaded that only those enclosed in brackets are properly Grimaldus’s or Alcuin’s. I consider the others to belong to the group concerning which Pelagius II, the predecessor of Saint Gregory, writes to the bishops of Germany and Gaul, when he decreed that the daily Preface, with the others omitted, should be exchanged for only nine Prefaces according to the ancient Roman order: for Christmas, Epiphany, Easter, the Ascension, Pentecost, likewise for the Holy Trinity, the Apostles, the Holy Cross, and the Lenten fast. Later, as Radolphus testifies in the passage often cited, Urban II, at the council celebrated at Piacenza, added a tenth, concerning the Virgin, in the year 1095.

No one, however, should say that they must therefore be suppressed. Nothing prevents their being read privately out of devotion, provided that they are omitted in the public sacrifice of the Mass; and since their antiquity is established, they certainly affirm the Catholic faith against its adversaries in more than one place. We have marked the Ambrosian Prefaces, as we believe, and the Gelasian Prefaces with the letters A and G, and those which we have recently edited from manuscript codices with Ms.

# PREFACES FOR THE SEASONS

## ON THE VIGIL OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

**(Ambr.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, whose [mystery] today, etc., as may be seen among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

### In the middle of the night

**(Gelas.)** Through Christ our Lord, whose divine birth was brought forth by the greatness of your innate power. We proclaim him eternally begotten as Son, even before the eternal ages, since, as you possessed fully and perfectly the name of eternal Father, it was not lacking to you; and we confess him equal to you in honor, majesty, and power, together with the Holy Spirit, and in the threefold name we believe in one majesty. And therefore, with the angels ...

### At the dawn

**(A.)** Eternal God. Because of our Savior, etc., as may be seen among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

### On the holy day

**(G.)** Eternal God. Because through the mystery of the incarnate Word a new light of your splendor has shone upon the eyes of our minds, so that, while we visibly recognize God, through him we may be carried into love of invisible things. And therefore ...

### Another

**(Ms.)** Eternal God. We continually offer the sacrifice of your praise, whose figure righteous Abel established, which the legal lamb also displayed, which Abraham celebrated, which Melchizedek the priest presented, and which Christ, the true Lamb and eternal High Priest, fulfilled today by his birth.

## ON THE DAY OF SAINT STEPHEN

**(G.)** Eternal God. As we recall the birthday of blessed Stephen, both Levite and martyr, who set before us venerable examples of faith, of sacred service, of excellent stewardship and chastity, of preaching and wondrous steadfastness, of confession and patience. And therefore, rightly above all others, he follows the birth of your Son with the festival of his own passion, since the first martyr went to meet his eternal glory. And therefore ...

## ON THE DAY OF SAINT JOHN THE EVANGELIST

**(G.)** Eternal God. As we celebrate the venerable birthday of your blessed apostle and evangelist John, who, having accepted the call of the Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, rejected his earthly father so that he might find a heavenly one; having attained in the kingdom of heaven the seat of apostolic eminence, he who had despised the bodily nets of his father; and who was familiarly loved by your only-begotten Son and approved by gifts of immense grace, so that the same Lord, already placed upon the cross, appointed him as a substitute son for his virgin mother, in order that the virginity of this approved and beloved disciple might serve the integrity of the blessed mother.

For at the sacred banquet of the mystical supper he had reclined upon the eternal fountain of life, namely upon the Savior’s breast. Drawing from it the ever-flowing streams of heavenly teaching, he was imbued with such profound and mystical revelations that, rising above every creature, he contemplated with exalted mind and proclaimed with evangelical voice that: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word.” And therefore, etc.

## ON THE DAY OF THE HOLY INNOCENTS

Eternal God. And in the precious deaths of the little children whom wicked Herod slew with bestial cruelty because of the infancy of our Savior, we proclaim the immeasurable gifts of your mercy. In them grace alone shines forth more than will, and confession is clear before speech, and passion precedes limbs capable of suffering. For they are witnesses of Christ who had not yet become acquainted with him. O infinite goodness! O ineffable mercy, which does not permit those slaughtered for his name to perish without the merit of eternal glory, but reckons to them the crown of martyrdom. And therefore ...

## FIRST SUNDAY AFTER CHRISTMAS

**(G.)** Eternal God. And, with our hearts raised above, to adore the divine mystery: so that what is accomplished through God’s great gift may be celebrated with the Church’s great joys. For, with the ancient earthly order having ceased, human nature is wondrously restored and brought forth with a new and heavenly substance. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom ...

## THE OCTAVE OF THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

**(G.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. As we celebrate today the day of his circumcision and the eighth day of his birth, we venerate your wonders, Lord. For she who gave birth is both virgin and mother; he who was born is both infant and God. Rightly, therefore, the heavens spoke, the angels rejoiced, the shepherds were glad, the Magi were summoned, the kings were troubled, and the little children were crowned with glorious suffering. And therefore ...

## ON THE VIGIL OF THE EPIPHANY

**(G.)** Eternal God. And to praise you, the wondrous God, in all your works, through which you have revealed the most sacred mysteries of your kingdom. For the star, herald of the Lord’s manifestation, went before this festival; it announced to the increasingly astonished that the Lord of heaven had been born on earth, so that God, who was to be revealed to the world, might be proclaimed by a heavenly sign, and he who had been born in time might be disclosed through the service of temporal signs. And therefore ...

## ON THE EPIPHANY OF THE LORD

**(G.)** Eternal God. Because you have made your mercy known among the peoples and declared your salvation to all nations, choosing this day on which a star brighter than the other stars would lead Magi, aroused from distant regions, to adore the infancy of the true King, and would show by the ray of its light the Lord of heaven and earth, bodily born. And therefore ...

### Another

**(G.)** Eternal God. When your only-begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortality, he restored us through the new light of his immortality. And therefore ...

## ON THE FEAST OF THE PURIFICATION OF HOLY MARY

**(G.)** Eternal God. Because through the mystery of the incarnate Word a new [light of our mind], etc., as at the Nativity of the Lord.

## SECOND SUNDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

**(G.)** Eternal God. You who, in the indulgence of your loving-kindness, recalled to pardon and life the human being exiled from the bounds of salvation through the sin of his first parent, by sending us your only-begotten Son, our Lord and Savior.

## FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

Eternal God. Because when your only-begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortality, etc.

## SECOND SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And always to proclaim your powers and praises with lips of rejoicing, etc., as above among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

## THIRD SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to praise and bless you at all times, because in you we live, etc., as among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

## FOURTH SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

Eternal God. You who deigned to restore the human race, condemned by its transgression at the very root of its origin, acquitted through the flower of the virgin womb, so that through your Son, God and man, you might recreate the human being whom you had created as your only-begotten one. And the devil, who had overcome Adam in fragile flesh, was himself overcome by God taking flesh, while justice was preserved. Through whom majesty ...

## FIFTH SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

**(A.)** Eternal God. To offer you this sacrifice, which is salutary, etc., as among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

### Another

**(Ms.)** You who, through the sin of the first parent, recalled to pardon and life the human being exiled from the bounds of salvation, in the indulgence of your loving-kindness, by sending us your only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Savior.

## SIXTH SUNDAY AFTER THE THEOPHANY

**(G.)** Eternal God. To whose immense glory it belongs not only to assist mortals through your loving-kindness, but also to provide us with a remedy from our very mortality, and to save each of the lost from the very place where they perished. Through Christ.

## SUNDAY IN SEPTUAGESIMA

Eternal God. Because through the things that are seen we are instructed in the ways by which we ought to strive toward invisible things. Finally, as the year advances in its course, we are admonished to pass from past things to future things, from oldness to the newness of life, so that, freed from earthly supports, we may receive more desirably the abundance of the heavenly gift; and through that food which is bestowed by the benefits of another, may we reach the food that will endure without end, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through whom ...

## SUNDAY IN SEXAGESIMA

Eternal God. You who deign to instruct rational creation, lest, devoted to temporal goods, it fail to strive toward eternal rewards, by such an ordering that it neither grows faint under chastisement nor becomes insolent amid prosperity, but that its glorious devotion should rather consist in this: that, overwhelmed by no adversities, it may be overcome. Through Christ.

## SUNDAY IN QUINQUAGESIMA

Eternal God. And to entreat your majesty with bowed-down [that is, continual] devotion, so that, looking upon the measure of earthly frailty, you may not rebuke us in your anger for our perversity, but may purify, instruct, and console us through your boundless mercy. Since without you we can do nothing that is pleasing to you, your grace alone will grant us to live in a wholesome manner. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom ...

## TUESDAY AT THE BEGINNING OF THE FAST

**(G.)** Eternal God. You who through bodily fasting suppress vices, lift up the mind, and bestow virtue and rewards. Through Christ.

## THURSDAY

Eternal God. Since these feasts return, through which immortal exchange is provided for our mortality and eternity is substituted for temporal life; and through which sins are cleansed from the punishment of sin, and salvation is brought forth from destruction by wondrous means: so that the condition of human nature, which through the insolence of happiness came to sorrow, may return through mourning, humble and restrained, to eternal joys. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. And to beseech your majesty humbly, that in your kindness you may pour into us the spirit of understanding, by which we may either rationally discern what ought to be done ourselves or show those who think useless things what should be judged; and that we may not pursue our own ambitions, but submit to those who offer better things. For with you this is wisdom: it does not cling to its own vices, but loves truth wherever it is brought forth. Through Christ.

## SATURDAY

Eternal God. And to beseech your majesty humbly, that in your kindness you may make our mind pleasing to you: a mind that displays not merely the appearance of goodness, but shines, illumined by the fruits of righteousness; and, always devoted to your majesty, receives the benefits it desires. You who do not fail to accompany with necessary gifts those whom you have made suitably attentive to your worship. Through Christ.

## FIRST SUNDAY IN LENT

*[Note: Ambrosian; Tuesday of this week.]*

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. He who, continuing this fast for forty days and nights, consecrated it without hunger—for afterward he hungered, seeking not so much human food as salvation. Nor did he desire the banquets of worldly foods, but rather desired the holiness of souls. For his food is the redemption of peoples. His food is the affection of every good will. He taught us to labor not only for the food prepared from earthly provisions, but also for that which is received through reading the divine Scriptures. Through whom majesty ...

## MONDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. You who give food to all flesh and refresh us not only with bodily but also with spiritual foods, so that we may not live by bread alone, but may have life-giving nourishment in every word of yours, and may be fed not only by feasting but also by fasting. For just as bodies are fattened by food and drink, so souls are nourished by fasts and virtues. You have bestowed great healing of mind and body in this gift, because you consecrated the venerable fast for us, so that by fasting we may return more solemnly to the paradise from which we fell by not abstaining. Through Christ.

## TUESDAY

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, in whom the faith of those who fast is nourished, etc., as above on the First Sunday of Lent among the Ambrosian Prefaces.

## WEDNESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. You who commanded an abundance of crops to be produced as food for the human body, and placed in fasting for us the medicine of souls. Therefore we humbly invoke you: may our fast be acceptable to you, and, while fasting from foods, may you absolve us from sins. Through Christ.

## THURSDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Because religious fasts have been instituted for us suitably and beneficially, so that we may restrain the immoderate enticements of bodily pleasure; so that, once the insolence of earthly delight has been curbed, the appetite of faithful souls may become purer and calmer for contemplating heavenly mysteries. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. You who have taught us through the observance of fasting and the most pleasing generosity of almsgiving to obtain remedies for our sins. Therefore we implore your mercy: fortified by these observances and by the performance of other good works, may we do those things by which both hope and ability may be supplied to us for attaining eternal joys. Through Christ.

## SATURDAY

*[Note: Ambrosian; Thursday of the fifth week of Lent.]*

**(A.)** Eternal God, illuminator and redeemer of our souls, you who, after we were expelled from paradise through the first Adam’s violation of the law of abstinence, recalled us by the remedy of a stronger fast, through grace, to the blessedness of our ancient homeland, and taught us by loving instruction through which observances we might be freed from all sins. Through Christ. Through whom ...

## SECOND SUNDAY IN LENT

**(G.)** Eternal God. And to beseech your majesty humbly, that you pour into our minds the gift of healing observance; and you who never cease to bring assistance even to the negligent, grant greater benefits to the devout. Through Christ.

## MONDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to ask your loving-kindness with humble devotion, that, appeased by the offering of our fast, you may grant us forgiveness of sins and free us from harmful snares. Through Christ.

## TUESDAY

Eternal God. You who commanded bodies to be disciplined through the devotion of fasting for the healing of souls, grant, we ask, that our hearts may be able so to practice the commands of your loving-kindness that, with your help, we may merit to attain your promises. Through Christ.

## WEDNESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom you have brought about the reconciliation of the human race by a wondrous ordering; grant, we ask, that, purified by holy fasting, we may be subject to you with our whole heart and, amid the snares of worldly perversity, remain unharmed through your mercy. Through whom majesty ...

## THURSDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to entreat your loving-kindness, together with the celebration of fasting, with devout minds: may we, who are weighed down by the burden of evils as sins press upon us, be freed from all sins and serve you with a liberated mind. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. You who do not permit those who sin to perish, but exhort them to turn to you and live: therefore we ask your loving-kindness, that you suspend the vengeance of your severity against our sins and mercifully grant us the forgiveness we desire. May the mass of our iniquities not provoke you to vengeance, but may the observance of fasting and correction of conduct incline you to forgive our sins. Through Christ.

## SATURDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And continually to beseech your mercy, that you may grant our minds, which you see weighed down by earthly affections, to be relieved by healing fasts, so that from the affliction of our bodies there may arise for us strength of souls. Through Christ.

## THIRD SUNDAY IN LENT

Eternal God. And to beseech you humbly, that, together with bodily abstinence, our mind also may turn away from unlawful desires; and that what we renounce from bodily banquets because of earthly delight, we may cut away through the wicked intentions of the human will; so that by a fitting fast we may be made ready faithfully and beneficially to receive the holy of holies. We shall be all the more surely and continually confident that these things will be at hand for us, the more grateful we are for their instructions. Through Christ.

## MONDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to pray to your clemency with every supplication, that through this observance of fasts the affection of our devotion may increase; so that, with your help, we may always be drawn back from human excesses and, by your gift, may be able to cling to heavenly teachings. Through Christ.

## TUESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. You do not wish the souls of sinners to perish, but their sins; and you do not always immediately judge those who sin, but await those summoned to repentance. Turn away from us, we ask, the anger that we deserve, and pour over us the mercy that we desire, so that, purified by sacred fasting, we may merit to be enrolled in the company of your elect. Through Christ.

## WEDNESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to beseech your mercy humbly, that the sacred mysteries of our fasts may always be acceptable to your loving-kindness; and grant that those whose bodies are afflicted by the observance of abstinence may also have their minds adorned with virtues and heavenly disciplines. Through Christ.

## THURSDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to ask your immense clemency with humble prayer, that you may cause us, your servants, disciplined both by the mortification of fasting and instructed by the performance of other good works, to persevere unharmed in your commandments; and that, thus consoled by present aids, we may merit to reach eternal joys. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

*[Note: Ambrosian; Second Sunday of Lent.]*

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. He who, to disclose the mystery of his humanity, sat down weary beside the well; who asked the Samaritan woman to give him water to drink, he who had created in her the gift of faith; and who deigned to thirst for her faith in such a way that, while he asked her for water, he kindled in her the fire of divine love. Therefore we implore your immense clemency, that, despising the dark depth of vices, abandoning the harmful pitcher of desires, and thirsting always for you, who are the fountain of life and the source of goodness, we may please you through the observance of our fasts. Through whom ...

## SATURDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. You who consecrated the observance of the Lenten fast in Moses and Elijah, and adorned it in your only-begotten Son, the Lord of the law and prophets and of us all. Therefore we humbly ask your immense goodness that, aided by his most generous mercy, we may be able to fulfill what he completed through the unbroken continuation of constant fasts; and, fulfilling what he commanded, may merit to receive the gifts that he promised. Through whom ...

## FOURTH SUNDAY IN LENT

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to glorify you, Creator of all, for past fruits, and to beseech you humbly for future ones, so that, when we are not found ungrateful for what we have received, we may not be judged unworthy of what we are to receive; but, having so often offered the solemn fast, may we also gain, together with bodily assistance, progress of souls. Through Christ.

## MONDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. And to implore your mercy humbly, that the venerable exercise of salutary fasting may return us purified from the stains of our sins and bring us to the fellowship of the citizens above; and that here we may receive an increase of devout actions, and there obtain the reward of eternal blessedness. Through Christ.

## TUESDAY

Eternal God. Through the mediator of God and human beings, Jesus Christ our Lord, who, in the middle of the festival, ascended into the temple to teach—he who descended from heaven to free the world from the darkness of ignorance. His descent instructed the human race in saving doctrine; his death redeemed it from perpetual death; his ascent led it to the heavenly kingdoms. Through him we ask you, supreme Father, that, taught by his instruction and purified by devotion to salutary moderation, we may reach your promises securely. Through whom majesty ...

## WEDNESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. He who by the illumination of his faith drove away the world’s darkness and, through the mystery of his incarnation, restored the human race, which the womb of the first mother had brought forth blind, as illumined; and made children of adoption those who were held in the bonds of just condemnation. Through him we ask you that we may be found, in his most just examination, such as we were made in the most blessed rebirth of the saving bath; so that, imbued with the medicine of his incarnation, washed by the cleansing of the sacred bath, and adorned by devotion to moderation, we may reach eternal joys unharmed. Through whom majesty ...

## THURSDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Your goodness created the human being, your justice condemned him, and your mercy redeemed him. We humbly beseech you that, just as through unlawful desires we fell from the blessed region, so through abstinence we may return to our eternal homeland; and that our frailty may be so governed by your mercy that our mortality may be sustained by transient supports, while immortality may be acquired through the increase of good works. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who is eternal God, unfailing light, everlasting splendor. He commanded his followers here to walk in the light, so that they might escape the darkness of eternal night and happily reach the homeland of light. Through the humility of assumed humanity he wept for Lazarus; through the power of divinity he restored him to life. And he brought the human race, overwhelmed by the fourfold mass of sins, back to life. Through him we ask to be released through the observance of fasting from the bonds of our sins, restored to the blessedness of eternal life, and numbered among the assemblies of the saints.

## SATURDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God, giver of mercy and author of every goodness. You who through fasts, prayers, and almsgiving grant remedies for sins and increase every virtue. We pray to you with humble devotion: you who have given the most salutary teaching for doing these things, grant effectiveness for completing them without weariness, so that, obediently carrying out your commands, we may happily receive your promises. Through Christ.

## FIFTH SUNDAY IN THE PASSION OF THE LORD

*[Note: Ambrosian; Monday.]*

**(A.)** Eternal God. We implore your majesty with increasing earnestness so that, the nearer the day of the salutary festival approaches, the more devoutly we may advance toward celebrating its Paschal mystery worthily. Through Christ.

## MONDAY

**(G.)** Eternal God. We beseech you humbly that our fasts may be sanctified in such a way that forgiveness of all our sins may come to us; so that, as the passion of your only-begotten Son approaches, we may please you through the offering of good works. Through the same Christ.

## TUESDAY

Eternal God. And to beseech you with devout minds, that you may restore us inwardly and outwardly and cleanse us from the filth of sins by salutary moderation. Those whom you do not wish to be hindered by enticing pleasures, strengthen with the vigor of spiritual virtues; and so cherish us in transient things that you may grant us to cling to everlasting things. Through Christ.

## WEDNESDAY

Eternal God. And to beseech you with humble devotion that, through the fasts which we carry out according to sacred institutions, we may merit to be cleansed from all guilt; and that we may be able to receive your favor, as we prepare ourselves to celebrate the passion of your only-begotten Son. Through whom majesty ...

## THURSDAY

Eternal God. You grant us to offer fasting to you with such solemnity that we hope to receive the aid of your forgiveness. You instruct us to celebrate the Paschal feasts in such a way that through them we may acquire everlasting joys. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

**(G.)** Eternal God. Your mercy goes before us so that we may do good; it follows us so that we may not act in vain; it kindles the intention by which we burn to perform good works; it grants the effectiveness by which we may bring these things to completion. Therefore we beseech your unfailing clemency with tireless voices, that, cleansed from sins by the sacrifices of fasting, you may make us devout for celebrating the passion of your only-begotten Son, our Lord. Through whom majesty ...

## SATURDAY

**(G.)** Eternal God. Our faith arouses us, hope raises us, and charity unites us to you; your gratuitous mercy purifies those whom the guilt of conscience accuses. Therefore we entreat you with inward groaning, that, disciplined by restraining bodily nourishment, we may be found fit to celebrate the Paschal mystery. Through Christ. Through whom ...

## BEFORE THE SOLEMN RITES OF THE MASS, AMONG THE BLESSINGS OF THE BRANCHES

*[Note: Roman Order, p. 45.]*

It is right and salutary to praise and bless you, Lord, among the other commandments of your wondrous works: you who gave Lamech, the righteous seed, to Noah, to whom you revealed through the Spirit that he should know beforehand the coming waters of the Flood. The Church testifies that his ark was for our salvation; from it the dove, sent forth in flight, brought back a fruitful branch of the spiritual olive, and Noah joyfully received it when it returned to him.

From the anointing of that branch, elect Jacob set up a pillar, made a vow to the Lord, and poured oil upon it. [This is an indication of that branch flowing forth,] flowing from the heavens, the grace that fills its own vessels and those of the people. This is the grace that also blessed the widow in oil; this is an indication of that branch planted beside streams of water, whose leaf does not fall away, through which each day the Church is brought forth by the bath of baptism and our sins are wiped away.

This is your planting, Lord, very good indeed; and you are the life and resurrection of the dead, who raised the four-day-old Lazarus from the dead. Therefore the crowd also came to meet you with palm branches, crying out: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel.”

Therefore we ask, Lord, that your mercy may rescue us, your servants, who have received the grace and faith of this event, from the mouth of hell; and that you may deign to grant us the help of your grace, so that, living justly, devoutly, and holily, you may cause us to share fellowship with your elect and saints. Through the same one.

## PALM SUNDAY

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom forgiveness is bestowed upon us and peace is proclaimed throughout every age; instruction is handed down to all believers, so that the coming day may receive us as sanctified. And therefore, with the angels ...

## MONDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. His humanity gathers us, his humility raises us, his betrayal absolves us, his punishment redeems us, his cross saves us, his blood cleanses us, and his flesh nourishes us. Through him we beseech you, supreme Father, together with the observance of fasting, that we may approach with purified minds to celebrate his passion. Through whom ...

## TUESDAY

**(A.)** Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. The days of his saving passion and glorious resurrection are known to be approaching; in them the pride of the ancient enemy is triumphed over and the mystery of our redemption is celebrated. Therefore we ask your immense clemency: just as the whole sum of our salvation rests in him alone, so through him may the sacrifice of our fasts and actions always be pleasing to you. Through whom ...

## WEDNESDAY
(A.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who, innocent, willed to suffer for the ungodly and to be unjustly condemned for the guilty. His death turned aside our sins, and his resurrection granted us justification. Through him we humbly beseech your goodness: cleanse us today from our sins, so that tomorrow you may satisfy us with the food of the venerable flesh; today accept the confession of our sins, and tomorrow grant the increase of spiritual gifts; today receive the vows of our fasts, and tomorrow lead us into the feast of the most sacred flesh. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

## HOLY THURSDAY, THE LORD’S SUPPER

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, whom on this night, amid the sacred feast, the conscience of the betrayer could not endure when he rebuked him. But, abandoning the company of the apostles, he accepted from the Jews the price of blood, so that he might lose the life which he had sold. Therefore today the betrayer supped his own death, and, soon to depart with bloodstained hands, accepted bread from the hand of the Savior, so that a greater punishment might bind him when he had been fattened by food—a man whom not even the sharing of the consecrated food could recall from his crime. Thus our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, suffers with the enemy at the final meal, although he knew that he was immediately to be betrayed by him, so that he might leave the world an example of innocence and complete his passion for the redemption of the world. Thus the gentle God feeds the harsh Judas, and the merciful one tolerates his cruel table-companion. He deservedly was to perish by his own noose, because he had planned the blood of his master. O Lord, patient in all things! O lamb, gentle amid his own feast! Judas bore his [i.e. Christ’s] food in his mouth while summoning those who would hand him over to his persecutors. But your Son, our Lord, like a devout victim, patiently committed himself to you for us [the printed *immorali* is uncertain], and forgave the sin which the world had committed. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

### Within the Canon

“Communicating together and celebrating the most sacred day on which our Lord Jesus Christ was betrayed, and also venerating the memory …”

“Therefore this offering of our service, and also of your entire household, which we offer to you on the day on which our Lord Jesus Christ gave his disciples the mysteries of his body and blood to celebrate: we ask, Lord, that you graciously accept it.”

“Who, on the day before he was to suffer for the salvation of us all—that is, today—took bread into his holy and venerable hands.”

## HOLY SATURDAY

(G.) It is right and salutary indeed, Lord, to proclaim you gloriously at all times, but especially on this night, when Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed; for he is the true lamb who took away the sins of the world. By dying he destroyed our death, and by rising he restored life. And therefore …

### Another

Eternal God. And to praise and proclaim you with greater glory at all times, but especially on this night, through Christ our Lord. When he broke open the prison-bars of hell, he took up the bright standards of his victory and, having triumphed over the devil, rose from the dead. [Later addition: victor a.] O night, which puts an end to darkness and opens the way of eternal light! O night, which was worthy to see the devil conquered and Christ rise again! O night, in which the depths of hell are despoiled, the saints are freed from the underworld, and the entrance to the heavenly homeland is opened! O night, in which the multitude of sins is destroyed in baptism and the children of light are born.
