As an image of the Lord’s mother Mary, holy Mother Church conceives them without corruption, gives birth without pain, and advances them joyfully toward better things. And therefore …

### Within the Canon

(G.) “Communicating together and celebrating the most sacred night of the resurrection according to the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and also venerating especially the memory of the glorious ever-virgin Mary, mother of the same God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and also of the blessed apostles …”

(G.) “Therefore this offering of our service, and also of your entire household, which we offer to you also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them the forgiveness of all sins: we ask, Lord, that you graciously accept …”

## ON HOLY EASTER DAY

(G.) It is right and salutary indeed, Lord, to proclaim you at all times, but especially on this day, as above.

### Another

Eternal God. And to praise, bless, and proclaim you at all times, but especially on this day, on which Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed. Through him the children of light are born to eternal life, the courts of the heavenly kingdom are opened to the faithful, and, through the blessed exchange, human things are changed into divine. For the death of us all was destroyed by Christ’s cross, and in his resurrection the life of all rose again. In the assumption of mortality we acknowledge the God of majesty, and in the glory of divinity we confess God and man. By dying he destroyed our death, and by rising he restored life. And therefore, with the angels …

### Within the Canon

(G.) “Communicating together and celebrating the most sacred day of the resurrection according to the flesh of our Lord and God, and also venerating the memory …” Therefore this offering, as above.

## MONDAY

Indeed, at all times, as above.

### Another

(A.) Eternal God. And humbly to beseech you that you graciously grant your faithful, etc., as above. On the following Saturday, among the Ambrosian prayers.

## TUESDAY AT SAINT PAUL

(A.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who by the offering of his body, etc., as above, Thursday in the Ambrosian prayers.

## WEDNESDAY AT SAINT LAWRENCE

(G.) Eternal God. And to implore your goodness with unwearied prayers, so that we who celebrate the solemn rites of the paschal feast may always live in your sanctification. By observing the temporal feast, may we deserve to attain the continuation of eternal joys. Through Christ.

## THURSDAY AT THE HOLY APOSTLES

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who through the paschal mystery taught us to leave behind the old way of life and walk in newness of spirit. Through him the bitterness of perpetual death is overcome, and the integrity of eternal life is granted to the faithful. Through whom …

## FRIDAY AT SAINT MARK

(A.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who, according to the unchanging character of his promise, etc., as can be seen among the Ambrosian prayers.

## SATURDAY AT SAINT JOHN

(A.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. Through whom we humbly ask that, of whose gift, etc., as above, Friday among the Ambrosian prayers.

## THE SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

(A.) Eternal God. Humbly beseeching you not to allow us to return to that former conduct, etc., as can be seen among the Ambrosian prayers.

## IN THE ANNOTATED EASTER TEXT

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. And to recall the feasts of our redemption, in which, freed from the bonds of transgression, human nature assumed the hope of resurrection through the renewal of its original dignity. And therefore …

## FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

(G.) Eternal God. And humbly to beseech the immense goodness of your compassion, so that, considering the ignorance of our mortality, you may make us ask, through your inspiration, for what is right, and by your mercy grant us to obtain what we ask. Through Christ. Through whom …

## SECOND SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF EASTER

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who deigned to be born of a Virgin, freed us from perpetual death through his passion and death, and bestowed eternal life upon us through his resurrection. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

## THIRD SUNDAY

(A.) Eternal God. And to ask for the mercy of your gift, so that we may treat with devout devotion, with his help, the time during which our Lord Jesus Christ dwelt bodily with his disciples after his resurrection, in such a way that during it we may remain free from the filth of every vice. Through the same one. Through whom …

## FOURTH SUNDAY

(A.) Eternal God. And to implore your majesty with unwearied prayers, etc., as above, the fifth Sunday among the Ambrosian prayers.

## MONDAY OF THE ROGATION DAYS

(Manuscript.) Eternal God. And to praise you as the author and sanctifier of fasting, through which you free us from the debts of our sins. Therefore receive the prayers of those who fast; and, so that in your mercy you may rescue us from every evil, graciously absolve our iniquities, by which we are deservedly afflicted.

## TUESDAY OF THE ROGATION DAYS

Eternal God. And humbly to beseech your majesty, so that the inclination of your indulgence may always precede us, not the inclination of our wickedness; may it unceasingly free us from harmful pleasures and graciously rescue us from worldly disasters. Through Christ.

## WEDNESDAY OF THE ROGATION DAYS

(Manuscript.) Since it is your work whenever we think or do anything pleasing to you, grant us always the ability both to understand what is right and to carry it out.

## ON THE VIGIL OF THE ASCENSION

(A.) Eternal God. And especially on this day, on which Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, having completed the divine mystery, fulfilled the charge of the ancient disposition: both to strike down, through the human being whom he had subjected, the devil, the enemy of the heavenly work, and to restore human nature to heavenly gifts. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

## ON THE HOLY DAY OF THE ASCENSION

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who, after his resurrection, appeared openly to all his disciples and, while they watched, was raised into heaven, so that he might grant us to share in his divinity. And therefore …

### Within the Canon

(G.) “Communicating together and celebrating the most sacred day on which your only-begotten Son, our Lord, placed at the right hand of your glory the substance of our weakness united to himself, and also remembering especially the glorious …”

## THE SUNDAY AFTER THE ASCENSION

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who by being born came to the aid of the human race—[read: *qui*]—by the death of his passion conquered the world, by the glory of his resurrection opened the way to eternal life, and by his ascension into heaven gave us the hope of ascending. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

## ON THE VIGIL OF PENTECOST

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who, ascending above all the heavens and sitting at your right hand, poured out today the promised Holy Spirit upon the children of adoption. Therefore the whole world rejoices with overflowing gladness throughout the earth. And the heavenly powers and angelic authorities sing together a hymn to your glory, saying without end: Holy, etc.

### Another

Eternal God. Having completed the paschal sacrament, you grant the gifts of grace through the Holy Spirit to those whom, through communion with your Only-Begotten, you have made children of adoption. You now bestow upon the fellow-heirs of the Redeemer the pledge of their heavenly inheritance, so that they may trust all the more certainly that they will come to him, the more they know themselves to have been redeemed by him and enriched by the infusion of that same Holy Spirit. And therefore …

### Within the Canon

(G.) “Communicating together and anticipating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit filled the apostles and the people of believers with the presence of his majesty. And also remembering …”

“Therefore this offering of our service, and also of your entire household, which we offer to you also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them the forgiveness of all sins: we ask, Lord, that you graciously accept it.”

## ON THE HOLY DAY OF PENTECOST

(G.) He who, ascending above all the heavens, etc., as above.

### Within the Canon

(G.) “Communicating together and celebrating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit appeared to the apostles in countless languages. And also remembering …” Therefore this offering, as above.

## MONDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who sent the promised Paraclete Spirit upon the disciples. At the beginning of the Church’s birth, he both implanted knowledge of divinity for the instruction of all nations and joined the diversity of languages in the confession of one faith. Through him we humbly beseech your majesty: may we receive the effect of the manifold grace of the one whose coming we celebrate. Through whom …

## TUESDAY

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who filled the hearts of the faithful with the infusion of the promised Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, so that by his marvelous operation he might kindle in them the fire of his love and establish the nations in the unity of faith through the diversity of languages. By his gift we ask that seductive pleasures be excluded from us and that spiritual virtues be built and planted within us. Through whom [we ask] your majesty.

## WEDNESDAY

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. Through him the Holy Spirit is given to the disciples on earth because of love of neighbor and sent from heaven because of love of you. We ask that his infusion burn away the filth of sins within us, nourish the fire of your love, and kindle us to the love of brotherhood. Through …

## THURSDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly ask your goodness that the Holy Spirit may mercifully cleanse our hearts and illuminate them with the radiance of his light, so that in him who is the giver of graces we may think rightly and rejoice forever in his consolation. Through whom …

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. And humbly to beseech your majesty that the Paraclete Spirit may come to us and, dwelling within us, make us a temple of his majesty. May you always deign to regard this temple with merciful attention together with your only-begotten Son, and illuminate it forever with the splendor of your indwelling. Through whom …

## SATURDAY

Eternal God. And to implore your omnipotence with devoted prayers, that you may pour into us the light of your Spirit, whose wisdom creates us, whose spirit renews us, and whose providence governs us. Although he is in no way different in substance from you, nevertheless by the diversity of his gifts he has filled the hearts of the faithful. And therefore …

## ON THE HOLY TRINITY

(G.) Eternal God. You are one God with your only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit; you are one Lord—not in the singularity of one person, but in the Trinity of one substance. For what we believe concerning your glory, as you reveal it, that we also understand concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit, without distinction of difference, so that in the confession of true and everlasting divinity there may be adored in the persons their distinctiveness, in the essence unity, and in the majesty equality. You are praised by angels and archangels, and also by cherubim and seraphim, who do not cease to cry out, saying with one voice …

## IN THE QUATUOR TEMPORA FAST OF PENTECOST—WEDNESDAY

Eternal God. Since, after those days of joy which we spent in honor of the Lord rising from the dead and ascending into heaven, and after we had received the gift of the Holy Spirit, holy fasts necessary for us have been provided, so that what has been divinely bestowed upon the Church may remain in those who live in pure conduct. Through Christ.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. Humbly and earnestly beseeching your majesty to make us good by a saving means, so that we may believe you to be the principal and only author, and the only Savior. You are praised by angels, adored by archangels, and also by cherubim, etc.

## SATURDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Seeking your goodness with every vow, so that, having received prosperity in human affairs, we may rejoice in earthly consolations. May we never cease seeking heavenly joys; rather, whatever joy is expended in temporal things may contribute to everlasting instruction. Through Christ our Lord.

## FIRST SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

(G.) Eternal God. It is your work that we have been created, your gift that we live, and your goodness that we recognize your gifts toward us. Although our nature has been wounded and corrupted by sin, nevertheless, by your indescribable gift, we are raised from earthly things to heavenly things. Through Christ our Lord.

## SECOND SUNDAY AFTER THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

(A.) Eternal God. Just as you never cease to instruct the children of your Church, so you never cease to assist them, so that, by your mercy, they may receive both the knowledge of doing what is right and the ability to carry it out. Through Christ. Through whom …

## THIRD SUNDAY

Eternal God. It was your wondrous and singular work and mystery that we, long lost and cast down, should be called from the devil and the sting of death to this glory, in which we are now called a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a people of possession, and a holy nation. Therefore, giving unceasing thanks and proclaiming your holy generosity, we bring these sacred offerings before your majesty—offerings which Christ himself, the author of our salvation, instituted for us. Through whom …

## FOURTH SUNDAY

Eternal God, we beseech your clemency with bowed minds, that you may order our minds and perceptions. For then, Lord, we shall perceive you to be favorable toward us if we refrain from harmful excesses; then we trust that we shall receive your benefits if you infuse within us a zeal for truth by which we may deserve them. Through Christ.

## FIFTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. And continually to implore your omnipotence, that you may grant us both support in the present life and the everlasting reward of eternal life, so that here we may receive mutable goods and through them be able to attain unchanging gifts. May the times of temporal joy pass away in such a manner that everlasting joys may follow them. Through Christ.

## SIXTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Humbly beseeching your majesty, that you may graciously bestow your help upon those who ask for it, and kindly grant what will benefit those who desire it. Through Christ.

## SEVENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, the true and eternal high priest and the only priest without the stain of sin, whose blood cleanses the hearts of the faithful; by whose institution we sacrifice to you offerings of appeasement, not only for the sins of the people but also for our own offenses. We ask your clemency: may every sin which we have contracted through the weakness of the flesh be absolved, with that supreme bishop intervening for us. Through whom …

## EIGHTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. And to vow to you, in contrition, the sacrifice of the heart; to pour out to you, in humility, the offering of the breast—from you we receive every good and draw every joy. Therefore we pray that our conscience may serve you and that, improved day by day in you, it may advance and submit itself undefiled to your grace. We ask, Lord, empty us of our evils and fill us entirely with your goods. Having received grace, which our merits do not demand, may we, freed from every adversity and established in every good thing, deserve to be joined to the citizens above. Through Christ.

## NINTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. And to implore your mercy with all our strength: do not condemn us for our iniquity, but by your goodness always direct us on the right path. Do not be angry with us sinners as we deserve, but assist our weakness with unconquerable goodness. Through Christ. Through whom …

## TENTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. And to implore your mercy, so that, with your assent, we may be able to avoid what is evil and consequently accomplish what is good. And since you have made us belong to your sacraments, mercifully work their gift within us. Through Christ.

## ELEVENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. And to render you the service owed through the fulfillment of this mystery, because you grant forgiveness not only to sinners but also bestow rewards upon those who ask for them. What we deserve through evil works you drive away by magnificent goodness, so that you compel us to worship your reverence both through fear and lead us to it through love. Through Christ.

## TWELFTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. The first sign of your goodness is that you make us subject to you with our whole heart and infuse into us a spirit of such devotion that, in your favor, you may consequently grant us help. Through Christ.

## THIRTEENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. By chastising us you heal us, and by restoring us you kindly instruct us, since you prefer us to be saved when corrected rather than perish when cast down. Through Christ. Through whom …

## FOURTEENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Since, by always making power present in our weakness, you have granted your Church to grow amid adversity, so that when it was thought to be oppressed, it might then prevail all the more once exalted; while affliction at once reveals the experience of faith and devotion, with your help, always perseveres most victoriously. Through Christ our Lord.

## FIFTEENTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. You raise us from the gifts of temporal goods to the reception of eternal ones; you grant the former and bestow the latter, so that we may already begin to be joined to what endures and not be held by what passes away. For it is by your doing that we live, since, although our nature has been corrupted by the wound of sin, it is nevertheless your work that, having been generated as earthly beings, we are reborn as heavenly ones. Through Christ.

## SIXTEENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who by the eternity of his priesthood sanctifies as priests all who serve him. Since we are surrounded by mortal flesh, we need the daily remission of sins in such a way that the blood of that same High Priest may intercede with you not only for the people but also for us. Through whom …

## SEVENTEENTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. And to pray to you without ceasing, so that, since we subsist by your authorship, we may be directed by your governance. Do not leave us to our own senses, but, always brought back to the path of your truth, may we strive to practice what you command, so that we may receive the gifts which you promise. Through Christ.

## SEPTEMBER EMBER WEDNESDAY AT SAINT MARY

Eternal God. You have wished us to give thanks to you through abstinence from the collected fruits of the earth, so that from this very form of devotion we might understand that we have received these things not for bodily abundance but for the support of weakness; so that what we consume more sparingly from them may benefit as food for the needy; and so that the salutary discipline of mortality may moderate insolence, while the goodness of the giver may commend us to your kindness. Thus may we use transitory gifts in such a way that we learn to yearn for perpetual ones. Through Christ.

## SEPTEMBER EMBER FRIDAY, AT THE HOLY APOSTLES

Eternal God. With just and devout moderation you both impose scourges for sins and, once appeased after the scourges, grant forgiveness. Desiring the life of sinners rather than their death, you do not condemn them to destruction but mercifully wait for them to be corrected. Through Christ.

## SATURDAY AT SAINT PETER

Eternal God. And to sanctify for you the fast which you taught us to keep for the building up of souls and the chastisement of bodies. When bodies are restrained, souls are nourished; while our outward person is afflicted, the inward person is enlarged. Remember, we ask, Lord, our fasts and your mercies, which you have always piously bestowed upon sinners who fast; and grant that, abstaining not only from food but from every sin, we may please you by the fast of devotion. Through Christ.

## EIGHTEENTH SUNDAY

Eternal God. Although you do not need our praise, the devotion of your servants is nevertheless pleasing to you. Our proclamations do not increase you, but they advance us toward salvation. For just as passing by the fountain of life is a cause of death, so continually overflowing from that same fountain is a condition of living without end. Through the Lord.

## NINETEENTH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord, who conquered the devil and the world, restored humanity to paradise, and opened the gates of life to believers. Through Christ.

## TWENTIETH SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. And humbly to implore your majesty, that Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, may protect and preserve us by his grace. Since without him we can accomplish nothing rightly, may we receive by his gift what enables us always to please you. Through whom …

## TWENTY-FIRST SUNDAY

(G.) Eternal God. And humbly to beseech you to furnish us with your everlasting goods in such a way that you may also deign to console us with temporal ones. Support us with present things in such a way that you may lead us to joys which endure. Through Christ.

## TWENTY-SECOND SUNDAY

Eternal God. You rightly punish those who wander and mercifully restore those who have been chastised, so that you may draw us away from evil works and turn us toward doing good; for you do not wish to find something to condemn, but rather something to crown. Although according to our merits we deserve continually to be afflicted for our sins, you nevertheless temper judgment for correction and do not exercise perpetual punishment. Justly merciful in both respects, you order us by this law: by restraining us, you do not allow us to perish forever, and by sparing us, you grant time for correction. For this reason you scourge us with present evils, so that you may lead us to future goods. For this reason you console us with temporal goods, so that you may make us more certain of eternal ones, so that we may always praise you with devout confession both in prosperity and in adversity. Through Christ. Through whom …

## TWENTY-THIRD SUNDAY

Eternal God. And humbly to implore your clemency, so that your Son Jesus Christ, our Lord, who promised to be with his faithful until the end of the world, may not abandon, through the mysteries of his bodily presence, those whom he redeemed, nor leave them without the benefits of his majesty. Through whom …

## TWENTY-FOURTH SUNDAY

(Manuscript.) Through Christ our Lord. Through whom the holy and blessed name of your majesty is everywhere revered, adored, proclaimed, and worshiped. He is the source of salvation, the way of virtue, and the appeasement of your majesty.

## TWENTY-FIFTH SUNDAY

(Manuscript.) Eternal God. It is your work that we have been created, your gift that we live, and your goodness that we recognize your gifts toward us. Although our nature has been corrupted by the wound of sin, nevertheless, by your indescribable gift, it is raised from earthly things to heavenly ones.

## TWENTY-SIXTH SUNDAY

(Manuscript.) Eternal God. And to bring you the praises owed to you with devout honor, and to celebrate the indescribable proclamations of your wonders with the veneration of a devoted mind; and to praise, bless, and adore you, the ineffable and invisible God.

## FIFTH SUNDAY BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

(G.) Eternal God. Humbly beseeching your majesty, so that, once the unleavened bread of the old order has been cast out, we may be satisfied with the food and drink of that lamb who both restored our image and promised us his grace, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through whom …

### Another

(Manuscript.) Through Christ our Lord. We ask that you make us celebrate the mystery of his first coming with worthy praises and observances, and lead the present life blamelessly, so that we may be able fearlessly to await the second coming.

## FOURTH SUNDAY BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

(Manuscript.) Eternal God. It is proper and singular to you that you are good and that you are never changed by any alteration. We ask you to be favorable to our supplications and to show your mercy, which your Church implores. Manifest to your people both the mystery of the Incarnation and the marvelous sacrament of the coming, so that it may be evident among all nations that what was formerly promised through the oracles of the prophets has been brought to perfection; and may those whom the confession of truth adorns receive the dignity of adoption.

## THIRD SUNDAY BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

(Manuscript.) Eternal God. By your indescribable gift you granted that human nature, created in your likeness but made unlike you through sin and death, should not perish in eternal condemnation; rather, from the very source from which it had contracted sin and death, the immensity of your goodness should restore life, and a new and undefiled virgin, Mary, should atone for the crime of the ancient virgin. Greeted by the angel and overshadowed by the Holy Spirit, she was worthy to give birth to him who by his will permitted all things to be born. She marveled at the integrity of her body and the fruitfulness of her conception, and rejoiced that she would give birth to her own parent, Jesus Christ our Lord.

## SECOND SUNDAY BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

(Manuscript.) Through Christ our Lord. By his incarnation the world was saved, and by his passion the redemption of created humanity was accomplished. May he lead us to the eternal reward, who redeemed us from the darkness of the underworld; and may he justify at his second coming those whom he redeemed at his first, so that his exaltation may defend us from every evil, whose humility raised us to life.

## DECEMBER EMBER WEDNESDAY

(Manuscript.) Through Christ our Lord. Gabriel the archangel announced that he would be born for the salvation of humanity; the virgin Mary conceived him through the cooperation of the Holy Spirit; so that virginal purity might believe what angelic majesty announced, and ineffable divinity might accomplish it. Therefore, with your help, we desire to behold without shame the face of the one whose incarnation we rejoice to celebrate, so that, purified by fasts and cleansed from every vice, we may deserve to take part in the solemn festivals of his birth.

## FRIDAY

Eternal God. You are the sanctifier and institutor of abstinence, whose end and number are none. We ask you to pour over us, during the days of our fasts, the spirit of saving grace, and preserve us by your protection from all the disturbances of this world, so that we who celebrate the coming of your Only-Begotten may feel his continual help.

## SATURDAY WITH TWELVE LESSONS

(G.) Eternal God. You not only forgive sins but also justify sinners themselves; you not only release the guilty from punishments but also bestow gifts and rewards. We humbly beseech your goodness: since through fasts and solemn vows we anticipate the birth of your Only-Begotten, may we by his gift both be free from the disturbances of the present life and receive eternal gifts.

## THE SUNDAY THAT IS VACANT, OR THE FIRST BEFORE THE NATIVITY OF THE LORD

Through Christ our Lord. John preceded him by being born, by preaching in the desert wilderness, by baptizing in the streams of the Jordan, and by descending to the underworld. May the solemnity of his venerable Nativity, soon to come, render us pleasing to you in such a way that it may lead us, with the fruit of good works, into the heavenly kingdoms; so that, by preparing the way of the Lord in our hearts and producing worthy fruits of repentance, we may obey the Savior’s commands through John’s preaching. Thus may we come through the son of the barren woman to the Son of the Virgin, and through John, a great man, to that same Lord of ours, God and man. Just as he came to us hidden in order to redeem us, so may he justify us when he comes openly to judge.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT FELIX

Eternal God. And not to be silent about the memorable confession of Saint Felix, who could be changed from the uprightness of his state neither by heretical perversities nor by the allurements of the world; rather, an assertor of truth amid both dangers, he did not abandon the firmness of his faith. Through Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MARCELLUS

Eternal God. You are glorified in the confession of your saints, and you not only honor the glorious merits of your martyrs with superior rewards, but also kindly grant those who carry out the sacred mysteries with fitting service to enter into the joy of their Lord. Through Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF THE HOLY MARTYRS FABIAN AND SEBASTIAN

Eternal God. Because the venerable blood of the blessed martyrs Fabian and Sebastian, poured out in confession of your name, simultaneously manifests your wonders—you who perfect power in weakness, grant progress to our efforts, and provide the weak with help before you. Through Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT AGNES

(A.) Eternal God. And to solemnly celebrate the day consecrated to the martyrdom of blessed Agnes, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT VINCENT, MARTYR

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. For whose name the glorious deacon Vincent, an unconquered soldier, fearlessly approached the madness of the raging enemy, endured it with moderation, and mocked it with confidence: knowing that he was prepared to resist, but not knowing himself to be elated in order to conquer. In both respects he followed the footsteps of his master and Lord, who showed his servants examples to follow both in guarding humility and in triumphing over enemies. Through whom …

## ON THE FEAST OF THE CONVERSION OF SAINT PAUL THE APOSTLE

Eternal God. And humbly to beseech your majesty that you not allow the Church, instructed by the preaching of your blessed apostle Paul, to be violated by any deception. Since nothing in true religion is recognized to remain which his teaching did not season, may the faithful, through his intercession, be granted the power to carry out what he taught; and may the multitude of believing nations recognize that he is their intercessor with you whom they know to be their master and teacher. Through Christ.

## ON THE OCTAVE OF SAINT AGNES

Eternal God. Doubling the birthday celebration of blessed Agnes—for truly worthy of honor is the day of her who came forth here through earthly generation in order to attain fellowship with divinity. Through Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT AGATHA

Eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. For whose name you have granted to the faithful of every age and of both sexes contempt for punishments and death, so that among the palms of the blessed martyrs you might also crown the most blessed virgin Agatha with victorious endurance. Neither terrified by threats nor overcome by torments, she triumphed over the savagery of the devil because she remained steadfast in confession of your divinity. And therefore …

## ON THE FEAST OF THE CHAIR OF SAINT PETER THE APOSTLE

Eternal God. And to praise you as the wondrous God in your saints, in whom you have been greatly glorified, through whom you adorn the sacred body of your Only-Begotten, and in whom you establish the foundations of your Church—which you founded in the patriarchs, prepared in the prophets, and established in the apostles. From among them you made blessed Peter, chief of the apostles, because of his confession of that same Only-Begotten Son, confirmed by the mouth of that same Word of yours, having changed his name, the guardian and keeper of the heavenly gates in the foundation of your house, granting him by divine right that what he established on earth should be preserved in heaven. In his honor we offer these festivities to your majesty today and sacrifice an offering of thanksgiving and praise. Through the same Christ.

## ON THE FEAST OF SAINT MATTHIAS THE APOSTLE
Eternal God, and to praise you, wondrous God, in your blessed apostles, in whom you have been greatly glorified, through whom you gather the sacred body of your Only-Begotten Son, and in whom you establish the foundations of your Church. Therefore we beseech your clemency, most holy almighty God: that through the intercession of your blessed apostle Matthias, whose triumph of suffering we solemnly celebrate, we may deserve to be loosed from the bonds of our sins, restored to the blessedness of eternal life, and counted among the assemblies of your saints. Through the same Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0907] We have enclosed this preface and similar ones in brackets because they are more recent than the age of St. Gregory.]

[IN THE FEAST OF SAINT GREGORY, POPE.]

Eternal God, who gladden your confessor and bishop, blessed Gregory, in your kingdom, in everlasting blessedness without end, so that he may behold all things in your wondrous glory: where there is ineffable refreshment and indescribable joy; where is the presence of your Son, our Lord and Savior, upon whom the angels ever desire to gaze, while the dominions adore and tremble, etc.

[Col. 0907D] Another.

Eternal God, because you grant that your Church should rejoice in the commemoration of your bishop, Saint Gregory, so that you continually gladden her by his feast, train her by the example of his devout way of life, teach her by the word of his preaching, and protect her by a supplication pleasing to you.

[IN THE FEAST OF THE DEPOSITION OF SAINT BENEDICT.]

Eternal God, as we celebrate the honorable and glorious day of our Father Benedict, on which, leaving this sorrowful age, he migrated to the everlasting joys of the heavenly homeland. Filled with the gift of the Holy Spirit, he shone forth as a worthy Father for the beautiful flock of monks. Whatever he admonished in sacred words, he fulfilled in holy works, so that the path he had begun through divine oracles he might display through radiant examples. Thus the glorious multitude of monks, gazing upon their father’s footsteps, might deserve to attain the everlasting rewards of eternal light. Through Christ.

IN THE FEAST OF THE ANNUNCIATION OF SAINT MARY.

Eternal God, who granted your Church to celebrate the wondrous mystery and ineffable sacrament of the childbearing of the blessed Virgin Mary, in whom chastity remains untouched, modesty entire, and constancy firm. She rejoices that a virgin conceived, that she carried the Lord of heaven in chaste womb; that a virgin gave birth—a marvelous work of the divine dispensation—she who knew no man, yet is a mother; and after bearing the Son she remains a virgin. For, rejoicing in two gifts, she marvels that a virgin gave birth and is glad that she brought forth Jesus Christ, our Lord, the Redeemer of the world. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY TIBURTIUS, VALERIAN, AND MAXIMUS.

Eternal God, and to praise you at the feast of your holy martyrs, who are always worthy of praise in the commemoration of your saints; you grant the devotion of great faith, bestow endurance in suffering, and cause the schemes of the ancient enemy to be overcome, so that your outstanding martyrs may be hindered by no restraints of allurements from attaining the blessedness of heavenly rewards. And therefore.

[IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT GEORGE THE MARTYR.]

[Col. 0908C] Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. For the confession venerable because of his name, blessed George the martyr endured various torments; overcoming them, he earned the crown of everlasting life. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MARK THE EVANGELIST.

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord, whose grace chose blessed Mark for the priesthood, whose teaching instructed him for preaching, and whose power strengthened him for perseverance, so that through the priestly insignia he might also attain the palm of martyrdom. Teaching his subjects by preaching, instructing them by the example of his life, and strengthening them by suffering, he came to you to be crowned, having fearlessly overcome the threats of his persecutors. Through his intercession, we beseech you, cleanse us from our offenses, for he pleased you through so many prerogatives of gifts. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT VITALIS.

(G., MS.) And humbly to implore your majesty, that the result may always come to us not from our wickedness but from your forgiveness; may he always release us from harmful pleasures and mercifully rescue us from worldly disasters.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE APOSTLES PHILIP AND JAMES.

(G.) Eternal God, who established your Church upon apostolic firmness, and among whose company are blessed Philip and James, whose feasts we venerate today, asking that just as we are formed by their teachings, so we may be fortified by their examples and aided by their prayers. Through Christ our Lord.

IN THE FEAST OF THE FINDING OF THE HOLY CROSS.

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord, who by the passion of the cross redeemed the world and softened the most bitter taste of the ancient tree by the medicine of the cross; and who conquered by the trophy of the tree the death that had come through the forbidden tree. Thus, by the wondrous dispensation of his goodness, we who through the taste of the tree had departed from the flower-bearing seat may return through the wood of the cross to the joys of paradise. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY NEREUS, ACHILLEUS, AND PANCRATIUS.

Eternal God, because faith receives steadfastness from you, and weakness receives strength from you; and whatever is savage in persecutions, whatever is terrifying in death, you cause to be overcome through the confession of your name. Therefore we bless you, Lord, in your works, and praise you in the advancement of your saints Nereus, Achilleus, and Pancratius. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT URBAN, POPE AND MARTYR.

(G.) As we render the service of due devotion in the commemoration of your holy confessor and martyr Urban, Lord, we proclaim at his solemn feast your power, by whose grace he became such a man. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY MARCELLINUS AND PETER.

Eternal God, with whom the life of the saints is always glorious, whose precious death gladdens and protects us. Therefore, recalling the glorious birthdays of your martyrs Marcellinus and Peter, we offer you praises and humbly beseech your magnificence, that we whose martyrdoms we venerate may deserve to share in their blessedness. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY MARK AND MARCELLian.

Eternal God, who lead the devout contests of your holy martyrs Mark and Marcellian to abundant victory, and grant them everlasting triumph, so that they may always be an example to your Church. Grant us, we beseech you, through the intercession of those whose feasts we celebrate, to receive the gifts of your goodness. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY GERVASIUS AND PROTASIUS.

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. For the confession of whose name the blessed martyrs Gervasius and Protasius suffered, and in the heavenly realm they enjoy everlasting joys; and in solemn remembrance of them the Church rejoices with religious services. Through whom.

IN THE VIGIL OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST.

(A.) Eternal God, as we offer the solemn fast by which, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

IN THE NATIVITY OF THE FORERUNNER.

Eternal God, and on this day of the present feast, on which blessed John arose, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

Another.

Eternal God, that we may celebrate with joy this day of the Lord’s Forerunner and prophet, John the Baptist—for he is the one who announced repentance and foretold the way of salvation to the whole earth; he is the one whom the sacred trumpet of the Savior proclaimed, since no one has arisen among those born of women greater than John the Baptist. O how blessed the mother who deserved to receive such a son, promised from heaven! She recognizes the herald, born from the word, who preached the Savior to all. O how wondrous the twin virtues in the city where there are two mothers, a barren woman and a virgin! O how marvelous the mystery, where each is honored! One sent a herald from heaven, the other a judge. Elizabeth bore the Forerunner, and the Virgin Mary bore the glorious Redeemer.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY JOHN AND PAUL.

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. For love of whom the glorious martyrs John and Paul did not hesitate to undergo martyrdom; kinship joined them by the law of birth, unity of faith in the bosom of Mother Church, and fellowship in one love in enduring the bitterness of suffering. Through him we ask to be aided by the prayers of those whose feasts we are known to venerate. Through whom your majesty.

IN THE VIGIL OF THE APOSTLES PETER AND PAUL.

Eternal God, with whom the continuous feast and triumphs of the blessed apostles, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

IN THE PASSION OF THE APOSTLES PETER AND PAUL.

It is right and salutary. We humbly beseech you, Lord, that you, eternal Shepherd, not abandon your flock, but guard it continually through your blessed apostles Peter and Paul, so that it may be governed by those same leaders whom, as vicars of your work, you appointed to preside over it as shepherds. And therefore.

At the ordination of Saint Martin.

Eternal God, who enlightened the world toward recognition of the true faith through holy teachers, among whose company blessed Martin shone forth with particular excellence, gleamed more abundantly through the merits of his virtues, shone more brilliantly through the distinction of his signs, and appeared as a teacher of complete devotion to your people. He instructed some through words of heavenly teaching, strengthened others by examples of religious life, healed many from every affliction of illness, freed some from demonic spirits, and even restored to life through sacred prayers others who had been seized by death. Having become for all an odor of life unto salvation, he recalled all to the glory of eternal blessedness. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY SEVEN BROTHERS.

(G.) As we humbly beseech that we may be given this: just as your saints conquered the world through your power, so may they ask that we be freed from worldly errors. Through Christ.

IN THE TRANSLATION OF SAINT BENEDICT.

Eternal God, and to implore your glory with poured-out prayers, that we who venerate the feasts of your blessed confessor Benedict may, through your working, be able to imitate the examples of his holiness; and although we can in no way equal him in merits, may we deserve to be aided by his prayers. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT JAMES.

[Col. 0911A]

Eternal God, although the celebration of the divine sacrament always works salvation for us, nevertheless we trust more confidently that it will profit us if we are aided by the intercessions of your blessed apostle James. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY ABDON AND SENNES.

Eternal God, and to praise you, wondrous in your saints, whom before the foundation of the world you prepared for eternal glory with you, so that through them you might show this world the light of your truth. You armed them so thoroughly with the spirit of truth that they overcame the strength of death through the weakness of the flesh. Among their company are your martyrs Abdon and Sennes, who flourished in the meadow of your Church like roses and lilies. The blood of your Only-Begotten Son poured over them in the rose-red hue of confession [read: perfudit, “drenched”], and, as the reward of their suffering, clothed them in the snowy splendor of lilies. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY MACCABEES.

Eternal God, although you are wondrous in the protection of all your saints, in these we nevertheless recognize a special gift of yours: you made them brothers by the lot of birth and kin by their magnificent suffering, so that there might be at once the venerable glory of their mother and the most flourishing offspring of the Church. And therefore.

IN THE FINDING OF SAINT STEPHEN AND HIS COMPANIONS.

(MS.) Eternal God, as we humbly beseech that we may be given this: just as your saints Stephen, Nicodemus, Gamaliel, and Abibon conquered the world through your power, so may they ask that we be freed from worldly errors; so that we who venerate their most sacred discovery and merits may deserve to share in blessedness.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT SIXTUS THE MARTYR.

Eternal God, and especially on this day of the present feast, on which blessed Sixtus, priest and martyr alike, joyfully poured out devoted blood to you. To earn that same glory, he urged on the sons of his teaching; and those whom he instructed by exhortation, he preceded by example. Through Christ.

IN THE VIGIL OF SAINT LAWRENCE.

(G.) Eternal God, and in devout minds to anticipate the birthday of your martyr Lawrence, who, venerable as both deacon and martyr, shone gloriously both through the proper office of his ministry and through the martyrdom of his memorable passion. Through Christ.

ON THE DAY OF THE SAME SAINT.

(G.) Eternal God, and especially on this day of the present solemnity, on which blessed Lawrence was offered to you as a holy and living sacrifice pleasing to you. Kindled by the fire of your love, he steadfastly endured the fire of suffering. Through the enormity of his torments he reached the fellowship of the heavenly citizens. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT TIBURTIUS.

(G.) Eternal God, as we venerate the glorious merits of blessed Tiburtius the martyr, we beseech you to let the help of your propitiation be present to us, for we believe that through the intercession of those who pleased you we may obtain forgiveness for our sins. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT HIPPOLYTUS.

Eternal God, and to implore your clemency with suppliant vows, that the intercession of blessed Hippolytus and his companions may obtain forgiveness for our sins; through the torments of his passion he reached eternal glory. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT EUSEBIUS.

Eternal God, and to implore your clemency with bowed minds, that through the intercession of blessed Eusebius your confessor you may strengthen saving devotion in our minds, and grant that, just as we believe you alone to be the author and venerate you as Savior, so through his intercession we may have you as our helper forever. Through Christ.

IN THE VIGIL OF THE ASSUMPTION OF THE BLESSED VIRGIN MARY.

Eternal God, and on this day of the present feast, as we recall the solemn day of the Assumption of blessed Mary, we anticipate it with due service. The more humbly it is celebrated by our devotion, the more greatly its venerable feast will profit us through her intercession. Through Christ.

ON THE DAY OF THE ASSUMPTION OF THE BLESSED MARY.

Eternal God, and with rejoicing hearts to venerate you in the sacred virgins, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

IN THE OCTAVE OF SAINT LAWRENCE.

Eternal God, as we repeat the birthday feast of blessed Lawrence, whom the fire imposed upon his faith and confession did not deprive of them but kindled him so that he might shine more brightly. For just as gold is not consumed by flames but tested, so the blessed martyr is not consumed by the fires of torments but prepared for heavenly ornaments. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MAGNUS THE MARTYR.

Eternal God, rescuing the human race from the depths of death, you released our captivity through the passion of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord. Through him the power of the ancient enemy was so shattered that he even made your blessed martyr Magnus, whom that enemy had overcome, a victor. As we celebrate his triumph on the day when he shed his blood, we rejoice in your glory. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT TIMOTHY THE MARTYR.

[Col. 0912D]

(G. MS.) For the solemn feast is held for you; the sacred day is celebrated for you. The blood of your martyr Timothy, poured out in testimony to your truth, marked it with the magnificent honor of your name.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT BARTHOLOMEW.

(G.) Eternal God, who never abandon your Church in everlasting goodness, but continually instruct and endlessly guard her through your apostles. Through Christ our Lord.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT AUGUSTINE, BISHOP.

Eternal God, who filled blessed Augustine your confessor both with the evidences of knowledge and with the adornments of virtues, and enriched him. You imbued him with such varied forms of devotion that he himself was for you both ark and sacrifice, both priest and temple. Through Christ.

ON THE SAME DAY: SAINT HERMES.

Eternal God, since we confidently offer you sacrifices of praise, which we ask may be acceptable to you through the prayers of Saint Hermes your martyr. Through Christ.

IN THE BEHEADING OF SAINT JOHN THE BAPTIST.

Eternal God, who enriched the Forerunner of your Son with so great a gift that he was punished by beheading for proclaiming the truth. He who had baptized Christ with water, baptized by him in the Spirit, was dipped in blood for the same one. For the herald of the truth, which is Christ, was thrust into the darkness of prison for prohibiting Herod from his brother’s marriage-bed, where he enjoyed the light of your divinity alone. Then he underwent the capital sentence and descended to the lower regions to go before the Lord who was to come. He who had pointed him out in the world by his finger preceded him into the underworld by his precious death. And therefore.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT PRISCUS THE MARTYR.

(G.) Eternal God, who grant that your Church should advance through the commemoration of the saints, so that you continually gladden her by their feast, train her by the example of their devout way of life, and protect her by a supplication pleasing to you. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MARY.

It is right and salutary. That we should give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, for the advancement of all your saints. And especially, because of the merits of blessed Mary, Mother of God and perpetual virgin, fully to praise, bless, and proclaim your omnipotence with gratitude. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT GORGONIUS THE MARTYR.

(G.) And to praise you in the confessions of your saints, who became victors through your power. For when would human frailty be sufficient either to endure suffering with equanimity or to overcome the wickedness of the aerial enemy, unless you supplied the support of your strength and shattered the savage weapons of the raging enemy? Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY CORNELIUS AND CYPRIAN.

Eternal God, and to proclaim your power in your saints Cornelius and Cyprian [Note: [Col. 0913D] “Solemnity,” or something similar, is missing], whom, feeding flocks in different parts of the earth with sacred divine bread, you crowned with one faith, on the same day, and with an equal confession of your name. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT EUPHEMIA THE VIRGIN.

(G.) Eternal God, and in this solemnity to offer you sacrifices of praise, in which we recall with veneration the passion of blessed Euphemia your martyr and magnify the glory of your name with due proclamations. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MATTHEW, APOSTLE AND EVANGELIST.

(A.) Eternal God, who cause your Church, everywhere powerful in your faithful, to consist in the teachings of the apostles, grant, we beseech you, that through those by whom she received the beginning of divine knowledge, she may receive from them the increase of the heavenly kingdom until the end of the age. Through Christ.

[IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MAURICE AND HIS COMPANIONS.]

It is right and salutary that we should always and everywhere give you thanks and sing praises, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God. Through Christ our Lord. For we recognize how glorious in your sight is the life of the saints, whose precious death also gladdens and protects us. Therefore, recalling the glorious birthdays of your martyrs Maurice, Exuperius, Candidus, Victor, Innocent, and Vitalis, and of their companions, we offer you praises, saying with humble confession: Holy, etc.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY COSMAS AND DAMIAN.

Eternal God, and humbly to beseech your clemency, that you may join our joys to those of the rejoicing saints in the dwellings of the heavenly kingdom. And those whom we cannot follow in imitation of virtue, may we reach through the effect of due veneration. Through Christ.

[IN THE DEDICATION OF SAINT MICHAEL THE ARCHANGEL.]

Eternal God, as we proclaim the merits of Saint Michael the archangel. Although every angelic sublimity is worthy of veneration for us, since it stands in the presence of your majesty, that rank is nevertheless to be honored more earnestly which, in the dignity of its order, deserved the leadership of the heavenly army. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT JEROME.

[Col. 0914C] Eternal God, and especially on this day, which you adorned with the feast of blessed Jerome, to make the benefits of your gift resound. You willed to satisfy him with the streams of every kind of knowledge, so that through the splendor of his words he might become a raiser of many souls. Therefore, most holy God, we humbly beseech your goodness: fill us with his teachings, fortify us with his merits, and adorn us with his examples, so that, every blindness of ignorance having been driven away, and here strengthened by his prayers, we may deserve to fulfill your commandments and afterward attain everlasting joys. Through Christ.

[IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE HOLY DIONYSIUS, RUSTICUS, AND ELEUTHERIUS.]

Eternal God, who lead the devout contests of your holy martyrs to abundant victory and grant them everlasting triumph, so that they may always be an example to your Church. Grant us, we beseech you, through the intercession of those whose feasts we celebrate, to receive the gifts of your goodness. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT LUKE.

(A.) Eternal God, and to praise you in the merits of your saints, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

IN THE VIGIL OF THE APOSTLES SIMON AND JUDE.

Eternal God, because you are wondrous in all your saints, whom you made illustrious through confession of your name and glorious through the suffering undertaken for you. Therefore, just as they contended by fasting and working so that they might obtain this victory, so may we be formed by their examples, so that we may be found fit to celebrate the present feasts and, through their intercession, judged worthy to receive the eternal ones. Through Christ.

ON THE DAY OF THE HOLY APOSTLES SIMON AND JUDE.

(A.) As we glorify you in the honor of your apostles, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

[Note: [Col. 0915D] This preface also, and the following one, are more recent, as are all those enclosed in brackets.]

IN THE VIGIL OF ALL SAINTS.

Eternal God, as we rejoice in the fast dedicated to your reverence, since with devout services we anticipate the venerable solemnities of all the saints, so that we may be prepared to celebrate them solemnly. Through Christ.

ON THE DAY OF ALL SAINTS.

[Col. 0915B] Eternal God, as we humbly beseech your clemency, that you may join our joys to those of your rejoicing saints in the dwellings of the heavenly kingdom; and those whom we cannot follow in imitation of virtue, may we reach through the effect of due veneration. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF THE FOUR CROWNED MARTYRS.

(C.) As we celebrate the birthdays of the holy Crowned Martyrs, because whenever through them we commemorate the glory of your name, we grow in the increase of our faith. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT MARTIN.

Eternal God, by whose gift blessed Martin, confessor and priest alike, grew in the increase of good works, abounded in varied gifts of virtues, and shone with miracles. What he taught in words, he fulfilled by the presentation of his works; and by teaching and example alike he provided his subjects with guidance toward the heavenly kingdoms. Therefore we ask your clemency: may we be formed for good action by the examples of him who pleased you, fortified by his merits, aided by his intercessions, so that, with him intervening and you assisting, we may deserve to reach the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT CECILIA.

Eternal God, who perfect strength in weakness and conquer the enemy of the human race not only through men but also through women. By your gift blessed Cecilia was strengthened both in her purpose of virginity and in the confession of faith, so that she was neither diverted from her intention by the instability of age, nor softened by carnal blandishments, nor frightened by the frailty of her sex, nor conquered by the savagery of torments; but, preserving the integrity of body and mind, she deserved to attain eternal blessedness with the crown of virginity and martyrdom. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT CLEMENT.

Eternal God, and on this more glorious day, which the passion of blessed Clement consecrated and presented as venerable to us: he, imbued with apostolic preaching, educated in heavenly teachings, distinguished by the dignity of succession, shone forth both as an eminent martyr and as an outstanding priest.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT CHRYSOGONUS THE MARTYR.

[Col. 0916A]

(G.) Eternal God, who console us through the continual passions of the martyrs, and cause their triumphant blood, which they offered to be poured out before unbelievers for confession of your name, to pass over for the aid of your faithful.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT CATHERINE.

(MS.) [Note: [Col. 0916D] She is also attributed by some to Saint Ambrose.] Through Christ our Lord. Through him the most noble and outstanding virgin martyr Catherine, triumphant, instructed in the teachings of the prophets, apostles, and philosophers, and educated in every language by the gift of the Holy Spirit, overcame the emperor with his rhetoricians and the world with all its vices by wondrous wisdom. She converted the empress Augusta, together with the aforesaid rhetoricians, and Porphyry with all his companions, to Christ through her examples and magnificent teachings; and, having received faith with its sign, she sent them all, crowned by the martyrdom of Christ, ahead to the kingdoms of heaven. This was that wisdom, illumined, which conquered wickedness; it reaches mightily from end to end and orders all things sweetly. This is that most glorious woman who, offering herself with a hundredfold fruit and purpled by great martyrdom, presented herself to Jesus Christ. Therefore, strengthened by hunger for Christ and by the visitation of angels, she overcame with wondrous constancy nails, exceedingly sharp wheels, the tyrant’s sword, and threats. Even after being beheaded for Christ’s name, she shed milk instead of blood, so that her teaching and passion might be, for us who venerate her with pure mind, spiritual drink and food, and the remission of sins.

IN THE VIGIL OF SAINT ANDREW.

[Col. 0916C]

Eternal God, and humbly to implore your majesty, that we who anticipate the feast of blessed Andrew the apostle with solemn fasts and devout services may be aided by his merits before your majesty and instructed by his examples. Through Christ.

On the day of the same saint.

(A.) Eternal God, since the day of the magnificent votive feast has come to us, etc., as above among the Ambrosian prefaces.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT LUCY.

(MS.) Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Blessed Lucy, both virgin and martyr, feared him by loving and loved him by fearing; she was joined by dying to him to whom she had consecrated herself by living chastely. And for his sake she willingly endured temporal punishment, so that she might receive everlasting glory from him. As she wished to take up a double palm in the contest of the sacred struggle—both for the integrity of her body and for the purity of her faith—she chose more gloriously to endure the ancient enemy’s prolonged temptations than to lose the present life quickly through torments. For in martyrdom things are proposed that cause fear, while in the delights of the flesh there are things that soothe. The hidden enemy is endured with greater difficulty than the hostile one is overcome. Since, therefore, in both cases what conquered comes from your gift—for human weakness is powerless unless your goodness assists it—we beseech you: may she who received from you the power to conquer implore your goodness for us. And may she who deserved to enter the bridal chamber of your Only-Begotten, through her intercession, grant us aid amid the adversities of this world. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF SAINT THOMAS THE APOSTLE.

(A.) Eternal God, who granted your Church to stand upon apostolic foundations, and, as we celebrate the solemn feast of blessed Thomas, one of their company, we do not remain silent about your praises, Lord. And therefore.

IN THE VIGIL OF ONE MARTYR.

Eternal God, and to anticipate with veneration the devout contests of the glorious martyr N. His honorable solemnity, returning each year, is both perpetual and ever new, because the precious death of your righteous ones remains in the sight of your majesty, and the increases of joy are renewed when the beginnings of eternal blessedness are recalled. Through Christ.

COMMON PREFACES.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF ONE MARTYR.

Eternal God, and in the present feast of your holy martyr N. to offer you sacrifices of praise by confessing you, and to implore your immeasurable goodness: just as you gave him the palm of heavenly triumph, so, with him interceding, grant us cleansing and forgiveness of sin, so that we may rejoice in you through mercy, in whom he rejoices in glory. Through.

Another for the same.

(A.) Eternal God, and to praise you in the triumphs of all your martyrs, because through your gifts and offerings we venerate today the passion of your blessed martyr N., who for the confession of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, endured various torments and, overcoming them, earned the crown of everlasting life. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF MANY MARTYRS.

Eternal God, who lead the devout contests of your holy martyrs to abundant victory and grant them everlasting triumph, so that they may always be an example to your Church. Grant us, we beseech you, through the intercession of those whose feasts we celebrate, to receive the gifts of your goodness. Through Christ.

IN THE VIGIL OF ONE CONFESSOR.

(MS.) Eternal God, and humbly to implore your majesty, that we who anticipate with devout services the birthday feast of blessed N., your confessor and bishop, may be aided by his merits before your majesty and instructed by his examples.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF ONE CONFESSOR.

Eternal God, and especially on this day, which you consecrated by the sacred passing of blessed N., your confessor and bishop. We therefore beseech your clemency: grant us to follow that teaching which he taught both in word and fulfilled in deed, so that we may perceive ourselves aided before your mercy both by his examples and by his merits. Through Christ.

Another.

Eternal God, and to praise you through the virtue of your saints, to whom you granted the rewards of blessedness according to their merits; for they are always in your hand, and the torment of death will not touch those whom, under your protection, the bosom of blessedness shuts in. There they rejoice always in perpetual exultation; there also your blessed and supreme confessor N. rejoices in their fellowship. We therefore ask that he remember our miseries and obtain for us, from your mercy, a share in his blessedness. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF MANY CONFESSORS.

(G.) Eternal God, and to implore your majesty with suppliant devotion, that through the favor of your blessed confessors N., whose feasts we celebrate today, we may deserve to obtain your help. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF ONE VIRGIN MARTYR.

[Col. 0918B] Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Blessed virgin and martyr N. feared him by loving and loved him by fearing; she was joined by dying to him to whom she had consecrated herself by living chastely; and for his sake she willingly endured temporal punishment, so that she might receive everlasting glory from him. Through whom.

Another.

Eternal God, and as we recall the birthday of blessed N., to praise, proclaim, and bless you: you exalted her with so great a gift that you bestowed upon her both the crown of virginity and the palm of martyrdom; thus, she excelled in the strength of faith and the beauty of chastity, and entered the heavenly kingdom both a virgin and a martyr. Through Christ.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF ONE VIRGIN, NOT A MARTYR.

(G.) Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. For the ardor of love for whom this virgin and all holy virgins, receiving from blessed Mary the example of virginity, despised the pleasures and riches of the present age. By your gift it came about that, after the Virgin came forth from the Virgin, the fragile sex should be strong; and where there had been the capacity for sin, there should be the blessedness of conquering. And may the ancient enemy, who boasted that through the ancient virgin he had conquered the human race, now be conquered through holy virgins, followers of Mary rather than of Eve. May his confusion thereby increase all the more, since even the fragile sex now triumphs over him. Therefore we humbly beseech your immeasurable goodness: through the intercession of her whose feasts we celebrate—who conquered both her sex and the age, and pleased you both by the beauty of virginity and by the strength of suffering—may we deserve to overcome the invisible enemy and cling to your Only-Begotten Son, the Lord Jesus Christ. Through whom.

IN THE BIRTHDAY OF ONE VIRGIN, NOT A MARTYR.

(G.) Eternal God, and in this solemnity to offer you sacrifices of praise, in which we venerate the feast of blessed N., the virgin, and magnify the glory of your name with due proclamations. Through Christ.

[IN THE BIRTHDAY OF MANY MARTYRS.]

Eternal God, as we humbly beseech you to anticipate with due service the approaching birthday of your blessed martyrs N., may we feel that we have as patrons before your clemency those whom, through the generosity of your glory, we have deserved to receive as ministers of eternal salvation. Through Christ.

IN THE DEDICATION OF A CHURCH.

Eternal God, and for the annual dedication of this tabernacle to offer you honor and thanks, whose power is great and goodness abundant. Look down, we beseech you, from heaven, behold, and visit this house, so that if anyone supplicates your name in it, you may willingly hear and mercifully forgive those who make satisfaction. Through Christ our Lord. Here may your priests offer you the sacrifice of praise; here may the faithful people fulfill their vows; here may the burdens of sins be laid down; here may holy faith be established; here may you yourself distinguish between good and evil when the petitioner has stated the case, which you do not fail to know; here may complete devotion return; from here may corrected iniquity depart. May whoever, making satisfaction, flees here for refuge find with you, Lord, a place of forgiveness, and may the one overcome by conscious grief water your altars with streams of his tears. Here, whenever your people gather sorrowful and grieving, consent to be entreated, and, when entreated, grant pardon. Through whom.

IN THE CONSECRATION OF AN ALTAR.

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly beseech you to sanctify this altar, prepared for holy uses, with heavenly sanctification; so that, just as you wondrously and graciously received the offering of Melchizedek, the chief priest, so you may always deem acceptable the gift placed upon this new altar. Thus may the people who gather in this holy house of the Church, saved through these libations by heavenly sanctification, also attain the perpetual salvation of their souls. With the angels and archangels.

VARIOUS PREFACES.

[IN THE VENERATION OF THE HOLY TRINITY AND INDIVISIBLE UNITY.

Eternal God, whose divinity is one, whose power is eternal, whose nature is inseparable, and whose majesty is undivided; whom we confess to be one substantially and name threefold personally: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; who appear threefold in one and are acknowledged as one in three. Therefore, for the mystery of so great a revelation, in praise of your name we sing to you with the holy angels in devout devotion, saying with humble confession: Holy, etc.

## Of Holy Wisdom

[Col. 0919D]

Eternal God, who willed to reveal to us the knowledge of your name and the glory of your power in the Wisdom co-eternal with you, so that, confessing your majesty and clinging to your commandments, we might have eternal life with you. Through Christ.

## To Ask for the Grace of the Holy Spirit

Eternal God, who sees the secrets of our thoughts, and before whose providential gaze every intention of our mind lies open, look graciously upon the hidden chambers of our heart and purify our thoughts with the dew of the Holy Spirit, so that we may think and do what is worthy of your majesty. Through Christ.

## Of the Holy Cross

[Col. 0920A]

(G.) Eternal God, who established the salvation of the human race upon the wood of the cross, so that from the place whence death arose, life might rise again; and so that he who conquered by the wood might likewise be conquered by the wood. Through Christ.

## In Veneration of Holy Mary

(G.) Eternal God, and to praise, bless, and proclaim you with exultant hearts in the veneration of the holy virgins. Among them the undefiled virgin Mary, Mother of God, whose memory we devoutly celebrate, shone forth in glory. She conceived the Only-Begotten by the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit and, while the glory of her virginity remained, poured forth eternal light upon this world, Jesus Christ our Lord.

## To Ask for Angelic Intercession

[Col. 0920B]

Eternal God, while proclaiming the merits of the holy archangel Michael: although his dwelling, as a sublime angelic substance, is always in heaven, nevertheless the affection of your faithful presumes, out of reverence for your power, through these offices of pious devotion, to retain on earth a certain pledge of those ministers who continually stand in your presence. Through Christ.

## In Veneration of Saint Peter

Eternal God, we humbly beseech your majesty that, through the intercession of your holy apostle Peter, you may grant us to love you with our whole heart and to deserve to be participants with your saints in heavenly blessedness. Through Christ.

## On the Feast of Saint Stephen, Protomartyr

[Col. 0920C]

Eternal God, who gave blessed Stephen steadfastness in his passion and bestowed upon him, before all others after the passion of your Son, the grace of triumph: grant that, through the daily intercession of this same protomartyr of yours, we may be released from the bonds of our sins and attain the glory of eternal blessedness. Through Christ the Lord.

## In Commemoration of Saint Nicholas

It is right and salutary that we praise you, wondrous God, in your saints, in whom you have been greatly glorified. Among them you willed that Nicholas, of illustrious testimony and worthy to be celebrated for his proclamation of virtues, should preside over your Church by the merit of his confession as shepherd. You do not cease both to instruct it through the examples of his past virtues and to teach it through his present miracles. And therefore.

## In Veneration of All the Saints

[Col. 0920D]

Eternal God, we humbly entreat your glory with abundant prayers, that you may join our joys with those of your exultant saints in the dwellings of the heavenly kingdom, and that those whom we cannot follow by imitating their virtue we may reach through the effect of the veneration owed to them. Through Christ.

## At the Ordination of Priests

It is right and salutary. You who, overlooking the sins of human frailty, confer priestly dignity upon us unworthy ones: grant us, we ask, that you make us enter with minds pleasing to you in order to offer the sacred mysteries; for you alone, without fitting works, justify sinners; you, in your goodness, bestow grace upon the ungrateful. [Col. 0921A] You grant us to forget what lies behind and, by the most merciful direction, lead us toward the mysteries previously promised. And therefore.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, this offering of our hope, which we offer to you on the day of today’s solemnity, on which you have granted priestly vestments to us unworthy ones, we ask, Lord, that you graciously accept it and, in your mercy, preserve what you have accomplished in us.

## In the Priest’s Own Mass

Eternal God, who, overlooking the sins of human frailty, grant the dignity of the priesthood to the unworthy, and not only forgive sins but also deign to justify sinners themselves. It is your gift that [Col. 0921B] things not yet existing receive their beginnings, things begun receive nourishment, things nourished receive fruit, and things fruitful receive help to persevere. You created me when I did not exist; once created, you enriched me with steadfastness of faith; and, though faithful yet sullied by sins, you endowed me with priestly dignity. Therefore I humbly implore your omnipotence to cleanse me from past sins, strengthen me in good works during the course of this world, and confirm me in steadfast perseverance. Thus make me serve at your altars in such a way that I may be able to attain the fellowship of those priests who have pleased you. And through him may my vow be acceptable to you, who offered himself to you as a sacrifice, who is the maker of all things and the one spotless high priest, Jesus Christ our Lord. Through him.

### Another

[Col. 0921C]

Eternal God, through Christ our Lord. He who, for love of humankind, was made in the likeness of sinful flesh, the Lord assumed the form of a servant, and the physician walked in the appearance of one wounded. He is for us Lord and teacher of salvation, advocate and judge, sacrifice and priest. Through him I humbly beseech you, holy Lord, almighty Father: while I acknowledge the guilt of my conscience, by which I have become a transgressor of your commandments and through the crime of my offenses have fallen into ruin, raise me, Lord, whom the fall of sin has struck down; enlighten the heart that the gloomy darkness of sins has obscured; release the captive whom the chains of sins hold fast; grant this through that same holy, glorious, and adorable Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, whom angels, [Col. 0921D] thrones, and dominions praise. With whom, etc.

### Within the Canon

This offering, therefore, which I offer to you, Lord, for my excessive sins and offenses, I humbly ask your most merciful majesty with all my strength graciously to accept, entreating you to forgive the crimes that I wickedly committed through the frailty of the flesh and the temptation of evil spirits. Do not allow me thereafter to return to them, but strengthen me in your justifications, grant me perseverance in them, and make me worthy to stand before your presence and fittingly offer sacrifice to you, the Lord, with a chaste body and a pure heart. Through Christ.

## For a Community of Religious Monks

[Col. 0922A]

Eternal God, since we must pray to your clemency without ceasing, good Shepherd, do not abandon your flock, but guard it through the continual protection of the prayers of your confessor, blessed Benedict, so that, aided by his distinguished merits, we may follow without error the path pleasing to you—the obedience by which that Father advanced unharmed before us. Through Christ.

## In a Mass for a Friend

Eternal God, imploring the mercy of your majesty, we ask that you deign to grant your servant N. forgiveness of his sins; that, freed from all the bonds of the enemy, he may cling to your commandments with his whole heart; that he may always love you alone with all his strength and may deserve one day to attain the vision of your blessedness. Through [Col. 0922B] Christ.

### Within the Canon

This offering, therefore, which we offer to you for your servant N., that he may deserve to obtain complete forgiveness of his sins, we ask, Lord, that you graciously accept and, by the generosity of your compassion, grant that it may bring him forgiveness of offenses and correction of his deeds; so that he may live well here and happily reach eternal blessedness.

## For Relatives and Household Members

Eternal God, we earnestly beseech your clemency to make your male and female servants, whom you have joined to us by the intimacy of holy love, subject to you with their whole heart; so that, filled with the spirit of your charity, they may be cleansed of earthly desires and, by your gift, be made worthy of heavenly [Col. 0922C] blessedness. Through Christ.

### Within the Canon

May you, merciful and gracious, accept with a kind countenance this offering of your male and female servants, which we offer to you on account of their devotion of mind; protect them willingly as we beseech you, graciously hear them, and preserve them under eternal protection, so that, always rejoicing in your religion, they may persevere steadfastly in the confession of the holy Trinity and the Catholic faith.

### Another

Eternal God, whose omnipotence must be entreated, whose mercy must be implored, and whose loving-kindness must be embraced. We humbly beseech your majesty to grant your male and [Col. 0922D] female servants remission of sins, to direct their paths according to your will, and to rescue them from every evil, so that, delivered from all adversities and strengthened by your gifts, they may attain the desires of good things and, by your generosity, receive what they rightly ask. Through Christ.

## For Any Tribulation

Eternal God, who not only mercifully console our frailty with temporal gifts, so that you may advance us toward eternal things, but also, in your goodness, instruct us through the adversities of this age, so that you may lead us to the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ.

## For a Friend in Tribulation

Eternal God, who are the glory of the righteous and the mercy of sinners, we humbly beseech your loving-kindness [Col. 0923A]: through the intercession of blessed Mary, Mother of God, and of all your saints, look graciously upon your servant and grant him the protection of your mercy; rescue him from every tribulation and distress, so that he may serve you with his whole heart and his whole mind and always remain under your protection. Thus, when his final day comes, may he receive the fellowship of the saints and possess with them, without end, ineffable glory. Through Christ.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, this offering which we offer to you, Lord, for the liberation and consolation of your servant N., accept with a serene countenance, so that neither human fraud may overthrow him, nor your divinity punish him in judgment, nor justice, once he has been chastised, [Col. 0923B] crush him completely; let neither his own iniquity nor another’s adversity weigh him down. If he has sinned against you, forgive him; if he has offended * human beings, do you pardon him; remove from him the torments of mind and body together, so that, pierced with remorse, he may seek you and, touched by you, may diligently seek you out.
